entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: SAP confirms suspicious activity; GitHub, Project Granite and token theft reported; no customer-data access found
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

SAP: suspicious activity in its GitHub development platform (Project Granite), with reports that employee authentication tokens were stolen and source code copied or modified; SAP says it found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data and has not said whether any delivered software is affected

SAP told BleepingComputer and dpa that it identified suspicious activity, promptly took the necessary measures to protect its customers, and found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data on the investigation to date; it gave no vector, actor, discovery date or list of affected systems (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-27; tagesschau.de, 2026-11-27; Handelsblatt, 2026-11-27). A letter that dpa saw in part places the activity within SAP's platform for developer productivity and software delivery on GitHub and asks staff to check whether they must change credentials (translated from German) (tagesschau.de, 2026-11-27). Handelsblatt, citing company circles, says SAP detected the incident the week before and that software development was attacked (translated from German) (Handelsblatt, 2026-11-27).

Reported by media from internal sources and not confirmed by SAP: DER SPIEGEL's insider says the attacker stole authentication tokens of SAP employees and used them to copy and also modify SAP source code on GitHub, and that the attackers may have had help from AI systems; heise, relaying Handelsblatt, reports that SAP restricted access to GitHub, stopped automated processes in software development and replaced signing keys; BleepingComputer, Handelsblatt and heise add that, according to SPIEGEL, SAP tracks the incident internally as Project Granite, a name SAP has not confirmed (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-27; DER SPIEGEL, 2026-11-26; heise online, 2026-11-27; Handelsblatt, 2026-11-27). SecurityWeek notes that none of the reports indicate tampered code reached software delivered to SAP customers, and WirtschaftsWoche that SAP has left open whether customers must act (SecurityWeek, 2026-11-27; WirtschaftsWoche, 2026-11-27). SAP is part of the Swiss public sector's estate: the Federal Audit Office says the federal administration runs SAP R/3, supported until the end of 2027 and being replaced with S/4HANA, and Inside IT reports an existing S/4HANA landscape in the canton of Zurich's administration; no Swiss impact is reported (EFK, 2023-05-10; Inside IT, 2026-11-27).

Exposure
Organisations that consume SAP-delivered code, packages or updates, or verify SAP signatures; SAP has said nothing on which artifacts or keys are in scope, and no source says delivered software is affected (SecurityWeek, 2026-11-27).
Detection
The reported behaviour is use of stolen employee tokens against a source-control platform; for SAP customers the observable is on their side of the boundary, namely the provenance of SAP-delivered artifacts and any signing-key change in SAP's own communications.
Defender takeaway
SAP customers should watch SAP's own security communications for which artifacts or signing keys are in scope and verify any key change through SAP's channel; no customer action has been published, and SAP declined to say whether customers pulling SAP code from GitHub should act (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-27). For your own pipelines, 1Password disclosed on 2026-11-25 an intrusion through an employee's corporate GitHub account (1Password, 2026-11-25); review how employee tokens reach source control and CI.

Builds on: 1Password breach via an employee GitHub account exported customer records; vaults not affected

Sources: BleepingComputer · tagesschau.de (dpa) · DER SPIEGEL · Handelsblatt · heise online · SecurityWeek · WirtschaftsWoche · Swiss Federal Audit Office (EFK) · Inside IT · 1Password
entries.summary: SAP told dpa and BleepingComputer on 2026-11-26 and 2026-11-27 that it identified suspicious activity, took measures to protect customers and has found no evidence of unauthorized access to customer business data; a letter that dpa saw in part places the activity in SAP's GitHub developer platform. DER SPIEGEL's insider reports, without SAP's confirmation, stolen employee authentication tokens and copied and possibly modified source code, and heise, relaying Handelsblatt's company circles, reports restricted GitHub access, paused development workflows and replaced signing keys. SAP has not said how the attackers got in, who they are, or whether any software delivered to customers or any signing key customers verify is affected.

entries.action_label: Kudelski: assessed AI-driven insurer intrusion via…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Kudelski: assessed AI-driven insurer intrusion via onboarding and identity logic, no malware; alert on request bursts
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

Kudelski Security: a one-night intrusion at a European insurer, assessed as run by an offensive AI framework, abused customer onboarding, identity migration and a retired API to create accounts in customers' names and extract more than 100 documents, with no malware

Kudelski Security's incident-response team describes a one-night intrusion at an unnamed European insurer in which about three million identification requests arrived in under nine hours, about 30 legitimate customer identities were identified, more than a dozen customer accounts were created in those customers' names without their passwords, and more than 100 documents with sensitive customer data were extracted (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27). Kudelski found no malware and no compromise of the servers hosting the customer portal, and each forged account could read only its own customer's data (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27). It assesses with high confidence that an offensive AI framework was used, from correlated indicators of compromise, infrastructure characteristics, previously documented attack patterns, machine-speed execution, application-specific reconnaissance and automated handling of complex identity workflows, names no framework and could not establish how much human supervision there was (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27).

Among the weaknesses it lists, mostly business logic rather than software bugs: the API of a retired web interface remained accessible, identity information could be tested at scale, CAPTCHA was not enforced by the underlying API, rate limits were inactive after an infrastructure migration, alternative registration processes that did not consistently enforce prior identity checks, unverified contact information inherited a verified status, token validation was incomplete, authorization-related information was exposed to the client, and an identity-provider vulnerability weakened authenticator enrollment (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27). The identity-provider flaw is cited as GHSA-qqv8-37gw-ww2q, which is ZITADEL's advisory for a missing second-factor check on authenticator enrollment in its Login V2 interface, affecting 4.0.0 through 4.20.4 and fixed in 4.20.5; the post does not say the insurer ran ZITADEL (ZITADEL, 2026-11-18). Kudelski compares the case with BabidiGhost: that operation tried an AI agent against many organizations, this one explored a single organization's interconnected application and identity ecosystem in depth (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27).

Exposure
A customer or citizen portal that runs identity onboarding, identity migration or account recovery; the case came from an insurer, and the post names no public-sector victim.
Detection
Application and identity telemetry carried the evidence, not endpoint telemetry: Kudelski says abnormal application request volumes, extensive authentication failures and suspicious reconnaissance appeared well before data collection began and the attack still ran through the night (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27). Its recommended detections include distributed requests against one business function across rotating infrastructure, excessive one-time-code failures, authenticator enrollment without completed MFA, activity against retired APIs, source-map access by automated clients and abnormal onboarding and recovery sequences (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27). The sequence to alert on is a burst of identification requests, then accounts created in the names of existing customers without their original passwords, then sensitive information accessed by those accounts.

Triage: a newly created account may satisfy the portal's registration requirements, so a single account can look legitimate; Kudelski says abnormal request volumes, extensive authentication failures and reconnaissance activity were detectable well before data collection (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27).

Defender takeaway
For any portal with identity lifecycle workflows, Kudelski's hardening list is the checklist: user-supplied contact attributes must not inherit verified status, identity migrations must preserve existing account activation states, retiring a front end includes decommissioning its supporting APIs, and rate limiting, CAPTCHA and server-side validation must be tested again after each change (Kudelski Security, 2026-11-27); alert on identification-request bursts, and move a ZITADEL deployment on 4.0.0 through 4.20.4 to 4.20.5 (ZITADEL, 2026-11-18).

Builds on: BabidiGhost AI agent targeted 50+ organisations, mostly in Belgium, France, Switzerland; MFA…

Sources: Kudelski Security · ZITADEL security advisory (GHSA-qqv8-37gw-ww2q)
entries.summary: Kudelski Security's incident responders describe a one-night intrusion at an unnamed European insurer in which about three million identification requests in under nine hours identified about 30 customers, more than a dozen accounts were created in customers' names without their passwords and more than 100 documents were extracted, with no malware and no compromise of the portal's servers. Kudelski assesses with high confidence that an offensive AI framework was used, names none and publishes no indicators, and traces the chain to business-logic weaknesses: the API of a retired web interface that stayed accessible, CAPTCHA and rate limits that were not enforced or were inactive after a migration, registration paths that did not consistently enforce prior identity checks, unverified contact data that inherited verified status, incomplete token validation and an identity-provider flaw in authenticator enrollment.

entries.classification_html: NATOB3
entries.headline: Hunt.io: crew staged a Swiss tax office's AD database via ntdsutil IFM; fake JDBC driver loader; edge exploit kit
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB3

Hunt.io: exposed attacker directories show a crew staging a Swiss tax office's domain-controller database through ntdsutil install-from-media, a Java loader posing as the SQL Server JDBC driver and an exploit kit for edge services; the Swiss victim is unnamed, the access route is not shown and complete transfer is unconfirmed

Hunt.io recovered the contents of three exposed open directories and, reading the operators' own files, reports a domain-controller workflow against a Swiss tax office: a log records ntdsutil install-from-media creation, and a script copies the domain database and the registry hives from a controller share to a staging area, decodes them with a single-byte XOR and then requests removal of the install-from-media set (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25). Hunt.io says complete off-host transfer is not independently confirmed, that an NTLM-relay run against an internal LDAP service belongs to the same environment, and that the Swiss output begins after code execution was already available, so how the crew first got in is not shown (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25). The report names no canton, commune or federal body, and Hunt.io says it notified CISA before publishing (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25).

The same files hold a Java class registered as a java.sql.Driver service provider that poses as Microsoft's SQL Server JDBC driver: its boot routine runs when an application loads the JAR, with no scheduled task needed, and either polls an HTTPS endpoint on TCP 8443 for commands passed to cmd.exe or decodes a packed file into an Apollo-derived Windows executable written under the Java temp directory and started from Java (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25). Hunt.io also describes a Poseidon-derived Linux implant behind a server labelled Mythic, a commercial employee-monitoring product whose agents the operators drive with custom clients, and a reconnaissance stage that sends base64-encoded output in chunks inside GET request paths; it says the artifacts show a Poseidon-derived build, which does not establish that it ran on an external victim, and an Apollo derivation with no verified runtime command-and-control configuration (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25). Staged exploits cover edge and remote-access services, among them Citrix NetScaler (CVE-2025-5777), FreePBX (CVE-2025-57819) and PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), and Hunt.io states that their presence establishes availability, not successful operation against any named target (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25). Hunt.io reads the operation as a Chinese-speaking, Southeast Asia-based cybercrime crew running a Russian-authored toolkit and ties it to no named group and no state sponsor (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25).

Exposure
Active Directory domain controllers and Java application servers that load third-party JARs; Hunt.io's other victims are a US hospital system, a US manufacturer and a Bangladeshi university; law firms and US federal agencies are mainly reconnaissance targets, and one law firm was attacked without success (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25).
Detection
On domain controllers, ntdsutil install-from-media creation that no administrator requested, followed by reads of the database and the SYSTEM and SECURITY hive copies from the share by another host and a removal of the media; NTLM relay and coercion activity against domain controllers; on Java application servers, a JAR whose service-provider descriptor names a com.microsoft.sqlserver.jdbc class that matches no vendor build, java writing an executable under the temp directory and then starting a child process, and HTTPS polling from application servers to TCP 8443; in proxy logs, GET paths carrying long base64 chunks (Hunt.io, 2026-11-25).
Defender takeaway
Hunt domain controllers for install-from-media creation and share-staged copies of the directory database and hives, and enforce SMB signing and LDAP channel binding, which Hunt.io names as the hardening against the relay and coercion tooling; review Java servers for unexpected JDBC providers, and treat the Swiss victim claim as a single-source reading of recovered files until a Swiss body or the victim comments.
threat28 Nov 05:01Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Hunt.io
entries.summary: Hunt.io recovered three exposed attacker directories and reports a domain-controller workflow against "a Swiss tax office": a log of ntdsutil install-from-media creation and a script that copies the Active Directory database and registry hives from a controller share to staging, decodes them and requests removal of the media. Complete off-host transfer is not confirmed, the victim is unnamed and the report does not show how access was gained. The kit also holds a Java loader registered as a Microsoft SQL Server JDBC driver, Apollo- and Poseidon-derived implants, a commercial employee-monitoring product used as a command channel and staged exploits for edge services that Hunt.io says show availability, not success; it assesses a financially motivated, Chinese-speaking, Southeast Asia-based crew and names no group.

entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: RealVNC CVE-2026-137738: pre-auth UDP flaw can run code, as root on some platforms; update Server to 7.19.1
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-137738NATOA2

CVE-2026-137738, RealVNC Server 6.4.0 to 7.19.0 and the Viewer, Connect App and On-Demand Assist builds: a pre-authentication memory-safety flaw in UDP-based connections can give remote code execution, as root on certain platforms; fixed in Server 7.19.1, TCP-only direct connections are not exposed, no exploitation reported (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

RealVNC's advisory RVNC-2026-001 of 2026-11-20 fixes CVE-2026-137738, rated Critical with CVSS 3.1 9.8: a memory-safety flaw in UDP-based connections that could potentially be exploited before authentication to execute code remotely or crash the software, and that could give an attacker remote code execution as root on certain platforms (RealVNC, 2026-11-20; ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27). RealVNC says it affects all customers using its cloud-hosted connectivity and manually configured direct connections, offline-licensed and on-premises deployments included, and that TCP-only direct connections are not exposed (RealVNC, 2026-11-20). ENISA's entry appeared on 2026-11-27 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27), the day heise reported the flaw (heise online, 2026-11-27).

Affected are Server 6.4.0 to 7.19.0, Viewer 8.4.0 to 8.6.1, Classic Viewer 6.4.0 to 7.18.2, Connect App 8.6.1 and earlier, On-Demand Assist 3.4.1 and earlier, the iOS and iPadOS Viewer 3.7.0 to 4.9.5, the Android Viewer 3.5.0 to 4.9.5, iOS Server 2.8.1 and earlier and Android Server 2.8.3 and earlier; the fixed builds are Server 7.19.1, Viewer 8.6.2, Connect App 8.6.2, Classic Viewer 7.18.3, On-Demand Assist 3.5.0, the iOS and iPadOS and Android Viewers 4.9.6, iOS and iPadOS Server 2.8.2 and Android Server 2.8.4 (RealVNC, 2026-11-20). Updating is the only remedy RealVNC names, and for On-Demand Assist it tells administrators to advise end users to delete copies of older versions that they downloaded earlier (RealVNC, 2026-11-20). RealVNC says it is not aware of active exploitation in the wild, and heise repeats that no attacks are known (translated from German) (RealVNC, 2026-11-20; heise online, 2026-11-27).

Exposure
RealVNC Server, Viewer, Classic Viewer, Connect App or On-Demand Assist at the builds above that is reached through RealVNC's cloud connectivity or a manually configured direct connection; a server that accepts only TCP direct connections is not exposed (RealVNC, 2026-11-20). The advisory names no UDP port and does not say which platforms run the service as root.
Detection
Crashes or restarts of the RealVNC Server service and, on hosts where it runs as root, unexpected child processes of that service; both follow from the pre-authentication memory-corruption mechanism the vendor describes, which publishes no indicator; in network telemetry, unexpected inbound UDP to hosts that run the server is the pivot, since the flaw sits in UDP-based connections.
Defender takeaway
Inventory every RealVNC component, including On-Demand Assist copies that users downloaded, and update to the fixed builds, hosts reachable by direct connections or cloud connectivity first; RealVNC names no workaround, so the update is the control, and no exploitation is known.
vulnerability28 Nov 04:59Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: RealVNC (advisory RVNC-2026-001) · ENISA EUVD (EUVD-2026-137042) · heise online

entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: FreeRADIUS 3.2.11, 3.0.29: Critical unauthenticated use-after-free in default EAP-TTLS, TEAP bypasses; upgrade
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOA2

FreeRADIUS before 3.0.29 and 3.2.11: a Critical use-after-free in the default-enabled EAP-TTLS module can be started by an unauthenticated user and code execution may be possible; 21 issues fixed in all, among them TEAP bugs that return Access-Accept to an unauthenticated peer; no exploitation stated and no proof of concept for the Critical flaw

FreeRADIUS announced 3.0.29 and 3.2.11 on its security page of 2026-11-25 (GitHub release pages: 2026-11-26), fixing various overflows and memory leaks, and recommends that everyone on earlier versions upgrade (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25). The page lists 21 issues: one Critical, eight High, five Medium and seven Low (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25). The Critical issue is a use-after-free in the TTLS module, which the project says is enabled in the default configuration: an unauthenticated user could start an EAP-TTLS session and send invalid inner-tunnel data, and with heap shaping an attacker can cause a write of a heap pointer to a chosen address, so code execution may be possible (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25). The page states no exploitation and no proof of concept for this flaw, mentions a proof of concept that Ada Logics wrote for two High EAP-FAST issues, and says a system whose affected module is not enabled is not vulnerable to that module's issues (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25).

The High issues in DHCP, EAP-FAST, EAP-SIM and TEAP are in modules the project says are not enabled by default, among them an unauthenticated out-of-bounds write in the DHCP option encoder (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25). Three Medium TEAP issues let an unauthenticated peer that starts a TEAP session obtain an Access-Accept, through skipped Basic-Password checks, a Crypto-Binding check missing in production builds and an unexpected Crypto-Binding TLV; their fixes are listed on 3.2.x only, and TEAP is off by default (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25). CERT-FR restated the release on 2026-11-27, saying some of the flaws allow remote code execution, remote denial of service and a breach of data confidentiality (translated from French) (CERT-FR, 2026-11-27). The project page lists no CVE ids; ENISA's database lists CVE-2026-127030, an EAP-FAST session-ticket stack overflow, and CVE-2026-127029, an EAP-SIM identity-length stack overflow, both published on 2026-11-12 and scored CVSS 3.1 7.5 for availability impact only (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-12; ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-12).

Exposure
FreeRADIUS before 3.0.29 or 3.2.11 with the TTLS module enabled, as it is in the default configuration, for the Critical flaw; the project says EAP-TLS, TTLS and PEAP are enabled by default, and it states no default for the EAP-MSCHAPv2 module of a High issue, which a PEAP-only site should check; the issues in TEAP, EAP-FAST, EAP-SIM and DHCP apply only where those modules are enabled (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25). The project's standing advice on the same page, from its earlier 2026-06-01 announcement, is to keep the RADIUS server on a management VLAN and off the internet (FreeRADIUS, 2026-11-25).
Detection
Radiusd crashes and restarts, as service-manager events or core dumps, that follow EAP-TTLS handshakes, and on servers with TEAP enabled, Access-Accept replies for TEAP sessions with no completed inner authentication in the authentication detail log; both follow from the mechanisms the project describes, which publishes no indicator. A heap-corruption attack may leave only a crash, so review radiusd restarts in the days before the upgrade.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 3.2.11, or to 3.0.29 on a 3.0 server and then migrate, because the release notes call 3.0.29 the planned last 3.0 release and tell everyone to move to 3.2.11 or later (FreeRADIUS 3.0.29, 2026-11-26); check which EAP methods the server enables and switch off those in use by nobody, and keep the listener reachable only from network access servers and proxies. The Critical flaw sits in a method that is on by default, though no exploitation is stated.

Sources: FreeRADIUS project (security notifications) · CERT-FR (CERTFR-2026-AVI-1632) · FreeRADIUS 3.0.29 release notes · ENISA EUVD (CVE-2026-127030) · ENISA EUVD (CVE-2026-127029)
entries.summary: FreeRADIUS announced 3.0.29 and 3.2.11 on 2026-11-25; the project's page lists 21 fixed issues, one rated Critical: an unauthenticated use-after-free in the EAP-TTLS module, which is enabled in the default configuration and where code execution may be possible. Eight issues rated High sit mostly in modules the project says are off by default, and three Medium TEAP issues let an unauthenticated peer obtain an Access-Accept on 3.2.x; the project states no exploitation and no proof of concept for the Critical flaw. CERT-FR restated the release on 2026-11-27, and 3.0.29 is planned as the last 3.0 release.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Cacti 1.2.31 zero-day 4HTTP2ROOT: guest-session RCE, public PoC, no release; disable the guest user, restrict the UI
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

Cacti Core 1.2.31 (4HTTP2ROOT): an anonymous guest session reaches a stored SQL injection and command execution as the web or poller account in four requests, public proof of concept, no CVE id and no release; the chain needs the guest account enabled, which Cacti's documentation says is off by default

A researcher using the handle ek0ms savi0r published a write-up and proof of concept on 2026-11-26 for unauthenticated command execution on Cacti Core 1.2.31 in four HTTP requests that start from an anonymous guest session, a chain its repository calls 4HTTP2SHELL (ek0ms savi0r, 2026-11-26) and watchTowr named 4HTTP2ROOT (watchTowr, 2026-11-26). BleepingComputer relays the researcher's statement that the flaw was not reported to Cacti before release, and no fixed version exists: watchTowr says Cacti has not published one, and the project's releases page lists 1.2.31 as its newest release on 2026-11-28 (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-27; watchTowr, 2026-11-26; Cacti releases, 2026-11-28).

As RavenAI and The Hacker News describe the chain, the guest profile page stores a non-numeric graph page size; a graph-preview request concatenates it into a query that accepts a second statement, which rewrites a poller entry's command; and a realtime-graph request runs that command inside the web request as the web server and poller account, often a low-privileged web user according to watchTowr (RavenAI, 2026-11-26; The Hacker News, 2026-11-27; watchTowr, 2026-11-26). The guest account must be enabled for the chain to work, and Cacti's documentation says guest or anonymous access is disabled by default and works only when the Guest user is enabled and set as the guest user (watchTowr, 2026-11-26; Cacti documentation, 2026-11-28). Only 1.2.31 was tested, and it is unclear whether earlier versions are affected (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-27). Cacti stores SNMP strings and device logins, so a compromised server is a foothold into the monitored network (watchTowr, 2026-11-26).

watchTowr reports no exploitation as of 2026-11-27, while Previdian's honeypots recorded SQL-injection attempts from 2026-11-27 that it says do not show the target was vulnerable or that an attempt succeeded (watchTowr, 2026-11-26; Previdian, 2026-11-26; Previdian tracker, 2026-11-26). BSI classifies the issue as critical (BSI, 2026-11-26). On 2026-11-28 the project merged unreleased 1.2.x hardening commits that reject guest profile writes, validate the page size and require graph access before a realtime command, without referring to the disclosure and with no release or advisory yet (Cacti pull request 9014, 2026-11-28).

Exposure
Cacti Core 1.2.31 with the Guest user enabled and set as the anonymous user, reachable from wherever an attacker can load the web interface.
Detection
In web access logs, one client requesting the guest profile page, a profile update, a graph preview and a realtime graph in sequence; in the application log, a PHP warning about a non-numeric value in a graph display setting; in the Cacti database, a poller entry whose command is anything other than a normal poller command; on the host, new files written by the poller or web account, a shell or marker file among them (RavenAI, 2026-11-26; watchTowr, 2026-11-26). No release exists, so check guest-reachable servers for these artifacts and treat stored SNMP strings and device logins as exposed on a hit.

Triage: each request alone is ordinary guest behavior, so the stronger pivots are the non-numeric display-setting warning and a changed poller entry followed by a realtime-graph request (RavenAI, 2026-11-26).

Defender takeaway
Where the guest account is on, disable it and restrict the web interface to trusted internal networks now and review poller entries for unexpected commands; where it is off, the sources say the chain has no entry point, but watch for the first release with the hardening commits (watchTowr, 2026-11-26).
vulnerability28 Nov 04:55Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: ek0ms savi0r (Church of Malware) · watchTowr · RavenAI · The Hacker News · BleepingComputer · Previdian Research · Previdian (VULN-2026-0010) · BSI CERT-Bund (WID-SEC-2026-4845) · Cacti documentation (User Management, as read) · Cacti pull request 9014 · Cacti releases (as read)

Previdian's honeypots recorded SQL-injection attempts from 2026-11-27 with no confirmed success, and Cacti merged unreleased hardening commits on 2026-11-28 that cover each stage without referring to the disclosure. Cacti stores SNMP strings and device logins, so a compromised server is a pivot into the monitored network.

entries.headline: nginx2root: five unauthenticated flaws reach worker RCE, Rapid7 PoC public; update to 1.31.10, 1.30.8, Plus 37.3.1.1
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-123007 +10updatedNATOA1

NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated memory-corruption flaws (CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 in HTTP/2, CVE-2026-121810 in HTTP/3, CVE-2026-123634 in the resolver, CVE-2026-113425 in the mail proxy) can lead to code execution as the worker process; fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, Rapid7 proof of concept public, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

F5 and the nginx project published the nginx2root fixes (nginx.org, 2026-11-18); CERT-EU counts five vulnerabilities, all able to lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the NGINX worker process (CERT-EU, 2026-11-18). CVE-2026-123007 is an HTTP/2 flow-control overflow: cancelling queued response data makes nginx use an invalid length when copying a later response (Rapid7, 2026-11-18), and Wiz demonstrated code execution on nginx serving ordinary static files (Wiz Research, 2026-11-18).

Rapid7 published a working proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007 against nginx 1.31.8; the exploit needs about 128 GB of HTTP/2 traffic and likely fails with concurrent clients (Rapid7, 2026-11-18; Rapid7 repository, 2026-11-18). CERT-EU reports no exploitation in the wild and NCSC.ch rates exploitation unknown with a proof of concept available (CERT-EU, 2026-11-18; NCSC.ch, 2026-11-18).

The memory-corruption fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 (nginx.org, 2026-11-18); nginx 1.31.10 and 1.30.8 of 2026-11-23 add a fix for CPU exhaustion when ssl_early_data is on (CVE-2026-132779, affecting 1.21.4 to 1.31.9 per nginx.org, 2026-11-27), as do NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 (nginx.org, 2026-11-23; nginx.org, 2026-11-23; F5 NGINX Plus release notes, 2026-11-23). CERT.at lists NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1 as fixing four of the five (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-113425); it also says 37.2.0.1 and 37.0.7.1 already carry the fix for CVE-2026-123633 but stay affected by CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-121810, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update (translated from German) (CERT.at, 2026-11-18).

Exposure
An nginx build from the first affected release of each flaw (1.9.5, 1.19.7, 0.6.18, 1.25.0 and 0.5.33) up to 1.31.8 whose configuration uses the feature: an HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 listener, the resolver with variable proxy_pass destinations plus mirror or SSI, or the mail proxy with auth_http (nginx.org, 2026-11-18; Xint, 2026-11-18). A distribution backport can fix a flaw without changing the version nginx -v reports (Xint, 2026-11-18). Veeam Software Appliance and Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 are affected by the two HTTP/2 flaws and cannot disable HTTP/2; Veeam ships the fix through Veeam Updater (Veeam, 2026-11-25). GitLab's Linux package and Docker images carry nginx 1.31.9 from 19.6.2, 19.5.9 and 19.4.11 (GitLab, 2026-11-25).
Detection
Process-creation or audit telemetry for any program started by the worker's user, since a normal nginx worker runs no external programs and that is the clearest sign of success; worker exits and core dumps in the error log mark attempts, not successes (Xint, 2026-11-18; CERT-EU, 2026-11-18).

Triage: a large upload is a legitimate cause of an inbound-heavy connection and workers crash for unrelated reasons, so a program started by the worker is the discriminator, not the traffic shape alone (Xint, 2026-11-18).

Defender takeaway
Update and restart nginx, because a configuration reload does not replace the running executable; disabling HTTP/2 on exposed listeners blocks only the two HTTP/2 flaws (Xint, 2026-11-18) and, if it stays on elsewhere, leaves connection pressure (Unit 42, 2026-11-24), and Xint gives interim measures for the others: a fixed upstream group in place of request-time DNS lookups for CVE-2026-123634, no QUIC listeners for CVE-2026-121810 and bound or firewalled mail listeners for CVE-2026-113425 (Xint, 2026-11-18). An empty execution-audit result after the update cannot rule out an earlier compromise, and Xint chained CVE-2026-123007 with a separate Linux kernel SCTP flaw, unpatched when it published, to reach root on the host and escape a Docker container; hosts that do not use SCTP can block the module from loading (Xint, 2026-11-18).
Update21 Nov 2026 04:37 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-intelsummaryaffected_productsentitiessourcesevidenceactionsbody

Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama (virtual and M-Series) as affected by CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007 only where the HTTP/2 option is enabled, and says it knows of no malicious exploitation; disabling HTTP/2 is its workaround (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-11-20). The fixed builds are PAN-OS 12.2.4-h3, 12.1.10-h6 and 11.2.16-h3; 12.1.7-h15, 11.2.10-h19 and 11.2.13-h6 carry an ETA of 2026-11-23, and 12.1.2 to 12.1.4 and 11.2.0 to 11.2.7 need no action (Palo Alto Networks PSIRT, 2026-11-20).

Cisco's interim advisory (version 1.0, 2026-11-20) lists NX-OS Software, Smart PHY (fix 27.1.0, March 2027), the Intersight Virtual Appliance (1.1.9-0, December 2026), Cloud Hosted Services Vulnerability Management (1.30.7, November 2026) and Identity Services Engine 3.5 (3.5 Patch 5, December 2026) as affected, lists Catalyst Center, the SD-WAN Controller and Manager, ASA, FMC, FTD and UCS Central as not affected, and has IOS XE, IOS XR and UCS Director under investigation; its PSIRT knows of proof-of-concept code and of no malicious use (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Siemens (SSA-935812, 2026-11-20) lists five Industrial Edge device products (Cloud Device, Device Kit for arm64 and x86-64, Own Device and Virtual Device) as affected in all versions with no fix available, lists Industrial Edge Hub and the Industrial Edge Management products as not affected, and names disabling HTTP/2 or HTTP/3 on the affected listeners as the mitigation (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-20). Fortinet says none of its products uses NGINX Plus and is still investigating FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator and dozens of others (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-11-20).

Update22 Nov 2026 04:34 UTCrun 2026-11-22T0355Z-intelsummaryaffected_productssourcesactionsbodyentities

Cisco's advisory is at version 1.1 (2026-11-21): UCS Director moves from under investigation to affected with the release still to be determined, Identity Services Engine is affected only on release 3.5 (3.5 Patch 5, December 2026), NX-OS Software is fixed in 10.7.2F (December 2026), and IOS XE and IOS XR remain under investigation; the affected-products table now also names Unified Contact Center Express and NextFusion Platform (release to be determined), Finesse (15.0 US3, date to be determined), License (Smart Software Manager) On-Prem (10-202701, February 2027), AI PODs for Collaboration (1.0.3, December 2026) and Webex Assistant for Meetings (1.15.16, November 2026), among others (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Fortinet's timeline records an update of its not-impacted list on 2026-11-21: FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiMail, FortiNAC and FortiPAM are not impacted, while 51 product names, among them FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM, remain under investigation; Fortinet lists ten nginx CVEs, five more than the five above (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Ubuntu lists the fixes in USN-9159-1 for releases 16.04 LTS to 26.10, those for 16.04, 18.04 and 20.04 being available with Ubuntu Pro (Ubuntu, 2026-11-19). Synology's SA-26:20 lists DSM 7.4, 7.3, 7.2.2, 7.2.1 and 7.1, DSM Enterprise, BeeStation OS and APM as affected by CVE-2026-123007, scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1, names DSM 7.4.1-90080-2 and 7.3.2-86009-6 as the fixed releases with the other branches ongoing, and gives turning HTTP/2 off under Control Panel, Network, Connectivity as the mitigation (Synology, 2026-11-19).

Correction22 Nov 2026 14:55 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditbodysourcing_note

Siemens' SSA-935812 does not list every Industrial Edge product: the affected ones are five device products, Industrial Edge Cloud Device, Device Kit for arm64 and x86-64, Own Device and Virtual Device, with no fix available, while Industrial Edge Hub and the Industrial Edge Management products are listed as not affected (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-20). Rapid7 states only that its exploit runs code with the nginx worker's permissions; it does not discuss root (Rapid7, 2026-11-18).

Improvement23 Nov 2026 04:35 UTCrun 2026-11-23T0355Z-intelcvesbody

nginx.org lists ten flaws fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7, five more than the five above, and Fortinet's FG-IR-26-279 lists the same ten (nginx.org, 2026-11-18; Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-11-20). The additional five are CVE-2026-118899, an infinite loop while reading a client request body over TLS 1.3 (1.13.0 to 1.31.8, rated major); CVE-2026-120967, an SNI bypass when using client certificate validation in the stream module (1.25.5 to 1.31.8, medium); CVE-2026-125283, a buffer overflow when using alias with try_files (0.9.6 to 1.31.8, minor); CVE-2026-123640, insufficient validation in the stream ssl_preread module (1.15.2 to 1.31.8, minor); and CVE-2026-120993, a NULL pointer dereference when using PROXY protocol version 2 that affects only the mainline 1.31.4 to 1.31.8 and is fixed in 1.31.9 alone (nginx.org, 2026-11-18). NCSC-NL scores them CVSS 4.0 8.7 (CVE-2026-118899), 6.3 (CVE-2026-120967) and 6.9 (CVE-2026-120993, CVE-2026-123640 and CVE-2026-125283) (NCSC-NL, 2026-11-18), and Fortinet rates CVE-2026-118899 high and the other four medium (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Updating to 1.31.9 or 1.30.7 covers all ten (nginx.org, 2026-11-18).

Update26 Nov 2026 05:07 UTCrun 2026-11-26T0356Z-intelsummaryactionssourcesbodyupdated_at

Unit 42 published a first-person account of reaching pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the non-root NGINX worker on a two-VM lab target running 1.31.8: the first attempt recovered a libc address without a shell and the second opened an interactive shell. The chain needed a non-default configuration and a separate memory disclosure that F5 assessed as limited to a non-typical configuration and has not given a CVE, whose details Unit 42 withholds (Unit 42, 2026-11-24). The tested path needs HTTP/2 on the listener and a reverse-proxy route whose upstream is a variable resolved at request time, with free worker connections at or below one sixteenth of worker_connections; static upstream routes still need review, and Unit 42 publishes no confirmed indicators of compromise. A log signal Unit 42 gives is the error-log warning that worker connections are not enough and are being reused, which needs the warn log level (Unit 42, 2026-11-24). Raising worker_connections adds only headroom and disabling HTTP/2 on some listeners leaves extra HTTP/1.1 connections, so neither replaces the upgrade; no source reports exploitation.

Palo Alto Networks removed the ETA for 12.1.7-h15, 11.2.10-h19 and 11.2.13-h6 on 2026-11-24 because those builds are released, so every fixed build named above is available, marked PAN-OS 11.1 and 10.2 as not impacted, and says the impacted products for CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-123634 and CVE-2026-113425 are the same as for the two HTTP/2 flaws; it knows of no malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-20). Cisco's advisory, at version 1.5 of 2026-11-26 then, had rated the flaws High rather than Critical since version 1.2 of 2026-11-23, lists IOS XE as not affected, gives NX-OS 10.3.11, 10.4.9, 10.5.7, 10.6.5 and 10.7.1 in place of 10.7.2F, lists Catalyst Center with bug IDs and fixes 3.3.3 and 3.4.1 (dates to be determined) where it was listed as not affected, and writes the Finesse fix as 15.0(1)SU3 with Unified Intelligence Center on the same release (Cisco, 2026-11-20). Fortinet's advisory then listed FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer as not impacted and still had FortiAuthenticator and dozens of other products under investigation (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Synology's SA-26:20, revised on 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-26, now lists fixed builds beyond DSM 7.4 and 7.3: 7.2.2-72806-11 for DSM 7.2.2, 7.2.1-69057-14 for DSM 7.2.1, 7.1.1-42962-10 for DSM 7.1 and 1.5.6-68000 for BeeStation OS 1.5, with only DSM Enterprise 1.0 still listed as ongoing (Synology, 2026-11-19).

Update27 Nov 2026 04:55 UTCrun 2026-11-27T0355Z-intelheadlinesummaryaffected_productsentitiescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyupdated_at

nginx 1.31.10 and 1.30.8, both dated 2026-11-23, carry one security fix: when ssl_early_data is configured a client might cause excessive CPU usage (CVE-2026-132779) (nginx.org, 2026-11-23; nginx.org, 2026-11-23). nginx.org lists it as affecting 1.21.4 to 1.31.9 (nginx.org, 2026-11-27), so 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 fix the memory-corruption flaws but not this one; NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 of the same day are security releases whose only fix is this flaw, and the 18 November Plus builds do not carry it (F5 NGINX Plus release notes, 2026-11-23). F5's own advisory and a score were not readable, and no source states whether R33 to R36 are affected.

Veeam's KB4976 lists Veeam Software Appliance 13.1 and Veeam Infrastructure Appliance 13.1 as affected by CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633, because their nginx has HTTP/2 enabled on a listener that proxies requests to a backend; the other three flaws do not apply (Veeam, 2026-11-25). A fix has been in the Veeam repository since 2026-11-25, Veeam Updater checks every 12 hours and installs mandatory updates automatically on the nearest Sunday at 14:00, and until it is installed Veeam says to restrict TCP 443 on the appliances to trusted networks, because HTTP/2 cannot be disabled on them (Veeam, 2026-11-25). GitLab's Linux package and Docker images carry nginx 1.31.9 from 19.6.2, 19.5.9 and 19.4.11, and its page does not say whether they set ssl_early_data (GitLab, 2026-11-25). KB4976 also lists the Veeam Plug-In for AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure appliances as affected (install all available security updates through Veeam Updater) and Veeam Backup for Salesforce 3.2.1, which is affected by the same two HTTP/2 flaws (install the operating system vendor's update or disable HTTP/2); Veeam manages its Data Cloud services and asks for no customer action (Veeam, 2026-11-25).

Update28 Nov 2026 04:51 UTCrun 2026-11-28T0355Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesummary

Cisco's advisory is at version 1.6 of 2026-11-27 (updated affected products), still rates the flaws High and knows of no malicious use; besides the products named above, its table lists Crosswork Hierarchical Controller (11.0.4 and 12.0.1, November 2026), Secure Endpoint Private Cloud Appliance (PC 4.2.10, December 2026) and Intersight (1.30.7 and 1.31.f, December 2026), with UCS Fabric Interconnect and Optical Network Controller still to be determined, among about two dozen products (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-11-20). NextFusion Platform, named in the 2026-11-22 section, does not appear in it (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-11-20).

Fortinet's FG-IR-26-279 now lists FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM as not impacted, as it does FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer, keeps 29 product names under investigation, FortiAuthenticator among them, and says it has remediated the issue in FortiVoice Cloud and FortiEdge Cloud, so customers need not act (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-11-20). Synology's SA-26:20 revisions of 2026-11-24 and 2026-11-25 updated the fix status for APM, for which versions 2.0, 1.2, 1.1 and 1.0 should upgrade to 2.0.2-88107 or above (Synology, 2026-11-19).

entries.summary: F5 and the nginx project fixed five memory-corruption flaws in the nginx data plane on 2026-11-18, two in HTTP/2 and one each in HTTP/3, the resolver and the mail proxy, which CERT-EU says can lead to unauthenticated code execution with the privileges of the worker process; NCSC-NL scores all five CVSS 4.0 9.2, NCSC.ch and Wiz the two HTTP/2 flaws and Rapid7 CVE-2026-123007. The memory-corruption fixes are in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, nginx 1.31.10, 1.30.8 and NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 add a fix for one CPU-exhaustion flaw, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 have no update. Rapid7 published a proof of concept for CVE-2026-123007, CERT-EU reports no exploitation, and NCSC.ch, CERT-EU, CERT.at and NCSC-NL issued warnings; Unit 42 reached pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the worker user in a lab, on a non-default configuration and with a separate memory leak that F5 has not given a CVE. Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled as affected, Veeam lists its 13.1 Software and Infrastructure Appliances (fixed through Veeam Updater), Cisco lists Catalyst Center, Identity Services Engine 3.5, Nexus 3000 and 9000 in standalone NX-OS mode, UCS Director and about 20 other products with fixes dated November 2026 to March 2027 or still to be determined, Siemens and Synology list products with fixes pending or none, and Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy, FortiMail, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM not impacted while 29 product names, FortiAuthenticator among them, remain under investigation.
entries.title: NGINX nginx2root: five unauthenticated memory-corruption flaws (CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633 in HTTP/2, CVE-2026-121810 in HTTP/3, CVE-2026-123634 in the resolver, CVE-2026-113425 in the mail proxy) can lead to code execution as the worker process; fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 and NGINX Plus 37.3.0.1 and 37.0.8.1, Rapid7 proof of concept public, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

updates.summary: Four vendors published product impact for the nginx flaws: Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS and Panorama with HTTP/2 enabled (three fixed builds out, three due 2026-11-23, HTTP/2 off as workaround), Cisco lists NX-OS and ISE 3.5 among affected products, Siemens Industrial Edge has no fix, and Fortinet is still investigating. None reports exploitation.

Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.1, moves UCS Director to affected and adds Unified Contact Center Express, Finesse and other products with fixes dated November 2026 to February 2027 or still to be determined; Synology lists DSM as affected with fixed builds for 7.4 and 7.3; Fortinet confirms FortiOS, FortiProxy and FortiMail not impacted while 51 product names stay under investigation; and Ubuntu publishes USN-9159-1.

Siemens lists five Industrial Edge device products as affected, with Industrial Edge Hub and the Management products not affected; Rapid7 says only that its exploit runs with the nginx worker's permissions.

nginx.org and Fortinet list ten flaws fixed in nginx 1.31.9 and 1.30.7, five more than the entry's five: a TLS 1.3 request-body infinite loop rated major, an SNI bypass of client certificate validation in the stream module, a stream ssl_preread validation flaw, an alias and try_files buffer overflow, and a PROXY protocol version 2 NULL dereference in the 1.31 mainline; the fixed releases and the update action are unchanged.

Unit 42 reached pre-authentication code execution through CVE-2026-123633 as the worker user in a two-VM lab, on a non-default configuration and chained with a memory leak F5 has not given a CVE, and publishes the exposure test and a log signal. Palo Alto Networks released its last three PAN-OS fixed builds and cleared 11.1 and 10.2, and Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.5, rates the flaws High and changes several product statuses and fixed releases.

nginx 1.31.10 and 1.30.8 (2026-11-23) and NGINX Plus 37.3.1.1 and 37.0.9.1 fix a further flaw, CPU exhaustion when ssl_early_data is on (CVE-2026-132779), so the update target moves; Veeam lists its 13.1 Software and Infrastructure Appliances as affected by the two HTTP/2 flaws with a fix through Veeam Updater since 2026-11-25, and GitLab's Linux package carries nginx 1.31.9.

Cisco's advisory, now at version 1.6 of 2026-11-27, also lists Crosswork Hierarchical Controller, Secure Endpoint Private Cloud Appliance, Intersight, UCS Fabric Interconnect and Optical Network Controller and no longer names NextFusion Platform; Fortinet now clears FortiADC, FortiWeb and FortiSIEM as well, keeps 29 product names under investigation and says it remediated FortiVoice Cloud and FortiEdge Cloud; Synology's revisions updated APM's fix status to 2.0.2-88107.

entries.headline: GeoServer RCE chain: public PoC, CISA lists two flaws as exploited; update to 3.0.2, 2.28.6 or 2.27.7
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-129244 +5exploitedupdatedNATOA2

GeoServer 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7: a five-step chain from an anonymous WFS request to code execution (CVE-2026-129244, CVE-2026-129243, CVE-2026-120705, CVE-2026-129245, CVE-2026-129242) works on a default installation, was disclosed in advisories published on 2026-11-23 and has a public proof of concept; CISA lists CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243 as exploited, and watchTowr reports exploitation attempts, which NCSC Switzerland relays as actively exploited (CVSS 4.0 9.2 for the critical step)

The GeoServer project published a batch of security advisories on 2026-11-23, most for flaws fixed in 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7, which the project had announced on 2026-10-19 as an important upgrade for production systems (GeoServer, 2026-11-23; GeoServer, 2026-10-19). Five chain, in the order the project gives: a WFS stored-query exception that discloses the data directory path (CVE-2026-129244), service-security rules bypassed with a prefixed service name such as x/WFS so anonymous users can create stored queries (CVE-2026-129243), an unauthenticated WFS GetFeatureById XML injection (CVE-2026-120705), a predictable remember-me key that allows administrator session forgery (CVE-2026-129245, critical) and deserialization in the JDBC user and role services (CVE-2026-129242, administrator required) (GeoServer, 2026-11-23; GeoServer, 2026-11-23). The project says the critical advisory was first reported as step 4 of an unauthenticated remote command execution chain and that each step was given its own CVE at the CVE Numbering Authority's request (GeoServer, 2026-11-23).

The reporter says the chain gives unauthenticated remote command execution on a default installation: the service-name bypass lets an anonymous stored query read the files that hold the remember-me key and an administrator password digest, which forges an administrator session (CryptoCat, 2026-11-23). A full-chain proof of concept has been public since the reporter's write-up. Affected are 3.0.0 to 3.0.1, 2.28.0 to 2.28.5 and 2.27.6 and earlier, with 3.0.2, 2.28.6 and 2.27.7 as the fixed releases (GeoServer, 2026-11-23); the project says the 2.27 series has reached end of life (GeoServer, 2026-10-19). CISA lists CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243 as exploited, and watchTowr reports exploitation attempts, which NCSC Switzerland rated actively exploited on 2026-11-25 (CISA, 2026-11-27; NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-25).

Exposure
GeoServer on the affected builds with WFS reachable by anonymous users and the REST API reachable; the reporter says it works on a default installation, with the stock admin account enabled in the default user service and, for its payload, a Linux host, and that the chain read the live key, so it never depended on the shipped value and a rotated key alone does not close it (CryptoCat, 2026-11-23); the fixed releases use a random per-node key and invalidate existing remember-me cookies on upgrade (GeoServer, 2026-11-23).
Detection
In web access logs, WFS requests whose service parameter contains a slash such as x/WFS, and stored queries you did not create under the data directory's wfs/query and workspaces/*/wfs/query folders (GeoServer, 2026-11-23); in REST access logs, an administrator session that uploads a database file and creates a JDBC user group service (GeoServer, 2026-11-23). If exposure is suspected the project advises changing administrator passwords, because changing the key does not help when the same file disclosure also reveals it (GeoServer, 2026-11-23).
Defender takeaway
Update internet-reachable GeoServer to a fixed release now rather than at the next cycle, since a public full-chain proof of concept exists, CISA lists two of the chain's flaws as exploited and the fixes are weeks old; where it must wait, apply the project's workarounds for steps 2 and 4, and on any instance that ran an older build while reachable, review the stored-query folders and the administrator accounts.
Update26 Nov 2026 05:06 UTCrun 2026-11-26T0356Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytagssectorscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteclassificationactionsbodyupdated_at

watchTowr reports that attackers are exploiting the chain: its vulnerability FAQ of 2026-11-25 says the flaws are being exploited in the wild, and The Hacker News quotes watchTowr that attackers sent error-based exploit probes that create and invoke stored queries to check whether a server is vulnerable (watchTowr, 2026-11-25; The Hacker News, 2026-11-25). The sources disagree on which flaws: The Hacker News names CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129243 in its lead and CVE-2026-120705 and CVE-2026-129244 in its quote of watchTowr, watchTowr's prose names all five chain CVEs, and its own table then marked only CVE-2026-129245 as exploited. NCSC Switzerland's advisory 13242 of 2026-11-25 rates the chain Actively Exploited with a proof of concept available, labels only CVE-2026-120705 as actively exploited and lists watchTowr's post as its source (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-25). No victim, actor or scale is named; the project's own pages make no exploitation statement.

Eye Security's disclosure uses a different last step, CVE-2026-120704, administrator-controlled loading of an SQLite JDBC extension that gives native code execution and is fixed in the same three releases (Eye Security, 2026-11-24); on Windows the project says the extension library can load from an SMB share, so nothing needs staging on the server (GeoServer, 2026-11-23). CVE-2026-120705 echoes file contents only when a layer is published to anonymous users, and its fix reaches embedders through GeoTools 35.2, 34.6 and 33.7 (GeoServer, 2026-11-23). On a cluster, set the same GEOSERVER_REMEMBERME_KEY on every node, because the fixed releases generate a new random remember-me key at each start (watchTowr, 2026-11-25).

CISA added CVE-2026-120705, the unauthenticated XML injection in the WFS GetFeatureById stored query, and CVE-2026-129243, the service-level authorization bypass through a prefixed service name, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-27, saying it did so on evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-11-27). entries.headline: BACS: five confirmed AI-agent attacks in Switzerland, three on critical infrastructure; critical updates within 24 hours
entries.html:
HIGHupdatedNATOA2

BACS: first confirmed cyberattacks carried out with AI agents against Swiss companies and critical-infrastructure operators, five confirmed cases according to its director, three on critical-infrastructure operators; internet-reachable agents such as ARTEX and CyberStrikeAI have almost doubled since October

BACS reported on 2026-11-24 that in recent days it had received its first reports of cyberattacks against organisations in Switzerland carried out with the support of an AI agent, that the victims are various companies and operators of critical infrastructure in at least two sectors, and that in every case known to it then the use of AI agents led to a successful compromise of the victim's IT systems (BACS, 2026-11-24). Its director told SRF on 2026-11-26 that BACS has five confirmed cases, three on critical-infrastructure operators, with SMEs that reported voluntarily also hacked, and SRF reports that systems were compromised in four of the five (translated from German) (SRF, 2026-11-26); RTS reads three critical-infrastructure attacks of which two succeeded, without saying whether the count covers all five (translated from French) (RTS, 2026-11-26). BACS calls these the first confirmed Swiss cases and says the attackers used so-called "Agentic Offensive Frameworks", agents that independently search for weaknesses, choose attack tools, evaluate the results and plan the next steps (BACS, 2026-11-24). Neither the page nor the two outlets name a framework used in these cases, a victim sector or an entry point; SRF reports no larger outages and an unknown actor, and BACS shares technical indicators for detecting such AI tools with critical-infrastructure operators (SRF, 2026-11-26; BACS, 2026-11-24). Netzwoche reported on 2026-11-02 that BACS's GovCERT co-head had said at the Gohack26 symposium that no case in which autonomous AI agents hacked someone had been reported to the office so far (translated from German) (Netzwoche, 2026-11-02).

Describing the tool class in general, BACS says such agents exploit, for example, standard or easily guessed passwords and known vulnerabilities in software or internet-connected systems, often need only a fraction of the time a human would to find and exploit vulnerable systems, and switch to other known attack methods when they meet a defence (BACS, 2026-11-24). It adds that the number of internet-reachable AI agents such as ARTEX or CyberStrikeAI has almost doubled since October 2026, with no baseline or counting method given, names the two tools only as examples and does not say they were used in the Swiss cases, and expects an accumulation of fast, successful attacks (BACS, 2026-11-24).

Exposure
Internet-reachable systems with standard or easily guessed passwords or with known, unpatched vulnerabilities, which is what BACS says such agents exploit; BACS addresses its recommendations to companies in Switzerland and does not name administrations or sectors.
Detection
BACS recommends detecting when identities, applications, workloads and infrastructure deviate from their established behaviour patterns (BACS, 2026-11-24); BACS says it shares technical indicators with critical-infrastructure operators and publishes none in the text.
Defender takeaway
BACS asks that critical security updates for internet-reachable systems be installed as soon as possible and at the latest after 24 hours (the BACS German text gives no start point; the official English page and SRF's report say after release) (BACS, 2026-11-24; SRF, 2026-11-26), that access to exposed systems be limited by allow-list or geo-blocking, and that MFA or passkeys cover every internet-reachable internal resource without exception (BACS, 2026-11-24). Check the internet-facing estate for default and guessable passwords and for patch lag against that 24-hour ceiling first.
Update28 Nov 2026 04:41 UTCrun 2026-11-28T0355Z-intelbodyevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytitle

BACS director Florian Schütz told SRF on 2026-11-26 that BACS currently has five confirmed cases of attacks with AI agents, all reported in recent days (translated from German) (SRF, 2026-11-26). SRF reports that three victims are operators of critical infrastructure and that SMEs that reported voluntarily were also hacked with the help of AI agents, that systems were successfully hacked in four of the five cases (indirect speech, with no named speaker for that sentence), that there had been no larger outages, that it is still unclear who is behind the attacks and that BACS will not name the victims, who have the right to communicate themselves, in Schütz's words (SRF, 2026-11-26). RTS, relaying the interview, reads three attacks on critical infrastructure of which two succeeded, without saying whether that count covers all five cases (translated from French) (RTS, 2026-11-26), while BACS's own page of 2026-11-24, unchanged on 2026-11-28, still says that every case known to it ended in a compromise (BACS, 2026-11-24). The three readings differ, so no single success ratio is a BACS finding. Neither SRF nor RTS says which sectors the three critical-infrastructure victims belong to, and neither outlet names a framework or a public administration. SRF also reports that BACS recommends installing critical updates at the latest 24 hours after their release (SRF, 2026-11-26).

actions: Patch CVE-2026-46300 on every Linux host that runs PHP or other internet-facing code, then on multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners: apply the distribution kernel update and reboot; until then, where IPsec is not in use, block and unload the `esp4`, `esp6` and `rxrpc` modules (this breaks IPsec), and drop the page cache so a file already modified in memory reloads from disk.

On any PHP web host, appliance or management server that was reachable and unpatched for the PHP2Shell flaws, look for PHP files in web-reachable directories that nobody deployed, an outbound SSH session from the host that a systemd service or an rc.local entry keeps up, and password-spray bursts against Active Directory from the host's address, because Dream Research reports a chain of the two flaws that did exactly that.

entries.headline: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia): CISA lists the Linux kernel root flaw as exploited, chained with PHP2Shell
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-46300exploitedupdatedNATOB2

CVE-2026-46300, Linux kernel: local privilege escalation via xfrm ESP-in-TCP ("Fragnesia"), listed by CISA as exploited and chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to reach root, PoC public

CVE-2026-46300 ("Fragnesia") is a local privilege escalation flaw in the Linux kernel's XFRM ESP-in-TCP subsystem. Improper handling of shared page fragments during skb coalescing lets an unprivileged local user modify read-only file contents in the kernel page cache and gain root (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13). The public exploit uses user and network namespaces to obtain CAP_NET_ADMIN inside an isolated namespace, installs a crafted ESP security association over NETLINK_XFRM and overwrites the start of /usr/bin/su in the page cache only, so the on-disk binary never changes (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13). Dirty Frag discoverer Hyunwoo Kim says the flaw was accidentally activated by the patch for CVE-2026-43284 (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14). William Bowling of Zellic.io found it with the company's AI-agentic auditing tool, and a technical explainer and proof-of-concept exploit are public (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14).

The flaw is exploitable by unprivileged local attackers (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13), and CISA's catalog entry says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Risk is highest on shared Linux hosts, container clusters where the page cache is shared across the host, CI runners and build farms, and cloud services running user code (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14). Ubuntu's default AppArmor restriction on unprivileged user namespaces is a partial mitigation that forces an extra bypass (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13).

Exposure
Any multi-user Linux host, container node or CI runner whose kernel lacks the distribution's fix for CVE-2026-46300 (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14). In the exploited chain the host is a PAN-OS management interface exposed to the internet, and Unit 42 says customers who have applied the available PAN-OS fixes are not affected (Unit 42, 2026-10-29). Until the kernel update is deployed, Wiz and Help Net Security advise blocking and unloading the esp4, esp6 and rxrpc modules where they are not required (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13 · Help Net Security, 2026-05-14). Blocking esp4 and esp6 breaks IPsec. Where IPsec must stay up, Red Hat's alternative is disabling unprivileged user namespaces, which can affect rootless containers, sandboxed browsers and Flatpak (Red Hat RHSB-2026-003, 2026-07-03).
Detection
Process and syscall telemetry on Linux hosts (for example auditd or an EDR's Linux sensor): an unprivileged process that creates user and network namespaces and installs an ESP security association over NETLINK_XFRM, followed by su starting a root shell with no authentication step, because the exploit's overwritten su calls setresuid(0,0,0) and executes /bin/sh (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13). The primitive can rewrite any file the user can read, so a check limited to su misses variants (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14); Dream's chain overwrote /etc/pam.d/su instead of the binary (Dream Research, 2026-10-27).

Triage: unprivileged user namespaces are routine for rootless containers, sandboxed browsers and Flatpak, and IPsec is commonly used for VPNs and site-to-site tunnels (Red Hat RHSB-2026-003, 2026-07-03), so either alone is weak; the exploit's signature is one unprivileged process tree that sets up its own ESP security association inside a fresh network namespace and then runs su (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13).

Defender takeaway
Patch Linux hosts that run PHP or other internet-facing code first, and apply Palo Alto's PHP2Shell fixes to PAN-OS management interfaces, then multi-tenant hosts, container nodes and CI runners. After any interim mitigation, drop the page cache, because a binary already modified in memory stays modified until it is reloaded from disk (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14).
Update05 Sep 2026 05:10 UTCrun 2026-09-05T0409Z-intelupdated_atcvessummarysourcesevidenceentitiestechniquesclassificationsourcing_notebody

Red Hat rates CVE-2026-46300 CVSS 7.8 (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-05-13). Red Hat's own security bulletin groups it under the collective "Dirty Frag" name alongside CVE-2026-43284 and CVE-2026-43500, labelling it specifically "Fragnesia (skb coalescing via ESP-in-TCP)": "three vulnerabilities, collectively known as 'Dirty Frag', have been identified in networking subsystems of the Linux kernel, two of which affect Red Hat products" (Red Hat RHSB-2026-003, 2026-07-03). Applicability splits per CVE: "Red Hat says CVE-2026-43500 doesn't affect its products, while CVE-2026-43284 and CVE-2026-46300 do affect supported Red Hat Enterprise Linux kernels and anything built on them" (Aikido Security, 2026-09-04). Any RHEL, OpenShift or RHEL CoreOS estate must therefore confirm the CVE-2026-46300 fix specifically, not only the earlier two. For the Dirty Frag family as a whole (CVE-2026-43284, CVE-2026-43500 and CVE-2026-46300), Aikido writes: "Researchers have already published working proof-of-concept exploits for Kubernetes, and Ubuntu spells out the risk of a container escape"; it names no Kubernetes exploit for CVE-2026-46300 itself (Aikido Security, 2026-09-04). Because containers share the host kernel, a compromised workload that can reach the vulnerable code path (governed by seccomp, pod security and user-namespace settings) can escalate to root on the node (Aikido Security, 2026-09-04). As of 2026-09-05, no source stated confirmed in-the-wild exploitation of this specific CVE. Microsoft's previously reported limited in-the-wild activity ("privilege escalation involving 'su'") was itself stated as ambiguous between the "Dirty Frag" family and the separate, earlier "Copy Fail" vulnerability (CVE-2026-31431) (Microsoft Security Blog, 2026-05-08). That is not a distinction between the two Dirty Frag CVEs themselves, and not specific evidence of exploitation for CVE-2026-46300.

Detection
As an exposure check, compare uname -r against the distribution vendor's fixed package version, not the upstream kernel version string, since backports mean a patched RHEL or Ubuntu host can report an old-looking version (Aikido Security, 2026-09-04). lsmod | grep -E 'esp4|esp6|rxrpc' shows whether the vulnerable code path is loaded, but an empty result is not an all-clear because these modules load on demand (Aikido Security, 2026-09-04). In container and Kubernetes environments, review RuntimeDefault seccomp enforcement, restricted pod policies and unprivileged user-namespace availability, the settings that govern whether a compromised workload can reach this kernel path (Aikido Security, 2026-09-04).
Correction30 Sep 2026 07:16 UTCrun 2026-09-30T0639Z-auditsourcesevidencebodysourcing_noteactionsentities

The interim mitigation is corrected. Until the kernel update is deployed, block and unload the esp4, esp6 and rxrpc modules where they are not needed (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13 · Help Net Security, 2026-05-14). Blocking esp4 and esp6 breaks IPsec, and Red Hat's IPsec-preserving alternative is disabling unprivileged user namespaces (Red Hat RHSB-2026-003, 2026-07-03). At disclosure AlmaLinux and CloudLinux had shipped patched kernels (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14). The entry previously named other kernel modules, a CAP_NET_ADMIN restriction, an affected version range and wider distribution patch coverage that its sources do not state, and it wrongly described Dirty Frag discoverer Hyunwoo Kim as a Wiz researcher.

Correction21 Oct 2026 08:18 UTCrun 2026-10-21T0800Z-audittitleheadlinesummarybody

Aikido's statement that working Kubernetes proof-of-concept exploits have been published concerns the Dirty Frag family as a whole, which it defines as CVE-2026-43284, CVE-2026-43500 and CVE-2026-46300, and its link for the container-escape risk is Ubuntu's page for CVE-2026-43284 (Aikido Security, 2026-09-04). No cited source describes a Kubernetes exploit for CVE-2026-46300 itself; its public exploit overwrites /usr/bin/su in the page cache (Help Net Security, 2026-05-14). On a host, that exploit shows as an unprivileged process creating user and network namespaces and installing an ESP security association over NETLINK_XFRM before su starts a root shell (Wiz Research, 2026-05-13).

Update29 Oct 2026 04:52 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryupdated_atprioritytagstechniquesentitiescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says in the entry that the flaw can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, naming no actor or victim (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Dream Research describes a chain of this kind from artifacts its tooling recovered: a custom, non-public PHP2Shell build, tailored to the PAN-OS management web server, which runs PHP 8.0.30, gives code execution as the nobody user, and the Fragnesia exploit then overwrites /etc/pam.d/su in the page cache so that su root succeeds without a password; Dream says SELinux confines the web server's domain from modifying system files and that the whole chain runs in one HTTP request in under 15 minutes (Dream Research, 2026-10-29). From about 19,000 internet-facing PAN-OS firewalls that it found through a search engine, the attacker narrowed to 240 in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, rooted 24 and planted a PHP webshell on each; on the second of two firewalls of a US government-affiliated organization (the first crashed) it set up an outbound SSH tunnel kept up by a systemd service and an rc.local entry, rooted the organization's firewall management server through the tunnel, decrypted the LDAP service-account password with root access and sprayed passwords against a domain that had no lockout threshold (Dream Research, 2026-10-29). Dream says the recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration but could not tell whether the password spray succeeded, calls the campaign apparently Chinese and AI-assisted and does not attribute it to a named actor (Dream Research, 2026-10-27).

Improvement01 Nov 2026 03:28 UTCrun 2026-11-01T0256Z-intelsummarysourcing_notesourcesentities

Dream Research updated its report on 2026-10-29 to say that the firewalls rooted with a custom PHP2Shell build chained to this kernel flaw run Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS, and counts 25 rooted PAN-OS firewall and management servers; Unit 42 says it independently verified the attacker's tooling and confirmed the reported results (Dream Research, 2026-10-29; Unit 42, 2026-10-29).

Correction01 Nov 2026 13:49 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbody

Dream Research's report, as updated on 2026-10-29, names the rooted firewalls as Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and the exploited surface as the PAN-OS management web server, and says the recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration in the attacked Active Directory, while whether the password spray succeeded is unknown (Dream Research, 2026-10-29). Unit 42 says the PHP flaws are exploited against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet and that customers who have applied the available PAN-OS fixes are not affected (Unit 42, 2026-10-29). CISA's catalog entry says the kernel flaw can be chained with the PHP flaws to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root; it does not itself say which flaw supplies the web-server code execution (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28).

Update27 Nov 2026 04:59 UTCrun 2026-11-27T0355Z-intelsourcesevidencesourcing_notebodyupdated_at

Palo Alto Networks published bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 on 2026-11-24, titled "OSS CVEs Fixed in PAN-OS", whose exploitation-status block reads "Exploitation of CVE-2026-46300 has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet" (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-24). That is the vendor's own statement of exploitation of this flaw, next to CISA's listing and Dream Research's account. The bulletin says "The only known way to exploit this vulnerability requires an attacker to first exploit the PHP2Shell vulnerability through an internet-exposed management interface, and we are not aware of any other exploitation method" (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-24).

It lists a first fixed PAN-OS build for this flaw in every train, later than the hotfix that fixes PHP2Shell (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-24; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29). Its FAQ says a device running a fixed PAN-OS listed in the PHP2Shell advisory is protected, still recommends upgrading to a fixed release at the next maintenance interval where management access is restricted, and recommends upgrading immediately and restricting access where the management interface is internet-reachable (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-24). The bulletin says nothing on Panorama, Prisma Access or Cloud NGFW for this flaw.

updates.summary: CVE-2026-46300's CVSS score has now been published (7.8) and Red Hat's own bulletin confirms RHEL kernels are affected (unlike sibling CVE-2026-43500, which Red Hat states does not affect its products). Public proof-of-concept exploits now target Kubernetes specifically, and Red Hat's bulletin groups this CVE under the collective "Dirty Frag" name alongside CVE-2026-43284/CVE-2026-43500, confirming the ESP-in-TCP exploitation path this entry already described and the coalescing-marker root cause are the same flaw.

The CVSS 7.8 figure came from the MITRE CVE record rather than from a cited advisory. It now cites Red Hat's CVE page, which publishes the same 7.8 score, and an evidence quote taken from the MITRE record is removed. The main text and action now carry the sourced interim mitigation (block esp4, esp6 and rxrpc, or disable unprivileged user namespaces) and the sourced patch status and discovery credits. Unsupported module names, a CAP_NET_ADMIN restriction, a kernel version range, wider patch coverage and a leftover table of three unrelated CVEs are removed, as is an unrelated actor link. The 2026-09-05 section now attributes the 7.8 score to Red Hat and cites Aikido for its container and detection guidance, which no longer says a module listing confirms IPsec use.

Aikido's statement that working Kubernetes proof-of-concept exploits have been published concerns the Dirty Frag family as a whole, not CVE-2026-46300 specifically; the summary and the 2026-09-05 section now attribute it that way, and no source describes a Kubernetes exploit for this CVE. Detection and triage lines are added from Wiz's description of the public exploit and Red Hat's list of legitimate user-namespace uses.

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root; Dream Research describes such a chain used against 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and a US government-affiliated network. The CVE record moves to exploited, the priority from notable to high, and the earlier statement that no source reports exploitation of this CVE is replaced. Removed from the text: the sentence that an attacker can modify any file the user can read (the Detection line still carries it) and, from the summary, the clause on Aikido's report of working Kubernetes exploits for the Dirty Frag family.

Dream Research's updated report names Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS as the product in the chain that paired the PHP2Shell flaws with this kernel flaw, and counts 25 rooted PAN-OS firewall and management servers; Unit 42 says it independently verified the tooling and results.

Dream's report, as updated on 2026-10-29, names the rooted firewalls as PAN-OS, so the 2026-10-29 section now does too and gives Dream's account of what the Active Directory attacks confirmed; the Exposure and takeaway lines now name PAN-OS management interfaces and Palo Alto's fixes. The CISA catalog statement is given in CISA's words, the root-step sentence follows Wiz's wording, and two at-disclosure sentences (Microsoft's no-exploitation statement, which the KEV listing superseded, and the early patch note) are removed.

Palo Alto's bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 (2026-11-24) says exploitation of CVE-2026-46300 has been observed against internet-exposed management interfaces, the vendor's own statement beside CISA's listing and Dream Research's account, and lists a first fixed PAN-OS build for the flaw in every train that is later than the PHP2Shell hotfix.
