entries.headline: Juniper Session Smart Conductor: unauthenticated root command injection exploited; upgrade to 7.0.5, 7.1.7 or 7.2.3
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-103406 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-103406, Juniper Session Smart Conductor before 7.0.5, 7.1.7 and 7.2.3: an unauthenticated OS command injection as root through a crafted salt minion ID in the AutomatedProvisioner (CVSS 3.1 9.8) is exploited: Juniper says at least one malicious exploitation was reported to it, BSI reported exploitation and CISA listed it on 2026-11-25

CISA added CVE-2026-103406 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-25 (CISA, 2026-11-25); the catalogue record says a remote attacker could execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID and names both Session Smart Conductor and Session Smart Router (CISA KEV catalogue, 2026-11-25). BSI had revised its advisory on 2026-11-24 (23:00 UTC) with the summary "CVE-2026-103406 is being exploited" (translated from German), without stating its basis (BSI, 2026-11-24). Juniper itself updated its bulletin JSA112183 on 2026-11-24 to say that at least one instance of malicious exploitation of CVE-2026-103406 has been reported to its security response team, as SecurityWeek quotes it (SecurityWeek, 2026-11-26), and NCSC Switzerland rates the flaw actively exploited (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-26). No source names an actor, a victim or the number of compromised systems, and the only first-exploitation date, ENISA's exploited-since field of 2026-11-25, follows the catalogue listing (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-28).

ENISA's record, which carries Juniper's description, narrows the flaw to the AutomatedProvisioner of Session Smart Conductor: an improper neutralization of special elements lets a remote attacker execute arbitrary commands as root via a specially crafted salt minion ID, scored CVSS 3.1 9.8 with network access, no privileges and no user interaction (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-28). The affected ranges are Conductor before 7.0.5, from 7.1.0 before 7.1.7 and from 7.2.0 before 7.2.3, so 7.0.5, 7.1.7 and 7.2.3 are the first fixed releases (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-28). The record references Juniper's bulletin JSA112183, which could not be read, and its CVE record was published on 2026-10-28. The same release fixes CVE-2026-103409 in the Session Smart Router, an unauthenticated flaw scored 9.8 that can be exploited only before the device is onboarded to Mist or a Conductor (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A Session Smart Conductor on a release below 7.0.5, 7.1.7 or 7.2.3 that a network attacker can reach; NCSC Switzerland names network access to the Conductor's provisioning service (the AutomatedProvisioner) as the prerequisite, with no authentication or user interaction, and no source gives the port or says whether it is on by default (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-26). CISA's catalogue record and NCSC.ch also name Session Smart Router, and SecurityWeek lists 7.2.3, 7.1.7 and 7.0.5 for both products (CISA KEV catalogue, 2026-11-25; SecurityWeek, 2026-11-26), so read the running release on each Conductor and each Router and compare it with the three fixed releases.
Detection
Process-creation events showing a shell or interpreter started as root by the Conductor's provisioning or salt services, minion or router registration events whose ID contains shell metacharacters or command-substitution syntax, and the Conductor's audit and configuration-change records; these follow from the mechanism ENISA relays, and no source publishes an indicator. Upgrading does not remove an attacker who is already in, so a Conductor that was reachable before the upgrade needs a check for accounts, router registrations and configuration pushed from it that nobody made; NCSC Switzerland's check is the fleet list, for router names the team did not create (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-26).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade every Conductor to a fixed release now rather than at the next cycle, since Juniper, CISA and BSI report exploitation of an unauthenticated root command injection; until then, NCSC Switzerland advises keeping the Conductor's management and provisioning interfaces off untrusted network segments (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-26), because the flaw needs only network access.
Update27 Nov 2026 04:51 UTCrun 2026-11-27T0355Z-inteltitlesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyupdated_at

Juniper updated its bulletin JSA112183 on 2026-11-24, before CISA's listing, to say "At least one instance of malicious exploitation of CVE-2026-103406 has been reported to the Juniper SIRT" and to urge customers to upgrade to a fixed release as soon as possible and in the meantime mitigate; the bulletin page itself could not be read, so the wording is SecurityWeek's quotation (SecurityWeek, 2026-11-26). NCSC Switzerland's post of 2026-11-26 rates the flaw actively exploited and says the router ID a joining device supplies is passed unsanitised into a shell command during provisioning key setup, so that root on the Conductor exposes every managed router and its provisioning keys; it relays that Juniper lists no official workaround and advises keeping the Conductor's management and provisioning interfaces off untrusted network segments and auditing the fleet list for router names the team did not create (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-26). Neither source names an actor, a victim or a count of compromised systems.

entries.headline: NFS2ROOT: Linux nfsd pre-auth heap overflow, root shell claimed; limit TCP 2049, Ubuntu and RHEL 9/10 not fixed
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-99362NATOB2

NFS2ROOT, CVE-2026-99362, Linux kernel NFS server (nfsd): an unauthenticated heap overflow over NFSv4.1 or 4.2 that OpenSec says it turned into a root shell with one TCP connection to port 2049 (CVSS 3.1 9.8); fixed upstream in 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 and 7.4-rc1, Ubuntu and RHEL 9 and 10 list no fixed kernel on 2026-11-27, exploit private, no exploitation reported

CVE-2026-99362 is a heap out-of-bounds write in the Linux kernel's NFS server: nfsd4_sequence() narrows the reply buffer to the session's cached-reply limit before it accepts the slot sequence id, a client can negotiate that limit down so every slot has a zero-length buffer, and the server then caches a whole reply into a buffer with no room; the flaw has been present since Linux 3.16 (Linux kernel CVE team, 2026-11-19). The announcement lists fixes in 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 and 7.4-rc1 (Linux kernel CVE team, 2026-11-19); ENISA's record, last updated on 2026-11-23, adds 5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193 and 6.6.163 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-23).

OpenSec, which reported it, says an unauthenticated client reaches a root shell with one TCP connection to port 2049 over NFSv4.1 or 4.2, shows this in its own recording and says its exploit stays private (OpenSec, 2026-11-25). watchTowr reports no exploitation in the wild as of 2026-11-26 (watchTowr, 2026-11-26), and the fix with its root-cause text has been public on the linux-nfs list since 2026-08-17 (linux-nfs, 2026-08-17).

Distribution status as read on 2026-11-27: Debian trixie and the 6.12 backport kernel for bookworm are fixed, bookworm's default 6.1 kernel is not (Debian, 2026-11-27); Red Hat fixed RHEL 8 on 2026-11-26 (RHSA-2026:103817) while RHEL 9 and 10 are listed as affected with no fix (Red Hat, 2026-11-26); Ubuntu shows no fixed kernel on any release from 16.04 to 26.10 (Ubuntu, 2026-11-25).

Exposure
A host that serves NFS. Red Hat says default RHEL does not run nfsd, which limits the attack surface to systems configured to export NFSv4.1 or 4.2 shares (Red Hat, 2026-11-26). OpenSec's test is nfsd loaded, /proc/fs/nfsd/versions showing +4.1 or +4.2 and a listener on port 2049 on a non-loopback address, with a kernel older than the fixed one and no distribution backport (OpenSec, 2026-11-25). No source says whether an empty export list or client-address restrictions reduce the reach.
Detection
OpenSec says the traffic is valid NFS with no network signature and names kernel warnings from nfsd4_check_resp_size, oopses with nfsd4, svc or call_usermodehelper frames, shells spawned by kernel workers on a file server and bursts of short NFSv4.1 sessions from one source; no vendor confirms these (OpenSec, 2026-11-25). On a server that was reachable while unpatched, the kernel-worker-spawned shell is the compromise check.
Defender takeaway
On NFS servers, restrict TCP 2049 to trusted networks, the step OpenSec, watchTowr and Red Hat all name, or stop nfs-server where it is not needed (Red Hat, 2026-11-26); turning off NFSv4.1 and 4.2 is the researchers' mitigation and no vendor endorses it. Then install the first distribution kernel that lists the CVE and reboot. A host that does not run nfsd is outside the exposure the sources describe.

entries.headline: SoftwareOK Q-Dir and DesktopOK installers carried a Python RAT; check hashes, reinstalling may not remove it
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

SoftwareOK: Q-Dir 12.83 to 12.85 and DesktopOK 12.82 and 12.85 installers from the vendor's official site carried a Python remote-access tool, ASEC says the update function may have been affected too, and reinstalling may not remove it

AhnLab's ASEC reports that Q-Dir 12.83.0.0, 12.84.0.0 and 12.85.0.0 and DesktopOK 12.82.0.0 and 12.85.0.0 were replaced with tampered installers on SoftwareOK's official distribution path, and that the SHA-256 of some files downloaded from the official site did not match the value posted on its download page. ASEC says the evidence indicates malicious files were also generated during the update process of installed copies, a point it later hedges (users of the update function "may have been affected"), and that it has not identified how the files were replaced (ASEC, 2026-11-25).

The tampered installer embeds the genuine, correctly signed Q-Dir or DesktopOK executable and runs it from the public user folder so the program appears to work. It then downloads the legitimate 7-Zip console extractor and a package holding a Python runtime and a remote-access tool, unpacks it under a Microsoft-looking folder in ProgramData and persists through a scheduled task, named to look like Edge, that runs the windowless Python interpreter. The tool runs shell commands and Python code, transfers files, takes screenshots and collects system information, and it compares running processes with a list of 1,206 security-product process names and sends the matches to its server. ASEC does not describe the server protocol, names no malware family or actor, and reads Chinese-language comments in the code only as a hint (ASEC, 2026-11-25).

ASEC gives no distribution window. SoftwareOK's release pages date Q-Dir 12.83 to 4 November, 12.84 to 13 November and 12.85 to 21 November (SoftwareOK, 2026-11-21) and DesktopOK 12.82 to 28 October and 12.85 to 19 November (SoftwareOK, 2026-11-26), which bounds only when the listed versions could first have reached users, and its Q-Dir download page carries no notice about tampering as of 2026-11-27 (SoftwareOK, 2026-11-27).

Exposure
Any Windows endpoint on which the listed versions were installed or updated since 2026-10-28; ASEC adds that other versions installed or updated while the tampered files were distributed may be affected. The installed program is the genuine signed one, so a signature check on it passes; the check that finds the tampering is the installer's SHA-256 against the vendor page.
Detection
Software-inventory telemetry for the listed versions; in scheduled-task creation and process-creation telemetry, a task running a bundled Python interpreter from under ProgramData and an extractor tool started by an installer; and egress from that interpreter. After removal ASEC says to look for the Python environment, scheduled tasks, related files and external connections.
Defender takeaway
Treat every host that ran an affected installer or updater as compromised: isolate it, remove the tool and rotate the credentials used on it, because ASEC says uninstalling and reinstalling the utility may not remove the remote-access tool.

entries.headline: Java4Shell: OpenJDK Base64 heap overflow chained to pre-auth RCE in Jira and Keycloak; update Java, attempts seen
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-114938updatedNATOA2

Java4Shell, CVE-2026-114938, OpenJDK 17.0.6 and later and Oracle Java SE on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI: a heap overflow in the Base64 decoder that Calif chains into pre-authentication code execution in Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate; fixed in 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1 and 27.0.1.1, GreyNoise reports exploitation attempts, none confirmed successful against its sensors (CVSS 3.1 8.1)

Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update and the OpenJDK advisory of 2026-11-17 list CVE-2026-114938 in the hotspot compiler component, which Oracle rates CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity (Oracle, 2026-11-17; OpenJDK, 2026-11-17). Calif, one of the two reporters Oracle credits (Oracle, 2026-11-17), says HotSpot's x86-64 Base64 intrinsic, which uses AVX-512 VBMI instructions, calculates a negative output length for a short padded input and that length becomes a full 64-byte write that sends 62 bytes past the end of the array; only the landing position of the write is controllable, a misplaced write can crash the JVM (Calif, 2026-11-17). It scores the flaw CVSS 4.0 9.2 and reports pre-authentication code execution in the default configurations of Keycloak, Jira, Confluence, Artifactory, Jenkins and PingFederate, authenticated execution in several further server products, and a client-side path in which a Java program that opens a TLS connection to a malicious server is compromised (Calif, 2026-11-17). Tenable relays Immersive's claim of a working exploit with no release stated (Tenable, 2026-11-17).

The flaw needs an x86-64 processor with AVX-512 VBMI and affects OpenJDK from 17.0.6 on, ARM64 hosts are not affected (Calif, 2026-11-17). CISA published an alert to patch immediately (CISA, 2026-11-17), and the NCSC.ch Cyber Security Hub says the published research demonstrates exploitation without establishing malicious exploitation (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-17); Talos has seen no exploitation in the wild yet and expects probing (Talos, 2026-11-18), while Tenable relays GreyNoise's report of exploitation attempts as of 2026-11-18, none confirmed successful against its sensors, and VulnCheck's statement that a working RCE exploit is available to its customers (Tenable, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
A Java 17, 21, 25 or 27 runtime, or the Java 8 performance build, at or below the affected builds (Oracle, 2026-11-17), fixed in Oracle's 17.0.21.1, 21.0.13.1, 25.0.5.1, 27.0.1.1 and 8u513-perf (Tenable, 2026-11-17); BACS says to check that the running applications actually use the corrected Java version (BACS, 2026-11-18). The CPU must report the avx512f, avx512bw, avx512vbmi and bmi2 flags, which means Intel Ice Lake to Granite Rapids and AMD Zen 4 or newer (Upwind, 2026-11-17). Pre-authentication reach depends on the application decoding attacker-controlled Base64 with the basic or URL decoder of java.util.Base64 before it authenticates the caller (Upwind, 2026-11-17). Cisco's advisory (version 1.4) lists Secure Network Analytics and Secure Workload as affected and Catalyst Center, IOS XE and ISE as not (Cisco, 2026-11-23); Fortinet lists none as confirmed affected and dozens as under investigation (Fortinet, 2026-11-18); BACS adds internal systems and supplier-run Java software (translated from German) (BACS, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Unexplained hs_err_pid crash logs on internet-facing Java applications, where the log may not name Base64 because the crash comes later (Equixly, 2026-11-17); child processes of the server and administrative activity on identity, build and artifact platforms follow from Calif's chains. In request and application logs, Upwind suggests Base64-alphabet tokens of 32 or more characters that end in = with a length not a multiple of 4, starting with Authorization headers, and bursts of IllegalArgumentException from java.util.Base64$Decoder or of restarts (Upwind, 2026-11-17). An update does not remove a compromise that has already happened (BACS, 2026-11-18).
Defender takeaway
Update and restart, internet-reachable and identity services first. Where an update waits, Calif gives two JVM options, -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics or -XX:UseAVX=2 on x86-64 hosts only, because OpenJDK on ARM does not recognize it and fails to start (Calif, 2026-11-17).
Update19 Nov 2026 05:03 UTCrun 2026-11-19T0355Z-intelaffected_productsbodycvesevidencesourcessummaryheadlinesourcing_notetitleentities

Cisco's product impact: Secure Network Analytics, Secure Workload and further products are affected, Cisco offers no workaround, and its PSIRT is aware of proof-of-concept code but not of malicious use (Cisco, 2026-11-23). Fortinet says it is investigating the impact on its products and lists none as confirmed affected, with dozens under investigation (Fortinet, 2026-11-18). Tenable relays GreyNoise's report of exploitation attempts as of 2026-11-18, none confirmed successful against its sensors, and VulnCheck's statement that a working RCE exploit is available to its customers (Tenable, 2026-11-17). BACS's warning of 2026-11-18 asks operators to prioritise internet-reachable applications and central sign-in services, to include internal systems, to clarify other Java software such as banking software with their suppliers and to have externally operated services confirm the fix, and says an update removes no compromise that has already happened (translated from German) (BACS, 2026-11-18). Tenable adds that as of 2026-11-18 Red Hat and Ubuntu had released no fix and Debian had fixed only its unstable branch, so hosts on those distributions had no stable vendor build yet, and that the Keycloak project recommended starting its server with -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as an interim mitigation, its x86-64 container images tagged 26.8.2-1 and 26.8.2-2 carrying an affected Java build (Tenable, 2026-11-17).

Update20 Nov 2026 05:12 UTCrun 2026-11-20T0356Z-intelentitiesaffected_productssourcesbodysummarycves

Three more vendors published product status. Elastic says Elasticsearch 7.17.3 and later is affected with mitigating factors: remote code execution needs an authenticated user with at least read access on an affected CPU architecture, while unauthenticated actors can cause denial of service; Logstash 8.6.2 and later is affected only through the elastic_integration filter when an ingest pipeline decodes Base64 from an untrusted source, with a crash as the result, and Kibana, Beats, Elastic Agent, APM Server, the ECK operator and Elastic Maps Server are not affected, while Elasticsearch clusters that ECK manages follow the Elasticsearch rule (Elastic, 2026-11-19). Elastic plans fixes in 8.19.26, 9.4.10, 9.5.7 and 9.6.0 with a bundled JDK 27.0.1.1+4 and gives no dates, hot-fixed Elastic Cloud Serverless on 2026-11-18, and says fewer than about 5% of Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, on Azure only, run an affected CPU architecture; a self-managed node is affected only on an x86-64 CPU with AVX512_VBMI (Elastic, 2026-11-19).

Broadcom's Tanzu advisory TNZ-2026-1107 says several Tanzu products ship affected Java runtimes and lists released fixes: Java Buildpack 5.5.0 and 5.5.1, Ruby Buildpack 1.10.104, Tanzu OpenJDK 17.0.21.1+5, 21.0.13.1+5 and 25.0.5.1+5 and Foundation Core 3.1.19, 3.3.10 and 11.0.3, where the identity service and CredHub carry an affected Java 25 runtime that Tanzu has not yet confirmed from the bill of materials; it names -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics as the preferred workaround (Broadcom, 2026-11-19). Palo Alto Networks lists fixed builds of Privilege Threat Analytics, Remote Access Connector and the Secure Access HTML5 Gateway, says PAN-OS is not affected, offers no workaround and is not aware of any malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-11-20). None of these statuses changes the exploitation picture above.

Cisco's advisory reached version 1.3, whose change log reads "Changed Catalyst Center from affected to not affected", and its product table shows Catalyst Center, IOS XE, ISE and UCS Central as not affected, so the Cisco product list above follows that change (Cisco, 2026-11-23). Neither Cisco nor Siemens reports exploitation of its products.

Ubuntu lists fixed OpenJDK packages for openjdk-17 on 18.04 to 26.10, openjdk-21 on 20.04 to 26.10, openjdk-25 on 22.04 to 26.10 and openjdk-27 on 26.10, and marks openjdk-8 not affected on every release it lists (Ubuntu, 2026-11-18). Citrix lists the Linux VDA of Citrix Virtual Apps and Desktops, Citrix Analytics, Citrix Endpoint Management (XenMobile Server), App Layering and UniconOS Management (Scout) as impacted with fixed builds still to be determined, and NetScaler ADC and Gateway, NetScaler Console, StoreFront, XenServer and Provisioning as not impacted (Citrix, 2026-11-19). Mitel's first advisory marks MiVoice 5000, OpenScape Business, OpenScape Voice and OpenScape Xpert not affected and is still investigating, among others, MiCollab, MiVoice Business and OpenScape 4000 (Mitel, 2026-11-19). These supersede the reading of 2026-11-18 that Red Hat and Ubuntu had no fix: Red Hat has released fixed OpenJDK packages for Red Hat Enterprise Linux as of 2026-11-19, while it still lists some products that bundle Java, such as Red Hat build of Keycloak, as affected (Tenable, 2026-11-17).

Keycloak updated its 26.8 container images to Red Hat OpenJDK 21.0.13.1, which includes the fix; the updated tags are latest, 26.8, 26.8.2 and 26.8.2-3, replacing the 26.8.2-1 and 26.8.2-2 images that bundled an affected build (Keycloak, 2026-11-18). Atlassian rates the flaw CVSS 9.2 for its Data Center products, will release out-of-cycle patches once Temurin releases are available, and gives an interim JVM mitigation for the latest Bamboo, Bitbucket, Confluence, Crowd, Jira and Jira Service Management Data Center versions in standard installations (Atlassian, 2026-11-18). Oracle credits two reporters, Albert Yang and Calif's Quang Luong (Oracle, 2026-11-17).

Update26 Nov 2026 05:07 UTCrun 2026-11-26T0356Z-intelsummarysourcesaffected_productsentitiescvesbodyupdated_at

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05193 of 2026-11-25 (status Investigating) lists as known affected Central On-Premises 2.5.8 build 12 and below, New Central On-Premises 3.0.4.4 and below, NetEdit 2.19.0 and below, Analytics and Location Engine 5.2.0 and below, AirWave 8.3.0.7 and below, ClearPass Policy Manager 6.14.x and SD-WAN Orchestrator 9.7.x. It says exposure depends on the environment: an instance whose CPU does not expose the avx512vbmi feature is not vulnerable, which HPE checks with a search of /proc/cpuinfo for that flag (HPE Networking, 2026-11-25). Fixed builds are AirWave 8.3.0.8 and above, SD-WAN Orchestrator 9.7.2.41110 and 9.7.1.42066 and ClearPass 6.14.1-HF3 (expected 2026-12-01); Central On-Premises 2.5.8 build 13, NetEdit 2.19.1, Analytics and Location Engine 5.2.1 and the New Central On-Premises build have no date yet (HPE Networking, 2026-11-25).

Central On-Premises, New Central On-Premises and bare-metal ClearPass cannot hide the flag, so HPE says to restrict management access to a dedicated segment or firewall policy, and it names no JVM option. HPE knows of no public discussion or exploit code against its products (HPE Networking, 2026-11-25).

Cisco's advisory now reads version 1.4: Catalyst Center, ISE, IOS XE, IOS XR and NX-OS read not affected, about 26 other products are listed as affected with the release or date still to be determined, patches for Secure Network Analytics are planned for 7.6.1, 7.6.0 and 7.5.3, and Cisco says no workaround addresses the vulnerability (Cisco, 2026-11-23). Siemens' advisory SSA-810379, at version 1.1 of 2026-11-23, adds Desigo CC Advanced Reporting V8 and V9 as affected with no fix (Siemens, 2026-11-19).

entries.headline: PolinRider: forged backdated commits, npm hijacks and a fake recruiter run a loader at build or folder open
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

PolinRider: a North Korea-linked loader reaches developers through force-pushed forged commits in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories, hijacked npm releases and a fake employer's take-home test, and reads its server address from an Ethereum wallet

Apiiro calls PolinRider a North Korea-linked worm and found it in at least 7,609 GitHub repositories owned by 2,330 accounts, mostly developers' own (Apiiro, 2026-11-09). Three routes, none relying on an npm install script. Forged commits: with stolen GitHub access the worm force-pushes a copy of a commit the owner already made, with the same author, message and date, plus a loader hidden after hundreds of spaces in a build configuration file; in 94% of 9,990 injection pushes the copy claims to be more than an hour older than the push, so git log shows an old commit under the owner's name. Cloning runs nothing; building the project or running its dev, build or lint scripts loads the file, and in the newest wave opening the folder in VS Code is enough (Apiiro, 2026-11-09). Hijacked npm releases: Sonatype found concealed loaders in 12 releases across 10 hijacked packages with no install or postinstall hook, so disabling install scripts does not help (Sonatype, 2026-11-04). A fake employer: JFrog traced AccuraSoftHire, a decoy recruiter with ID-verified LinkedIn recruiters and job ads, whose take-home loads a look-alike npm package and whose scripted camera check fails and hands the candidate a command that installs the same loader (JFrog, 2026-11-09); StepSecurity says taking its site down, as had happened by 2026-11-13, does not end the operation (StepSecurity, 2026-11-13).

The loader reads the latest outbound transaction of a hard-coded Ethereum wallet and decodes two IPv4 addresses from its recipient field (Apiiro, 2026-11-09), then fetches XOR-encoded JavaScript over plain HTTP on port 443, so blocking one server changes nothing; the wallet in the hijacked npm releases also appears in GitGuardian's GhostAction report, which Sonatype says does not establish a shared operator (Sonatype, 2026-11-04). Cleanup does not hold: 1,949 repositories were infected again after being publicly listed, and where owners cleaned up the stolen access often still worked; Apiiro counts roughly 2,300 developers reached (Apiiro, 2026-11-09).

Exposure
Any developer machine, CI runner or coding agent that builds or opens a checkout the worm reached, installs one of the hijacked npm packages, or runs a take-home from an unverified recruiter. Apiiro's checks are a semicolon followed by 200 or more spaces on any branch, a .vscode/tasks.json task with runOn set to folderOpen that runs node, and force-pushes in the GitHub Activity view whose commit is dated days before the push (Apiiro, 2026-11-09).
Detection
In process telemetry, a detached node child with no console started from a build script, editor or package entrypoint; in egress telemetry, build hosts and CI runners resolving public blockchain RPC endpoints and then making plain HTTP requests on port 443 to a bare IP address; in GitHub audit telemetry, force-pushes whose replacement commit repeats the replaced commit's author and message (Apiiro, 2026-11-09; Sonatype, 2026-11-04).

Triage: blockchain developers legitimately call public RPC endpoints; the discriminator is a build or lint process in a project with no Web3 purpose doing so and then spawning a detached node child (Apiiro, 2026-11-09).

Defender takeaway
Treat a machine or runner that built an infected checkout as compromised and rotate what it could reach, because the stolen access, not the file, reinfects; run take-home tests from unknown recruiters only in a throwaway virtual machine with no tokens or keys, and block public blockchain RPC from CI runners (Apiiro, 2026-11-09; JFrog, 2026-11-09).
Update26 Nov 2026 05:07 UTCrun 2026-11-26T0356Z-intelsummarytechniquessourcessourcing_noteactionsbodyupdated_at

SafeDep reports that PolinRider now plants a Python loader in GitHub repositories, hidden in a small utils package or in conftest.py with five import lines added to a start file, and found it in 375 public repositories under 260 accounts on 2026-11-24; no PyPI or npm package carries it, and because it uses only the standard library a scan of requirements files or a lockfile does not show it (SafeDep, 2026-11-24). When Python imports the file, the loader reads the input data of the newest transaction an Ethereum wallet sent to itself, writes it as JavaScript to a temporary file and runs node on it; the next stage is written to the standard input of a detached interactive node process, so it is absent from the process command line, and the node child starts from python or pytest. pytest runs the loader through conftest.py every time, and fixing an import error for the missing utils package also starts it. SafeDep did not contact the command server, so later stages are unobserved, and the stealer behavior it describes comes from the September chain. Its remedy is to delete the planted package, import lines and conftest.py loader, then clean the machines that push to the repository and replace their GitHub tokens and SSH keys (SafeDep, 2026-11-24).

StepSecurity reports that the loader reached open-source projects through commits force-pushed on 2026-10-19 into pull requests that were still open, from one GitHub account, at AsyncAPI Generator, CircuitVerse and Open Food Facts; the malicious commits reuse a clean commit's message and date but are unsigned and carry a different committer name, and none of the merged pull requests contains the loader (StepSecurity, 2026-11-26). In the files it read, the added line is about 315 tab characters followed by the loader, so GitHub's diff looks empty, and the loader runs from a prefix on the build and dev scripts, from a Jest or PostCSS config file or from a hidden VS Code folder-open task. CircuitVerse's pull_request workflows ran on the poisoned fork commits with no approval step, and its maintainers confirmed the loader ran in the desktop build and deleted 40 installers that had stayed downloadable for more than a month; AsyncAPI's CI did not run it, and Open Food Facts' builds failed and its maintainers rotated a secret. StepSecurity counts 576 infected repositories of 622 it fetched, across 311 accounts, and assesses from a shared funding wallet that the fake interviews and these infections share an operator (StepSecurity, 2026-11-26).

Builds on: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets…

entries.headline: Danfoss AK-SM 800A hidden 'code-of-the-day' login is on CISA's exploited list; two post-auth flaws follow
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2025-41450 +2exploitedupdatedNATOB2

Claroty Team82: Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration system managers: undocumented 'code-of-the-day' authentication bypass and post-authentication command-injection RCE with thousands of publicly accessible management interfaces

Companion disclosure to Claroty Team82's Copeland XWEB Pro research, published the same day (2026-08-09T17:59Z), covering the Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration system-manager platform used in supermarkets, cold-storage facilities, warehouses and other commercial environments. Claroty found "thousands of publicly accessible management interfaces" via internet-wide scan data, using platforms including Shodan and Censys: "to understand the real-world exposure of the Danfoss AK-SM 800A, we searched publicly available internet-wide scanning platforms" (Claroty Team82, 2026-08-09).

CVE-2025-41450 is a hidden, undocumented "code-of-the-day" authentication mechanism (Claroty gives CWE-287 Improper Authentication; Danfoss scores it CVSS 8.2). Claroty says the application accepts a specially crafted authentication request containing a generated "code of the day" that bypasses normal login, and that successful authentication through it "results in a fully authenticated administrative session" (Claroty Team82, 2026-08-09). Danfoss's advisory and CISA's catalogue describe the same flaw as letting an attacker generate a web report that exposes internal IP addresses, usernames and store names (Danfoss, 2025-03-24; CISA KEV catalogue, 2026-11-25), and Danfoss fixed it in firmware build 4.2 (Danfoss, 2025-03-24). CVE-2025-41451 (CWE-77 OS Command Injection, CVSS v3 7.6) is a post-authenticated command injection in the alarm-to-email (SMTP) configuration field: a user-supplied value is formatted unsanitized into a shell command executed on the device, which Claroty used to achieve remote code execution (Claroty Team82, 2026-08-09). CVE-2025-41452 (CWE-15 External Control of System or Configuration Setting, CVSS v3 5.4) lets a post-authenticated user inject arbitrary Nginx directives via the exposed headers.conf include and so implant routing directives into the Internet-facing Nginx configuration, enabling denial-of-service (Claroty Team82, 2026-08-09). Danfoss shipped firmware R4.3.1 fixing CVE-2025-41451/41452 (build 4.2 for CVE-2025-41450). Danfoss's advisory scores CVE-2025-41451 at 8.7 and CVE-2025-41452 at 6.8 without naming a CVSS version (Danfoss, 2025-08-01), against Claroty's 7.6 and 5.4. The RCE and Nginx-injection primitives require an authenticated session. Claroty says bypassing authentication gave it the device's full administrative interface and every management function it exposed, among them email notifications, and its next finding is the command injection on the SMTP email configuration page, so on an unpatched device the bypass leads to the two post-authentication flaws (Claroty Team82, 2026-08-09).

Triage: Claroty says the code-of-the-day mechanism is likely intended for vendor support or maintenance, so a login by Danfoss support or by the contractor that maintains the unit is the benign lookalike and an administrative session that nobody on the operator or service-provider side opened is the signal; Claroty publishes no log field that separates them (Claroty Team82, 2026-08-09). On the post-authentication side, unexpected shell-metacharacter content in the alarm-email SMTP configuration field, or unexplained changes to the device's Nginx routing configuration, have no benign explanation for a device whose configuration should change only through documented administrative workflows.

Exposure
An AK-SM 800A on firmware before build 4.2 (CVE-2025-41450) or before R4.3.1 (CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452) whose management interface is reachable from the internet; Claroty found thousands of publicly accessible management interfaces through public internet-scan platforms (Claroty Team82, 2026-08-09), and Danfoss lists the affected range of CVE-2025-41450 as prior to version 4.2 (Danfoss, 2025-03-24) and that of the two post-authentication flaws as prior to 4.3.1 (Danfoss, 2025-08-01).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to firmware R4.3.1 or later (build 4.2 closes only CVE-2025-41450) and take the management interface off the public internet where the upgrade cannot happen at once; CISA lists CVE-2025-41450 as exploited without naming a campaign (CISA, 2026-11-25).

entries.headline: Drupal installer flaws SA-CORE-2026-017 and -019 exploited; update to 11.4.14, 11.3.23, 10.6.23 and run update.php
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-132165 +2exploitedupdatedNATOA1

Drupal core: SA-CORE-2026-017 and SA-CORE-2026-019 (CVE-2026-132165, CVE-2026-136716, both Highly critical) let an attacker use the installer to reinstall a site and take it over or run code, Drupal reports both exploited on live sites, and 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23 are the fixed releases that close both

Drupal shipped its core security release on 2026-11-18 and added a second installer advisory on 2026-11-25. SA-CORE-2026-017 (CVE-2026-132165, Highly critical 20 of 25) says that under specific conditions an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, which can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18); SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166, Moderately critical 14 of 25) is a gadget chain that Drupal says is not directly exploitable (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18). SA-CORE-2026-019 (CVE-2026-136716, Highly critical 21 of 25) says certain sites in unusual or incomplete install states remain open to takeover after the first fix, that the user interface does not show whether a site is in that state, and that it is being exploited in the wild (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-25). Drupal reports SA-CORE-2026-017 exploited on live sites from 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18), and CISA listed CVE-2026-132165 as exploited on 2026-11-24 (CISA, 2026-11-24).

Affected are core before 10.6.23, from 11.0.0 before 11.3.23 and from 11.4.0 before 11.4.14, with 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23 as the fixed releases, so a site on 11.4.13, 11.3.22 or 10.6.22, the fixed releases of the first advisory, is still open to the second; update.php must be run because an update hook repairs sites already in that state (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-25). Drupal says a site that has secured the installer is not vulnerable and strongly recommends securing it everywhere, that Drupal 8 and 9, 10.5.x and below and 11.2.x and below are end of life with no fix, and that Drupal Steward covers both advisories (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-25). Searchlight Cyber's write-up turns database or source-port exhaustion into installer re-entry and code execution on Drupal's official images (Searchlight Cyber, 2026-11-24), while Drupal rates the target distribution Uncommon (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-25). StepSecurity reproduced the re-entry on 11.4.12 and not on 11.4.13 and says the stock .htaccess rule blocking direct PHP requests is unchanged, so code execution survives for an attacker who can write a PHP file into a code directory; no source tests the newest builds (StepSecurity, 2026-11-26).

Exposure
Any Drupal site on core before 11.4.14, 11.3.23 or 10.6.23 whose /core/install.php can be requested from outside, and every site on an end-of-life line, which has no fix; patched Drupal publishes only its major version, so check the installer path and the drupal/core version the site was built from (StepSecurity, 2026-11-26). NCSC-NL says the condition arises when the installer is not correctly secured or removed after the initial installation (translated from Dutch) (NCSC-NL, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Web access logs for requests to the installer on a site that is already installed and, as StepSecurity describes, a burst of database connection-refusal errors together with a burst of HTTP 500 responses and requests to install.php; on a site that ran an affected build, changes to settings.php, a later install time or a changed user 1 (StepSecurity, 2026-11-26). Drupal advises checking logs for unexpected changes to or by the user 1 account (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-25).
Defender takeaway
Update each site to 11.4.14, 11.3.23 or 10.6.23 out of cycle, run update.php, secure the installer and move end-of-life sites to a supported branch; on any site that ran an affected build with the installer reachable, check user 1, the administrators and settings.php, since patching does not undo a takeover (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-25).
Update19 Nov 2026 05:02 UTCrun 2026-11-19T0355Z-intelactionsbodycvesevent_dateevidenceheadlineprioritysourcessourcing_notesummarytagstitleupdated_at

The release the pre-announcement described is out. Drupal published SA-CORE-2026-017 (CVE-2026-132165, Critical 18 of 25) and SA-CORE-2026-018 (CVE-2026-132166, Moderately critical 14 of 25, not directly exploitable) on 2026-11-18, fixed in Drupal 11.4.13, 11.3.22 and 10.6.22 (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18, Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18). SA-CORE-2026-017 says an attacker can use the installer to attempt to reinstall Drupal, which can lead to a site takeover or remote code execution, and the only workaround is to secure the installer (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18). The 18 of 25 rating in the pre-announcement is SA-CORE-2026-017's; neither advisory reports exploitation.

Update22 Nov 2026 14:46 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlineprioritysourcing_notesummarytagstitle

Drupal revised SA-CORE-2026-017 after the release: it now rates CVE-2026-132165 Highly critical 20 of 25, with exploit status Exploit, and says the Security Team received a report that the flaw was exploited on live sites as early as 2026-11-19 19:00 UTC (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-18). The fixed releases (11.4.13, 11.3.22, 10.6.22) and the installer workaround are unchanged.

Update26 Nov 2026 05:06 UTCrun 2026-11-26T0356Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytagscvessourcesevidenceverificationsourcing_noteclassificationactionsbodyupdated_at

Drupal published SA-CORE-2026-019 on 2026-11-25: CVE-2026-136716, Highly critical 21 of 25, a second installer flaw under which sites in unusual or incomplete install states stay open to takeover after the first fix, exploited in the wild according to Drupal, with 11.4.14, 11.3.23 and 10.6.23 as the fixed releases and a required update.php run (Drupal Security Team, 2026-11-25). CISA added CVE-2026-132165 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-24, and the newer flaw is not on the list (CISA, 2026-11-24). Searchlight Cyber published the technique on 2026-11-24 and StepSecurity published its reproduction of the installer re-entry on 2026-11-26, and neither reports observing exploitation itself (their statements repeat Drupal's report) (Searchlight Cyber, 2026-11-24; StepSecurity, 2026-11-26).

Improvement28 Nov 2026 07:33 UTCrun 2026-11-28T0355Z-intelcvessourcesevidencebody

CISA added CVE-2026-136716 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2026-11-27, in an alert that says the additions rest on evidence of active exploitation and does not describe that exploitation, so the statement in the 2026-11-26 section that the newer flaw is not on the list no longer holds (CISA, 2026-11-27). Drupal had already reported the flaw exploited in the wild, so the catalogue listing adds federal remediation tracking and no new exploitation detail.

actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, which do not close the six unpatched AK-SM 800A flaws that Midnight Blue and CCB report, so the interface stays off the internet; change all credentials where compromise is suspected and check the devices attached to the controllers, as BSI advises; and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.
