entries.summary: An independent researcher published proof-of-concept code on 2026-11-08 and 2026-11-09 for what Huntress counts as 33 critical flaws in N-able's N-central appliance, and a second disclosure on 2026-11-12 added 4EverAble2Shell, a chain through Apache Axis (CVE-2026-90436) that works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers, and Agent2Shell, SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints. Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26, 2026-11-10) fixed seven CVE ids and Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16) fixes 17 more, hardens how Agents and Probes authenticate and blocks the Legacy API permanently, but N-able does not name either chain or say it is fixed; Huntress reports public proof-of-concept code for all 17 and no exploitation of them in its partners' environments. Every on-premises server and every Agent and Probe must be on Hotfix 3, including those already on Hotfix 2.
entries.title: N-able N-central: 33 alleged flaws published, and Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16) now fixes 17 more CVE ids and blocks the Legacy API permanently, which 4EverAble2Shell (Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436, exploited on at least 21 servers) and Agent2Shell need; N-able does not say either chain is fixed, and public proof-of-concept code exists for the 17

updates.summary: N-able released N-central 2026.4 Hotfix 2 (build 2026.4.1.26) on 2026-11-10 with seven CVE ids, which replaces the entry's statements that no fix, no CVE ids and no affected or fixed builds existed, and reports scanning activity associated with the public proof-of-concept code but no evidence of successful exploitation; on-premises servers must be upgraded and every Agent and Probe upgraded too.

The researcher's second exploit set, 4EverAble2Shell, chains Apache Axis CVE-2026-90436 with a root escalation, works against Hotfix 2 when the Legacy API is on and is exploited on at least 21 production servers per Huntback, with attempts recorded on Previdian's honeypot; N-able has no fix yet and says it has seen no signs of compromise.

N-able confirmed via Huntress that Agent2Shell, the researcher's other chain set that gives an unauthenticated attacker SYSTEM commands on managed Windows endpoints, also needs the non-default Legacy API, and N-able has published indicators of compromise for customers that have not disabled it; N-able still has no fix, and its earlier statement that it saw no signs of compromise predates the indicators.

N-able released Hotfix 3 (build 2026.4.1.39, 2026-11-16): 17 more CVE ids fixed, Agent and Probe authentication hardened, the Legacy API permanently blocked, and every Agent and Probe must be upgraded even from Hotfix 2. N-able does not say Hotfix 3 fixes 4EverAble2Shell or Agent2Shell, and Huntress reports public proof-of-concept code for all 17 ids.

CISA listed the Apache Axis flaw CVE-2026-90436 behind 4EverAble2Shell as exploited on 2026-11-18. N-able's remediation page reads agent impersonation more narrowly than Huntress reads Agent2Shell: it needs an existing foothold on an endpoint and yields only what an agent receives.

entries.headline: Brotli flaw: Apple fixes iOS, macOS; Siemens WinCC, UMC, Teamcenter, Opcenter mostly unfixed; Mitel, Cisco listed
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-111497exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-111497, Brotli decoder flaw in Siemens industrial and software products (Desigo CC, SIMATIC WinCC, Industrial Edge, Teamcenter and Opcenter among them), Mitel MiVoice Business and OpenScape, with Cisco listing Duo Network Gateway, RoomOS and Nexus 3000 and 9000 switches (Guest Shell) in its combined advisory: Desigo CC takes the .NET updates, while most Siemens products, most Mitel updates and the Industrial Edge Common Configurator fix are still pending

The Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write caused by improper handling of malformed compressed data (Mitel, 2026-10-28), and CISA lists it as exploited (CISA, 2026-10-27). Siemens' advisory SSA-045512, revised on 2026-11-18, lists Desigo CC V8 and V9, all versions, remedied by the latest .NET security updates, Gridscale X DSA from V5.3 below V5.4 (fixed in V5.4) and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0 (fixed in V36.8.0) and, since V1.3, SENTRON Powermanager, Integrated PA Suite Tester and two SICAM products, and scores the flaw CVSS 3.1 9.8 (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30). Its Industrial Edge advisory SSA-443410 fixes six configurator and monitoring applications and has no fix for Common Configurator (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30). Two interim Siemens advisories of 2026-11-10 list 15 industrial and 28 software products, with a fix only for WinCC OA V3.20 and BRAUMAT and SISTAR and mitigations that differ by product, some products having none; neither addresses exploitation (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10) (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10).

Mitel's MISA-2026-0010 (revision 6.0, 2026-11-18) rates the flaw high (CVSS 3.1 8.1) and lists MiVoice Business, six OpenScape products, MiCollab Advanced Messaging and Performance Analytics as affected; OpenScape SBC (V11R3.4.5), MiCollab Advanced Messaging and OpenScape Alarm Response have fixes, the rest planned (Mitel, 2026-10-28).

Cisco's advisory, version 1.14 of 2026-11-17, says proof-of-concept exploit code is available and it knows of no malicious use against Cisco products; it lists Catalyst SD-WAN, ISE, IOS XE, IOS XR and Secure Firewall as not impacted (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27). Its fix table lists Duo Network Gateway (3.4.2), Spaces (24.22.1), RoomOS on Board, Desk and Room Series devices (on-premises 11.41.2.3 and 26.7.4.3) and others with fixes dated November 2026 to March 2027 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A Siemens WinCC, UMC, TIA Administrator, Teamcenter or Opcenter system the 2026-11-10 advisories list, a Desigo CC, SENTRON Powermanager, Integrated PA Suite Tester, SICAM PAS CC or SICAM SCC host, a Gridscale X DSA or PSS®E installation below its fixed version, an Industrial Edge Management instance with Management Applications installed or a Common Configurator on an Edge device, a Mitel product at the versions Mitel lists, a Cisco Duo Network Gateway, RoomOS device or Nexus 3000 or 9000 switch running Guest Shell below the builds Cisco lists, or an iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch, Vision Pro or Apple TV below its November release.
Defender takeaway
Install the 2026-11-09 Apple releases on managed iPhones and iPads (Apple, 2026-11-09), Macs (Apple, 2026-11-09), Apple Watches (Apple, 2026-11-09), Vision Pro (Apple, 2026-11-09) and Apple TV (Apple, 2026-11-13) and the current .NET updates on every Desigo CC, SENTRON Powermanager and Integrated PA Suite Tester host, disable Brotli where it is not required on SICAM PAS CC and SICAM SCC, and move Gridscale X DSA to V5.4 and PSS®E to V36.8.0. On Industrial Edge, update the monitoring and configurator applications to the fixed versions and, where Common Configurator runs, uninstall all Management Applications or stop it on Edge devices. Update OpenScape SBC to V11R3.4.5 and apply Mitel's SESAP and Contact Center workarounds (Mitel, 2026-10-28), and update Duo Network Gateway to 3.4.2 and Nexus Guest Shell to Guestshell 4.9, as Cisco's table lists (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27). For the SSA-242944 products with no fix, disable Brotli at the application or proxy layer and apply the UMC request-filter rule; for Teamcenter, the Opcenter family and Process Preparation X use the knowledge-base mitigations SSA-678870 links.
Correction08 Nov 2026 13:54 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodycvessummary

Siemens' revision of advisory SSA-045512 on 2026-11-06 also added two grid products: Gridscale X DSA from V5.3 up to but excluding V5.4, fixed in V5.4 or later, and Gridscale X PSS®E below V36.8.0, fixed in V36.8.0 or later (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30). Siemens describes Gridscale X DSA as real-time grid stability assessment and PSS®E as transmission planning and analysis software (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-30).

Update12 Nov 2026 04:21 UTCrun 2026-11-12T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryaffected_productscvessourcessourcing_noteactionsbodyentities

Siemens published SSA-242944 and SSA-678870 on 2026-11-10, each still interim, extending CVE-2026-111497 to 15 industrial and 28 software products (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10; Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Fixes exist only for SIMATIC WinCC OA V3.20 below V3.20 P17.1 (update to V3.20 P17.1) and for BRAUMAT and SISTAR V8.2 Update 1 to below Update 5 (update to V8.2 Update 5); Siemens plans no fix for the SIMATIC Profiling Tool and lists none available for SIMATIC WinCC V7/V8, WinCC Unified, WinCC Runtime Professional, WinCC Companion, WinCC OA V3.21, TIA Administrator, the User Management Component, COMOS Walkinside, the Project Server Web Administration Tool or, in the software advisory, any of the 28 products, among them Teamcenter V2412 to V2606, the Opcenter family, PADS and Xpedition (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10; Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). For the industrial products the mitigation is to disable Brotli compression and decompression at the application or proxy layer where it is not required, and the User Management Component and, when UMC authentication is enabled, TIA Administrator also get an IIS request-filtering rule that denies the value br in the Content-Encoding header (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). For the software products Siemens points Teamcenter, the Opcenter family and Process Preparation X to knowledge-base articles that need a Siemens login and were not readable without one, tells HyperLynx, PADS and Xpedition to disable Brotli compression and block it at the network firewall, and lists no mitigation for Innexis Architecture Native Acceleration, Insights Hub, PAVE360 Automotive and Simcenter Executable Digital Twin and Studio (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Polarion, Solid Edge, Calibre, Capital and four other software products are listed as not affected because Node.js is not present or predates Brotli (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-11-10). Neither advisory says anything about exploitation; the exploited status rests on CISA's listing.

Update13 Nov 2026 03:56 UTCrun 2026-11-13T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarycvesaffected_productssourcesbodyentities

Apple fixed CVE-2026-111497 on 2026-11-09: its security notes list a Brotli component entry, "An out-of-bounds write issue was addressed with improved input validation", with the impact "Processing maliciously crafted input may lead to memory corruption", in iOS and iPadOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and 26.7.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Golden Gate 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Tahoe 26.7.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), macOS Sequoia 15.8.3 (Apple, 2026-11-09), watchOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and visionOS 27.2.1 (Apple, 2026-11-09); HomeView Software 27.2, released on 2026-11-12, carries the same fix (Apple, 2026-11-12). The Apple pages read carry no statement about exploitation of this flaw, so exploitation still rests on CISA's listing, and the iOS 18.7.12 (Apple, 2026-11-09) and watchOS 26.6.1 (Apple, 2026-11-10) releases list no Brotli entry, which does not by itself show that those branches are unaffected. Cisco's advisory is now at version 1.12 of 2026-11-12 and lists Identity Services Engine as not impacted (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Update15 Nov 2026 15:04 UTCrun 2026-11-15T1407Z-audittitlesummaryaffected_productscvessourcesbody

Cisco's combined advisory, revised to version 1.13 on 2026-11-13, lists Nexus 3000 and Nexus 9000 Series switches in standalone NX-OS with Guest Shell as affected under bug CSCwx56979, without tying the rows to one of the four Node.js CVEs the advisory covers, fixed by Guestshell 4.9 or by NX-OS 10.3.11 (December 2026), 9.3.19, 10.5.7 and 10.7.1 (January 2027) or 10.4.9 and 10.6.5 (February 2027) (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27). Apple fixed the flaw in tvOS 27.2.1 on 2026-11-13 for Apple TV 4K 2nd generation and later, with the same Brotli entry as its other notes (Apple, 2026-11-13).

Update22 Nov 2026 14:49 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodycvesevidencesourcing_notesummarytitlereferences

Mitel revised MISA-2026-0010 to revision 6.0 on 2026-11-18: OpenScape SBC V11R3.4.4 and earlier now has a released fix in V11R3.4.5, MiCollab Advanced Messaging 23.4 and earlier is affected with a patch available (KB000129143), OpenScape Alarm Response V1.10 and earlier is affected with an update to DAKS-IoT V2.00, and Mitel Performance Analytics 3.6.3.313 and earlier is affected with an update planned for 3.6.4 (Mitel, 2026-10-28). entries.headline: Microsoft's agent-framework on PyPI carried a Python-startup stealer in 1.26.1 and 1.26.2; hash-lock the tree at 1.26.0
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB1

Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 published on 2026-11-17, carried a credential stealer that a .pth startup hook runs every time Python starts, collecting environment secrets and requesting Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions OIDC tokens; both versions were removed and 1.26.0 is the last clean release

Socket reports that the Microsoft agent-framework PyPI package was compromised on 2026-11-17, in versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, both of which install Python startup hooks that collect credentials, environment data and cloud identity tokens and send them to a web endpoint (Socket, 2026-11-17). SafeDep, which flagged both releases independently, says the project is Microsoft's official metapackage, that 1.26.1 appeared at 20:35 UTC and 1.26.2 at 21:08 UTC, that each is a single wheel where earlier releases shipped a wheel and a source archive, and that both were removed from PyPI and 1.26.0 is the last clean release (SafeDep, 2026-11-18). The attacker published 1.26.2 after 1.26.1 was gone, so removing one version did not stop it (SafeDep, 2026-11-18). PyPI lists two maintainers, microsoft and vibiret, an account that joined on 17 November and can also publish five sibling projects; SafeDep reads the join date as pointing to vibiret as the uploader, which neither PyPI nor Microsoft has confirmed, and how the account got maintainer access is not known (SafeDep, 2026-11-18).

Nothing has to import the package: a .pth file runs on Python startup, imports a module and launches collection in a background process or thread, so a pip install in a CI job is enough (Socket, 2026-11-17; SafeDep, 2026-11-18). 1.26.1 routes through the package's own initializer, while 1.26.2 moves the payload to a new top-level module and restores the legitimate initializer byte for byte, so checking only the initializer misses it (Socket, 2026-11-17). The code matches environment variables by substring, such as TOKEN, SECRET, KEY and AZURE, reads other processes' environments and credential files for pip, npm, netrc, git, Docker, Hugging Face and Foundry, and actively requests fresh Azure managed-identity and Azure DevOps tokens, with GitHub Actions OIDC tokens added in 1.26.2; it compresses the result and posts it to a web endpoint and downloads no further code (Socket, 2026-11-17). There is no persistent on-disk marker, so fresh process trees can trigger collection again (Socket, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
Any developer machine, CI job or container that installed agent-framework 1.26.1 or 1.26.2 and then ran Python; lockfiles and requirements files show the installed version, and the last clean release is 1.26.0 (SafeDep, 2026-11-18). While vibiret keeps its access, a fresh install of 1.26.0 also pulls in any new release of agent-framework-openai, -purview, -redis or -tools, which 1.26.0 accepts below 2.0 (SafeDep, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Lockfiles and requirements files naming the two versions, and a .pth file added to site-packages by the package, looked for on disk without starting the environment's Python, because starting it runs the stealer again (SafeDep, 2026-11-18); outbound POSTs to a web-hook service from build and developer hosts; because the stealer requests identity tokens, review sign-in and activity logs for the managed identities and federated credentials the environment could use, from the install time onward (SafeDep, 2026-11-18).
Defender takeaway
Remove both versions, rotate every secret and federated identity a host or job could read, and lock the whole dependency tree with hashes rather than pinning agent-framework alone, which leaves its four sibling dependencies free to update (SafeDep, 2026-11-18); Socket advises rotating potentially exposed credentials where either version was installed (Socket, 2026-11-17).
Update22 Nov 2026 14:47 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditactionsbodyevidenceheadlinesummary

SafeDep updated its analysis on 2026-11-18: PyPI shows that vibiret, an account created on 17 November, the day both malicious versions went up, is a maintainer of agent-framework and can publish five related projects (agent-framework-openai, -purview, -redis, -tools and -postgres), and on 18 November it still had access to all six (SafeDep, 2026-11-18). Version 1.26.0 requires agent-framework-core with an extra that accepts any release of four of those siblings below 2.0, so SafeDep advises locking the whole dependency tree with hashes, since a pin on agent-framework alone leaves the siblings free to update, and holding off on new releases until Microsoft removes vibiret and confirms the releases are clean (SafeDep, 2026-11-18).

It collects environment secrets and credential files and requests Azure managed-identity, Azure DevOps and, in 1.26.2, GitHub Actions OIDC tokens. Both versions were removed from PyPI and 1.26.0 is the last clean release; a second maintainer account created on the day of the attack can still publish agent-framework and five sibling projects, four of which 1.26.0 installs, and how it got access is not known.

entries.action_label: RIKEN Fugaku: intruder entered via the public…
entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: RIKEN Fugaku: intruder entered via the public status dashboard, exfiltrated 430 SSH private keys, tried some elsewhere
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA2

RIKEN Fugaku and Rikyu supercomputers: an intruder entered the internal operational network through the internet-facing operating-status dashboard, planted malicious programs on internal servers and took users' stored SSH private keys and access keys, then tried them on other systems

RIKEN's Center for Computational Science says that between 2026-11-10 and 2026-11-13 an external third party entered Fugaku's internal operational network through the publicly accessible web page that displays the supercomputer's operating status, and that the exact method is still under investigation (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). The intruder tampered with multiple internal servers, some of them with malicious programs; up to 4,222 Fugaku users and 375 Rikyu users are affected (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). From users' home directories it collected and exfiltrated credentials for connecting to external systems such as other organisations' supercomputers and cloud services: 430 SSH private keys, 233 of them without a passphrase and 197 with one (RIKEN, 2026-11-20). RIKEN has confirmed that the intruder tried some of the obtained credentials against other systems and is checking whether damage or secondary misuse followed (RIKEN, 2026-11-17).

RIKEN and the external provider that maintains the system began investigating suspicious network traffic on 2026-11-12, confirmed the access on 2026-11-13 and suspended Fugaku on 2026-11-14 (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). It replaced the administrative keys, invalidated the public keys all users use to log in and halted all running and queued jobs, and it names no actor; it says there is no evidence yet that research data was exfiltrated (RIKEN, 2026-11-17; BleepingComputer, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
A shared compute or research system whose operating-status page is reachable from the internet and sits on a network path to its internal operations servers, and whose users keep SSH private keys or cloud access keys in their home directories (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). Relevant to Swiss research and high-performance-computing operators as a transferable pattern of exposure.
Detection
Authentications to other systems with keys that belong to users of the affected host, arriving from unfamiliar addresses, and changes or unknown programs on the servers that run the system's operation; RIKEN's own reviews cover the network configuration and the rebuilding of compromised servers (RIKEN, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Treat every private key and access key stored on a compromised host as stolen, and a key without a passphrase as usable at once: RIKEN asks users to revoke the matching public key at each external service where it is authorised and to generate a new pair, and to replace any other stored credential through the service concerned (RIKEN, 2026-11-17). A status page that is public should not give a route into the operations network.
Update22 Nov 2026 14:47 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditbodyevidenceheadlinesourcessummary

RIKEN's second notice confirms what the first said only might have happened: the intruder collected and exfiltrated SSH private keys and similar credentials for external systems from users' home directories, 430 keys in all, 233 without a passphrase and 197 with one (RIKEN, 2026-11-20). It has also identified access traces to the registration data of the 4,222 Fugaku users (address, affiliation, phone numbers and the type of identity document used), reports no misuse beyond the connection attempts already disclosed, and says Fugaku resumes only after public services are separated from the administrative network and the servers are rebuilt (RIKEN, 2026-11-20).

Up to 4,222 Fugaku and 375 Rikyu users are affected, RIKEN confirmed that some of the stolen credentials were tried against other systems, and it suspended Fugaku on 2026-11-14. actions: Upgrade every MONAI Label server to 0.8.6 (pip install -U monailabel==0.8.6, or the projectmonai/monailabel:0.8.6 image), because CVE-2026-133968 is exploited and every version through 0.8.5 is affected.

On every MONAI Label 0.8.5 or older server that was reachable from an untrusted network, review it for unexpected file changes before it returns to service, starting with sitecustomize.py, authorized_keys and cron entries that the service account wrote and nobody deployed, because the upgrade does not evict an attacker who is already in.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: MONAI Label CVE-2026-133968 exploited since September: upgrade to 0.8.6; authentication is off by default
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-133968exploitedNATOB2

CVE-2026-133968, MONAI Label through 0.8.5: an unauthenticated path traversal in the datastore upload endpoints gives arbitrary file write and code execution, exploited since September 2026 (Amazon says Cairn AI agents found it as a zero-day against East Asian university servers); fixed in 0.8.6, authentication is off by default (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

MONAI Label 0.8.6, released on 2026-11-22 as a security release, fixes CVE-2026-133968, rated critical: PUT /datastore/image and PUT /datastore/label built the destination path from the image ID and label tag without confining it to the datastore, so a caller could write files anywhere the server process can write, in all versions up to and including 0.8.5 (Project MONAI, 2026-11-22). The project's advisory adds that arbitrary file write can lead to remote code execution, for example through application code, authorized_keys or cron, that authentication is off by default and that with authentication on the ANNOTATOR role is enough (Project MONAI, 2026-11-18). The same release fixes a second path traversal in session upload: PUT /session/?uncompress=true extracted uploaded tar archives without checking member names, and session IDs were used as paths without validation, in all versions up to and including 0.8.5 (Project MONAI, 2026-11-22).

Amazon Threat Intelligence found on 2026-09-10 a publicly reachable, unauthenticated instance of Cairn, an open-source autonomous AI penetration-testing framework, whose exposed history showed a roughly 48-hour campaign from 2026-09-08 against IP addresses of universities in East Asia outside mainland China (Amazon Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-20). Against a medical-imaging AI application the agents mapped the API, found an upload endpoint with a filename parameter, tested it for path traversal and reached arbitrary file write in about 11 minutes; in a later session they wrote a Python reverse shell to sitecustomize.py and triggered a training endpoint, which started a new Python process that imported it and gave a root shell (Amazon Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-20). The operator later gave the agents a proxy into a second university network that ran the same software, which Amazon infers it had reached through the same flaw, and Amazon assesses with moderate confidence that the actor is Chinese-nexus; the same agents ran 16 hours against a hardened Redis instance and tried more than 30,000 credential combinations against a GPU server without success (Amazon Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-20).

Exposure
Any MONAI Label server through 0.8.5 that untrusted clients can reach; authentication is off by default (MONAI_LABEL_AUTH_ENABLE=False), so any client that can connect can write files, and with authentication on the ANNOTATOR role is enough (Project MONAI, 2026-11-22; Project MONAI, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Web or reverse-proxy access logs for PUT requests to the two datastore endpoints whose image parameter carries parent-directory sequences or a leading dot, which the fix neutralises or rejects, and for tar uploads to PUT /session/ with uncompress=true (Project MONAI, 2026-11-22; Project MONAI, 2026-11-18); unexpected creation or change of sitecustomize.py, authorized_keys or cron entries by the service account; and a Python interpreter started by the service after a training-endpoint call that then opens an outbound connection (Project MONAI, 2026-11-18; Amazon Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 0.8.6, which the project calls a security release for every deployment, and whatever the version keep the server off untrusted networks, turn authentication on with roles only for trusted users and run it as an unprivileged account that can write only to the datastore; on a 0.8.5 or older server that was reachable from an untrusted network, the project asks for a review for unexpected file changes before it returns to service (Project MONAI, 2026-11-22). Amazon's own advice is to favour high-confidence detections that trigger automated response, because the agents ran for hours without a break (Amazon Threat Intelligence, 2026-11-20).

entries.action_label: Arctic Wolf: a cleared Windows event log keeps…
entries.classification_html: NATOB3
entries.headline: Arctic Wolf: a cleared Windows event log keeps earlier records in its first EVTX chunk; carve it
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB3

Cleared Windows event logs are not empty: Arctic Wolf shows that clearing an EVTX log truncates it after the first 64 KB cluster and leaves the earlier records in that chunk's free space, where standard forensic tools do not parse or flag them, and recovered a ransomware encryptor's command line this way

Arctic Wolf's incident responders report that clearing a Windows event log does not wipe the underlying EVTX file (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). On clearing, Windows truncates the file after the first 64 KB cluster and resets the first and last record numbers, but that first chunk keeps its earlier records in free space until enough new events fill it (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). In a ransomware case the encryptor needed a password argument to run, and Arctic Wolf found its full command line inside the allocated System.EVTX of a domain controller, stamped about three hours before the final clear and absent from the parsed output of Event Viewer, EvtxECmd and Magnet AXIOM; another log held a netscan execution record and an attacker hostname that survived the same way (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). In a second case a PowerShell log held 44 records of which one was allocated, all of them the same command that clears every log, which shows repeated clearing (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20). Arctic Wolf identified no forensic tool that flags records left in the slack space after a clear, and records come back with some template-held fields missing (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).

Detection
The clearing itself is the alertable event, since Arctic Wolf notes that it often triggers EDR or IDS alerting and is frequently what exposes an attack in progress; the recovery step is forensic: when a log shows as cleared, acquire the EVTX file and carve its first chunk for records with earlier timestamps and lower record identifiers than the allocated ones (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
Do not treat a cleared log as empty; preserve the EVTX files of affected hosts promptly, because new events overwrite the free space once they fill the first 64 KB, and search the whole file, not only the parsed events, for the encryptor's command line, tool names and hostnames (Arctic Wolf, 2026-11-20).

Sources: Arctic Wolf Incident Response

entries.action_label: Rapid7: Webworm hides SoftEther VPN Bridge behind…
entries.classification_html: NATOB3
entries.headline: Rapid7: Webworm hides SoftEther VPN Bridge behind NtMonitor branding, new endpoints and an encrypted config
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB3

Webworm's NtMonitor: Rapid7 finds a custom rebuild of the SoftEther VPN Bridge that removes the open-source tool's detection fingerprints (rebranded metadata, renamed handshake endpoints, a custom handshake watermark, an embedded resource archive and an encrypted configuration), attributed with moderate confidence to the China-aligned actor that targets European governments

Rapid7 analysed what it believes is a so-far unknown custom tool, a modified build of SoftEther VPN Bridge version 4.44 (build 9807) that it attributes to Webworm with moderate confidence (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Webworm is the China-aligned actor that ESET reported in May 2026 moving to European government targets and to dual-use tools such as SoftEther (ESET Research, 2026-05-20). The rebuild keeps the bridge function, which cascades a remote network into the victim's local network, and removes the fingerprints: the PE metadata and internal strings are rebranded as a network-monitoring product (inconsistently, since the service name and many registry paths still say SoftEther), the HTTP handshake endpoints get update-style names, the handshake watermark becomes a truncated PNG header so stock SoftEther peers cannot connect and the stock watermark cannot fingerprint the build, the resource archive that normally sits beside the executable is embedded in it as a PE resource, and the configuration is stored under a new name in a custom-encrypted format (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Rapid7 found no backdoor or other added capability, concludes the actor puts stealth above capability, and says only one antivirus vendor detected the sample although it has been public since January (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
Windows hosts in government networks that Webworm has already compromised; Rapid7 says that in every configuration it holds the VPN is set to bridge a remote network into the local one (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).
Detection
Rapid7's most reliable network detection, where TLS traffic can be inspected, is a POST request to an update-themed CGI path with a JPEG content type whose body starts with a PNG file header; on hosts, look for a SoftEther VPN Bridge service that was not installed by the organisation, in particular one whose binary carries its resource archive inside itself, and for firewall rules added by such a service (Rapid7, 2026-11-19). Rapid7 calls the branding the easiest change for the actor to make next and says the endpoints and watermark can be swapped out trivially, so behaviour that is intrinsic to SoftEther matters more than any one string (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).
Defender takeaway
Government networks in Europe should treat any unmanaged SoftEther VPN Bridge, however it is named, as a persistence mechanism that bridges an outside network into theirs, and learn the tool's intrinsic behaviour, as Rapid7 recommends for the government sector (Rapid7, 2026-11-19).

Builds on: ESET: China-aligned Webworm targeted governments in Belgium, Italy, Serbia and Poland with…

entries.action_label: Hokkaido: municipal data on a subcontractor's PC…
entries.classification_html: NATOA2
entries.headline: Hokkaido: municipal data on a subcontractor's PC hit by K2F stealer via a game launcher; Rumoi's contract had ended
entries.html:
ROUTINENATOA2

Hokkaido: resident-register, support-needed and tax data of the cities of Rumoi and Iwamizawa and the town of Shintoku sat on a subcontractor's development PC infected with the K2F information stealer, which GIS Hokkaido links to the NIKKE game launcher; Rumoi's data was still there after its contract ended

Three Hokkaido municipalities disclosed on 2026-11-18 and 2026-11-19 that personal data they had handed to their contractor GIS Hokkaido was stored on a development terminal of GIS Hokkaido's subcontractor Rimgate, on which traces of the information stealer K2F were found: the terminal was infected overnight on 2 to 3 November, Rimgate found the traces on 4 November and cut it from the network, and GIS Hokkaido told the municipalities between 13 and 16 November (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; Iwamizawa City, 2026-11-18; Shintoku Town, 2026-11-18). The data at risk is up to 71,002 resident-register records (as of February 2022) and 4,503 records of people needing support, with disability category and care level, for Rumoi, whose personal data was still on the terminal after its contract ended; 6,001 resident-register and 986 disaster-evacuation-support records for Shintoku; and up to 10,348 land parcels and 7,037 buildings of fixed-asset-tax data for Iwamizawa; none contains the national My Number and no leak or misuse is confirmed (translated from Japanese) (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; Iwamizawa City, 2026-11-18; Shintoku Town, 2026-11-18). GIS Hokkaido told ITmedia that the PC launcher of the game NIKKE is involved and declined to say whether Rimgate staff ran the game on the work PC; ITmedia adds that a third-party tampering with that launcher, which could deliver K2F on start, became public on 5 November (translated from Japanese) (ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19). This is municipal public-sector data held through a supplier chain.

Exposure
Any administration whose resident, social-care or tax data went to a contractor that subcontracts, and any supplier endpoint where consumer software such as a game launcher can run next to project data; the check is which supplier terminals still hold extracts from finished projects (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19; ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19).
Detection
The infection path is the observable: a consumer game launcher on a workstation that holds project data, and, because K2F steals passwords and allows remote control, password-store reads by non-browser processes and unexplained remote sessions on such machines; the sources give no more specific indicator (ITmedia NEWS, 2026-11-19).
Defender takeaway
Ask each supplier and its subcontractors which of your extracts they still hold, have them delete data of finished contracts and confirm it, and keep consumer software off the machines that handle it; Rumoi's contract had ended yet its data was still on the infected terminal (Rumoi City, 2026-11-19).

entries.headline: Basel-Landschaft: attackers took about 97,000 cross-border work-permit records; no entry point or actor named
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA2

Canton Basel-Landschaft: attackers took about 97,000 records from a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) in the cyberattack on the cantonal administration; the canton cannot say which records, assumes all, and names no entry point or actor

A confirmed data theft from a Swiss cantonal administration: the canton of Basel-Landschaft said on 2026-11-20 that forensic analysis showed the attackers reached a database of work permits for cross-border commuters (permit G) and took about 97,000 records for applications lodged through its online platform since 2016-11-28 (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20). It cannot establish which records were taken and assumes all, took the platform off the network, filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons and names no entry point, tool or actor (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20; Polizeiticker, 2026-11-20), after other cantonal applications had been switched off earlier in the week (Inside IT, 2026-11-20).

Exposure
Persons for whom a permit-G application was lodged, renewed or changed through the cantonal platform since 2016-11-28, and the contact persons of their employers in the canton; the database kept completed procedures too, so people whose permits ended are affected as well (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20). The canton cannot exclude that uploaded documents such as contracts or ID copies were taken but has no indication of it (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
An online application platform that keeps every historic procedure puts the whole archive in play when it is reached, so check how much completed data your own citizen-facing and supplier-run platforms retain; employers of cross-border commuters in the canton should expect phishing and social engineering that quotes correct personal details, because the canton warns that such messages can be built from the stolen data (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-20).
Improvement22 Nov 2026 04:35 UTCrun 2026-11-22T0355Z-intelsourcessourcing_notebodysummary

The canton's media release of Wednesday 2026-11-18 says diverse attacks on the cantonal IT had run since Sunday 2026-11-15, that individual servers had to be isolated from the internet and that further measures would be announced through the AlertSwiss app (translated from German) (Canton Basel-Landschaft, 2026-11-18). Its update of that evening, relayed by Keystone-SDA, counts about twenty applications on six servers being reinstalled and says the IT of the rescue and security organisations was never affected; the Alertswiss warning of the night that the emergency numbers 112, 117 and 118 might be restricted was withdrawn a few hours later, and a government spokesperson said the numbers had stayed reachable and the warning was issued as a precaution (watson.ch, 2026-11-18).

NOTABLECVE-2025-42884exploitedNATOA3

CVE-2025-42884, SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50: a JNDI injection that an unauthenticated attacker can use to read or change server information, fixed by SAP Security Note 3660969 in November 2025 and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-11-20 (CVSS 3.1 6.5)

CISA added CVE-2025-42884 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20, naming SAP NetWeaver, on evidence of active exploitation that it does not describe (CISA, 2026-11-20). The flaw is a year old: SAP's November 2025 Patch Day lists a JNDI injection in SAP NetWeaver Enterprise Portal, EP-BASIS 7.50 and EP-RUNTIME 7.50, fixed by Security Note 3660969 at priority Medium and CVSS 6.5 (SAP, 2025-11-11). ENISA's record describes an unauthenticated attacker who injects JNDI environment properties or passes a URL used during a JNDI lookup, reaching an unintended JNDI provider, which could lead to disclosure or modification of information about the server, with no impact on availability, and it marks exploitation from 2026-11-20 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-20). No source names an actor, a victim or the way the flaw is chained.

Exposure
SAP NetWeaver AS Java with Enterprise Portal, components EP-BASIS and EP-RUNTIME 7.50; whether it is fixed depends on Security Note 3660969 being implemented, and the note text is behind SAP's login (SAP, 2025-11-11).
Detection
Web access logs of the portal for requests that carry JNDI environment properties or lookup URLs from unauthenticated sources, and outbound connections from the portal's server to hosts it does not normally contact, which a lookup to an attacker-chosen provider would produce; no source publishes an indicator or a post-compromise check (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-20).
Defender takeaway
Confirm Security Note 3660969 is implemented on every Enterprise Portal 7.50 system and apply it where it is not; the listing shows the year-old flaw is being used, though no source says against whom or with what effect (CISA, 2026-11-20).

entries.headline: Apache Roller XML-RPC deserialization RCE is exploited and on CISA KEV; upgrade to 6.1.6 or later
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-129448 +1exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-129448, Apache Roller 4.0.0 to 6.1.5: an unauthenticated request to the XML-RPC endpoint deserializes attacker-controlled objects before authentication and runs code on the server; Apache says it is being exploited, CISA lists it, fixed in 6.1.6 (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

Apache's announcement of 2026-11-17 assigns CVE-2026-129448 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) to Apache Roller 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 and says "This issue is being actively exploited" (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). It is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which Apache disclosed on 2026-09-25 for 6.1.5 only (Apache via oss-security, 2026-09-25). Roller's XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17); the servlet is mapped unconditionally, so the request is parsed even when the XML-RPC feature is switched off and no non-default configuration is needed (Apache via oss-security, 2026-09-25). CISA added CVE-2026-129448 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 (CISA, 2026-11-20), and Apache has not said who is exploiting it or how many servers are compromised (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-18). Roller 6.1.6 or later disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the feature is off, and the project's downloads page offers 6.1.7 as the best available release (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17; Apache Roller, 2026-11-21).

Exposure
Any Apache Roller from 4.0.0 to 6.1.5 whose /roller-services/xmlrpc path is reachable, including sites where XML-RPC was switched off in the administration interface; the checks are the deployed version and the enabledForExtensions setting in WEB-INF/web.xml, both of which Apache names (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). Roller is a niche Java group-blogging server with a much smaller market share than mainstream blogging platforms (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Web access and reverse-proxy logs for POST requests to /roller-services/xmlrpc from unfamiliar sources, and child processes started by the Java application server's account, since the flaw runs attacker-chosen code; Apache's announcement names no indicator and no post-compromise check, and an upgrade does not undo an earlier compromise (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 6.1.6 or later now; where that waits, Apache's interim steps are setting enabledForExtensions to false in WEB-INF/web.xml or removing the /roller-services/xmlrpc servlet mapping, then restarting (Apache via oss-security, 2026-11-17). Treat an exposed instance on an older release as possibly compromised, because Apache and CISA report exploitation (CISA, 2026-11-20).

entries.headline: USI Lugano: forms system exploited 9 to 17 November; mainly contact data, 8,000+ warning e-mails sent
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOB2

Università della Svizzera italiana (USI, Lugano): third parties exploited a vulnerability in an online-forms system and had access to form responses and attached documents from 9 to 17 November 2026, mainly contact details, and more than 8,000 e-mails warned those concerned; USI names no product or actor

USI said on 2026-11-19 that unauthorised third parties had access to data held on one of its applications between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-17, by exploiting a vulnerability in the software of an online-forms system that the university uses to collect certain job applications, scholarship requests and surveys (USI via Corriere del Ticino, 2026-11-19). The affected server held the responses to the forms and their attached documents; USI's IT services secured it, USI informed the competent authorities and the people whose data may be affected, and it says the causes and the risk to those concerned are still being checked, which will take several more weeks (USI via laRegione, 2026-11-19). It names no product, vulnerability or attacker, and Ticinonline adds that it is not yet clear when the intrusion began or how long it lasted (Ticinonline, 2026-11-19).

Defender takeaway
Check any forms, survey or application-intake system, your own or a supplier's, that stores uploaded documents, and treat those documents as exposed on a system that was reachable with vulnerable software during the access window of 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-17 (USI via laRegione, 2026-11-19).
Update21 Nov 2026 04:40 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

In an interview of 2026-11-20 USI's chief operating officer said the stolen data are essentially names, e-mail addresses and phone numbers and only to a minimal extent job applications or scholarship requests, that the forms software also serves event management, and that more than 8,000 e-mails warned those concerned (translated from Italian) (Corriere del Ticino, 2026-11-20). He calls the attack the work of AI agents that scan the network for vulnerabilities, offers no technical evidence for that, and leaves the product and the vulnerability unnamed (translated from Italian) (Corriere del Ticino, 2026-11-20).

actions: Upgrade every clustered Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E to X15.5.20 now (X14 and earlier has no fix and must migrate) and, until it is in, limit TCP 4371 to 4372 to the cluster peers' addresses as F6 advises, because CISA lists CVE-2026-76466 as exploited and F6 saw two internet-reachable nodes compromised soon after a public proof of concept appeared.

On every clustered Expressway that was reachable before the upgrade, search erlang.log for a nodeup record naming wombat@127.0.0.1 and check for scanning, SMB, SQL Server and WinRM traffic that starts on the Expressway or its cluster peers, treating a hit as a root compromise, because an upgrade does not evict an attacker who already holds root.

entries.headline: Cisco Expressway root RCE is exploited (CISA KEV, F6 incident): upgrade clustered units to X15.5.20 and check them
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-76466 +4exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-76466, Cisco Expressway-C and Expressway-E: unauthenticated root command execution on clustered devices, listed as exploited by CISA and used in an intrusion F6 investigated, fixed in X15.5.20 with no workaround (CVSS 9.8), alongside same-day hardening releases for Unified CM, Unity Connection and Snort 3

Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-21 fixes CVE-2026-76466 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) in the database service of Expressway-C and Expressway-E: an unauthenticated remote attacker who holds persistent cookies can run operating-system commands as root, because of the use of persistent cookies, and because client certificates are not validated when TLS Verify Mode is enabled for clustering; Cisco does not say how an attacker obtains the cookies (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21). Only devices configured in a cluster are affected; X15.5.3 and earlier are fixed in X15.5.20, X14 and earlier must migrate, and there is no workaround (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21). Cisco's advisory was still at its initial version as of 2026-11-21 and says its PSIRT is not aware of malicious use (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21), which CISA's listing of the flaw as exploited (CISA, 2026-11-20) and F6's incident report below contradict.

The same day Cisco shipped two hardening releases whose worst classes are exploitable over the network without authentication: 9.8 for the Unified CM family and Unity Connection (CVE-2026-76473 and CVE-2026-76474; fixed in 15SU5, release 14 migrates) (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21), and 9.0 with high attack complexity for Snort 3 products (CVE-2026-20043 and CVE-2026-20236; FTD 7.0.10, 7.2.12, 7.4.8, 7.6.6, 7.7.13, 10.0.2 or 10.1.0, Snort 3.12.4.0, Cyber Vision 5.6.0), while Meraki MX devices connected to the Dashboard and Cisco's cloud firewall services updated automatically (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21). Cisco found them in internal testing that included frontier AI models and knows of no exploitation (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21; Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Expressway-C and Expressway-E in a cluster on X15.5.3 or earlier, or on X14 or earlier; the affected component is the database service, and Cisco does not say on which network it listens, so an Expressway-E in a cluster is the case to check first (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21). A standalone Expressway is outside the vulnerable-product statement for CVE-2026-76466 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21), but it still needs X15.5.20 for the hardening fixes, which Cisco lists for every Expressway-C and Expressway-E regardless of configuration (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21).
Detection
F6's marker of a successful exploit is a nodeup record for a node named wombat@127.0.0.1 in Expressway's Erlang system log (erlang.log) (F6, 2026-11-18). Also check firewall and flow logs for connections to TCP 4371 to 4372 from hosts that are not cluster peers, and for scanning, SMB, SQL Server and WinRM traffic that starts on an Expressway or its cluster peers, which is what F6 saw root access used for (F6, 2026-11-18). An upgrade does not evict an attacker who holds root, so review erlang.log from before it.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to X15.5.20 now, clustered units first, and check them for compromise, because CISA lists the flaw as exploited (CISA, 2026-11-20) and F6 saw internet-reachable nodes compromised soon after a public proof of concept appeared (F6, 2026-11-18); until then F6's stop-gap, not a Cisco workaround, is limiting TCP 4371 to 4372 to the cluster peers (F6, 2026-11-18). Plan the move of X14 and earlier, the Unified CM family, Unity Connection and FTD to their fixed releases; Cisco reports no exploitation of those (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21; Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21).
Update21 Nov 2026 04:36 UTCrun 2026-11-21T0355Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryprioritytagstechniquescvessourcesevidenceverificationsourcing_noteactionsbody

CISA added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-20 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe (CISA, 2026-11-20). F6 reports what it calls the first case of exploitation, an intrusion at a Russian organisation: after a public proof of concept appeared, the attackers compromised two internet-reachable Expressway X15.5.3 devices, reached two further cluster nodes in the internal network through one of them and, with root, ran Python scripts they wrote for network scanning, SMB share discovery, SQL Server and WinRM interaction and the review of GitLab repositories to take credentials; F6 reads comments in the code as showing that an AI assistant helped adapt the scripts during the intrusion (F6, 2026-11-18). The actor is not named, and it is not stated whether CISA's evidence is this case. F6's stop-gap when the upgrade has to wait is to limit TCP 4371 to 4372 to the cluster peers (F6, 2026-11-18).

Correction22 Nov 2026 14:43 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditbody

Cisco gives two causes for CVE-2026-76466: the use of persistent cookies and, separately, client certificates that are not validated when TLS Verify Mode is enabled for clustering; it does not say that clustering is what uses the persistent cookies (Cisco, 2026-10-21).

entries.headline: Mitel OpenScape 4000: two unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 Platform flaws; upgrade to V11 R2.14 or restrict access
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-137724 +2updatedNATOA2

Mitel OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, MISA-2026-0013: two unauthenticated flaws in the Platform component rated CVSS 3.1 10.0 (CVE-2026-137724 improper authentication, CVE-2026-137721 command injection) and an adjacent-network command injection (CVE-2026-137723, 9.6); fixed in V11 R2.14, Security Mode restricted access is the workaround, no exploitation stated

Mitel's advisory MISA-2026-0013 of 2026-11-18 covers three flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, tracked by Mitel's internal ids, which the advisory page still lists without CVE ids (Mitel, 2026-11-18). MTLVULN-1785 is an unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw that gives unauthorized access and MTLVULN-1786 an unauthenticated command injection through insufficient parameter sanitization, both CVSS 3.1 10.0 with changed scope; MTLVULN-1793 is a command injection that an unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access can use, scored 9.6 (Mitel, 2026-11-18). The CVE Program records published on 2026-11-27 map them as CVE-2026-137724 for MTLVULN-1785 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27), CVE-2026-137721 for MTLVULN-1786 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27) and CVE-2026-137723 for MTLVULN-1793 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27). Affected are OpenScape 4000 V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.68 and earlier, and OpenScape 4000 Manager V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11 and V10 R1.34, R1.42, R1.54 and R1.68; Mitel does not assess end-of-support releases (Mitel, 2026-11-18).

The issues are corrected in V11 R2.14, Mitel provides PLT HF5 for V11 R1.26 and a patch for V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22 (for the Manager, V10 R1.34 to V11 R0.22), and for customers who cannot apply the fix quickly, enabling Security Mode restricted access is a workaround that prevents exploitation, with the steps in a portal-only article (Mitel, 2026-11-18). CERT-FR lists the risks as remote arbitrary code execution, remote denial of service, policy bypass and loss of integrity and confidentiality, and BSI describes an attacker who can bypass safeguards, disclose information or run arbitrary commands in the context of the system (CERT-FR, 2026-11-19; BSI, 2026-11-19). Mitel's text does not mention exploitation.

Exposure
OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager at the releases above; the vulnerable component is the Platform, and the advisory does not say which of its interfaces are normally reachable (Mitel, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Unauthenticated access to the Platform component from hosts that are not administration or maintenance systems, and unexpected command execution on the platform; both follow from the improper-authentication and command-injection mechanisms, and the advisory gives no detection guidance.
Defender takeaway
Apply the fix for the release in use now; where that waits, turn on Security Mode restricted access, and read the affected range against CERT-FR's wording if the system runs R2.12 or R2.13 (Mitel, 2026-11-18; CERT-FR, 2026-11-19).
Improvement28 Nov 2026 04:42 UTCrun 2026-11-28T0355Z-intelbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytitle

The CVE Program published CVE ids for the three flaws on 2026-11-27, which Mitel's advisory, still at revision 1.0 on 2026-11-28, does not yet list. CVE-2026-137724 is MTLVULN-1785, the unauthenticated improper-authentication flaw (CVSS 3.1 10.0) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27); CVE-2026-137721 is MTLVULN-1786, the command injection (10.0) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27); and CVE-2026-137723 is MTLVULN-1793, the command injection from the adjacent network (9.6) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-27). Each record's description ends with Mitel's internal id, so the pairing is stated and not inferred. The fixed releases and the Security Mode workaround are unchanged, and the page still says nothing about exploitation (Mitel, 2026-11-18).

entries.headline: PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36: FPM request smuggling to code execution; the open session flaw is fixed
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-129289 +7updatedNATOA2

PHP 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37 and 8.2.36: CVE-2026-129289 lets an unauthenticated request smuggle a second FastCGI request into PHP-FPM and run PHP code when the front end reuses FastCGI connections; the release also fixes the session flaw left open in October and follow-ups to an incomplete earlier fix (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

PHP released 8.5.13, 8.4.28, 8.3.37, 8.2.36 and 8.6.0 on 2026-11-19, with up to 18 CVEs per branch (PHP, 2026-11-19). The most direct is CVE-2026-129289: when php://input was opened but not read to the end, PHP-FPM leaves the unread request bytes on a persistent FastCGI connection, so a malformed multipart body can place a second FastCGI request inside the first, and an unauthenticated attacker can bypass front-end routing and execute attacker-controlled PHP code with the privileges of the worker (PHP, 2026-11-19). It requires a front end that enables persistent backend connections and an application path that opens php://input without reading it fully; standard nginx and Apache configurations that close the FastCGI connection after each request are not affected by the demonstrated attack (PHP, 2026-11-19).

Two session flaws close the item the October release left open (watchTowr, 2026-11-20): CVE-2026-115560, where upload-progress session data is written in one serializer format and read in another, and CVE-2026-126714, where an interrupted write by the default files handler leaves a mixed old and new session file; both end in object injection and need an object gadget chain in the application (PHP, 2026-11-19; PHP, 2026-11-19). The fix for the first disables upload progress by default (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129481, a use-after-free of a stale session filename after an interrupted session shutdown, is in PHP's words an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-109619, the PHP2Shell flaw CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-26 (CISA, 2026-11-20), and affects PHP 8.3 and later, and CVE-2026-129182, for PHP 8.5 only, covers further scenarios after the 8.5.12 fix (PHP, 2026-11-19; PHP, 2026-11-19).

CVE-2026-129474, PHP 8.5 only, is exposed on the built-in defaults, because fatal error backtraces are on in 8.5 and the default includes arguments, and php.ini-production, which sets zend.exception_ignore_args=1, or fatal_error_backtraces=0 prevents the attack; PHP confirmed code execution on 8.5 (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129496 needs a startup diagnostic written through a file-based error_log in a non-thread-safe build (PHP, 2026-11-19). CVE-2026-129291, an epoll use-after-free in PHP-FPM, gives root from a worker where catch_workers_output is on and the FPM master runs as root (PHP, 2026-11-19). NCSC.ch lists exploitation as unknown with no public proof of concept referenced, and watchTowr reports none as of 2026-11-20 (NCSC.ch, 2026-11-19; watchTowr, 2026-11-20).

Exposure
PHP 8.5 without php.ini-production settings is exposed to CVE-2026-129474 on the defaults, when an application path enters a magic method (PHP, 2026-11-19). For CVE-2026-129289, PHP-FPM servers whose front end keeps FastCGI backend connections open (nginx fastcgi_keep_conn on, Apache mod_proxy_fcgi enablereuse=on, HAProxy in FastCGI mode) and whose applications open php://input without consuming it, which the PHP advisory says some frameworks do; standard setups are outside the demonstrated attack (PHP, 2026-11-19). The session flaws need an object gadget chain in the application, and the version is shown by php -v on the host or in the container image.
Detection
In web and proxy access logs, malformed multipart/form-data bodies sent to endpoints whose application opens php://input without consuming it, followed by PHP execution that no logged request explains; in process telemetry, a shell or network tool spawned by the PHP-FPM worker, which follows from worker-level code execution.
Defender takeaway
Move the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, to the fixed build of its branch and restart PHP-FPM; where that waits, turn FastCGI connection reuse off (PHP, 2026-11-19). PHP 8.1 hosts need a newer branch for CVE-2026-129291 (PHP, 2026-11-19).

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Cyderes: 'tcherber' VPN toolkit for FortiGate and SonicWall, credential file mixing default and real logins, LDAP sweep
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

tcherber: Cyderes finds an access broker's Go toolkit with VPN clients for FortiGate and SonicWall that, once a tunnel is up, maps internal routes and sweeps Active Directory over LDAP; a credential file mixes default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords (more than 500 FortiGate entries) and connection logs show root-level tunnels into multiple victims in May and June 2026

Cyderes' Howler Cell identified a database holding more than 500 FortiGate VPN credential entries and VPN connection records showing successful root-level tunnels into multiple victim environments during May and June 2026 (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). The recovered Go toolkit wraps OpenConnect with --protocol=fortinet for FortiGate, with a 30-second reconnect loop that keeps the tunnel up, and NetExtender for SonicWall, whose wrapper probes seven login URL paths and ten page patterns to find the authentication domain (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). The credential file mixes default guest, admin and test logins with organisation-specific passwords, which Cyderes reads as both brute-force harvesting and credential-dump sourcing; the broker's forum advert claims the access came from brute-forcing and an "exploit toolkit", which Cyderes relays without confirming (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).

The orchestrator launches the FortiGate client in the background with a 20-second stabilization delay, maps internal subnets and gateways from the established tunnel, and runs an LDAP module that enumerates users, groups, domain structure and domain controllers; port scanning, SMB reconnaissance and credential validation sit in separate tools that the operator runs by hand (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). Cyderes assesses a Russian-speaking operator working as both an initial access broker and a malware-as-a-service provider, with operations ongoing as of September 2026, and notes that the handle comes from a build-path username that one machine or several could share (Cyderes, 2026-11-17). VMRay independently links the same build path to Zer0day Stealer and ENIGMA Locker and calls the same developer the likely author of an HVNC remote-control sample, without mentioning VPN access brokerage (VMRay, 2026-09-01).

Exposure
A FortiGate or SonicWall VPN gateway reachable from the internet that accepts a VPN account with a default or guessed password, or a password that appears in a credential dump; Cyderes names no vulnerability or firmware version and does not discuss multi-factor authentication (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).
Detection
VPN gateway logs for successful logins by default-named accounts and for repeated reconnect attempts from one source about every 30 seconds, the interval of the FortiGate client's retry loop; after the tunnel is up, route parsing and a broad LDAP enumeration of users, groups and domain controllers from an address in the VPN pool follow from the toolkit's orchestrator (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Audit VPN credentials on FortiGate and SonicWall appliances, which is Cyderes' own recommendation, and treat default-named accounts and dumped passwords as the entry the toolkit relies on (Cyderes, 2026-11-17).

actions: On every host that runs CyberPower PowerPanel Business, domain controllers first, compare the extcmd and temp\\profile\\extcmd folders with the product defaults and compare the extcmd folders and the console's event-to-command assignments with what administrators configured and treat unknown scripts as hostile; where the techniques Symantec lists are found (ntdsutil or esentutl on a domain controller, scripts staged under extcmd that no administrator configured, a side-loaded implant), assume Active Directory credentials are exposed and plan a krbtgt reset and wider credential rotation, because Symantec saw this channel used to export ntds.dit from a domain controller.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Symantec: attacker ran SYSTEM commands on a domain controller through CyberPower PowerPanel Business, then took ntds.dit
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

CyberPower PowerPanel Business as a SYSTEM script channel on a domain controller: Symantec traces ntds.dit extraction with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss and a side-loaded implant to scripts that the UPS-management service ppbed.exe runs as SYSTEM; Symantec does not say how the console was reached and no actor is named

Symantec analysed an intrusion in which the attacker used CyberPower PowerPanel Business (PPB), software that manages UPS devices, as the execution channel on a Windows domain controller (Symantec, 2026-11-18). Scripts placed in the product's extcmd folder and staged first under temp\profile\extcmd, are run by the PPB service ppbed.exe as SYSTEM, so the commands of the chain have ppbed.exe as their ancestor and the lineage runs ppbed.exe, cmd.exe, powershell.exe and then the implant (Symantec, 2026-11-18). The attacker pushed the scripts to the PPB web service endpoint /local/rest/v1/file/upload on TCP port 3052, worked hands-on, iterating scripts until ntds.dit was exported with ntdsutil ifm and esentutl /vss, and then side-loaded the implant, an old trusted executable paired with an unknown DLL in a user-profile path (Symantec, 2026-11-18). The channel is a documented product function: CyberPower describes user-programmable command executions for event actions (CyberPower, 2026-11-19), and Symantec notes the attacker did not use power events to trigger them (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

Symantec does not say how the attacker reached the console; public advisories or stolen administrator credentials could give that access, and it names no actor, victim sector or product version (Symantec, 2026-11-18). CISA's 2024 advisory lists PowerPanel Business 4.9.0 and prior as affected by weaknesses fixed in version 4.10.1 or later, which Symantec does not cite (CISA, 2024-05-02).

Exposure
Every host that runs PPB, a domain controller above all, whose web service on TCP 3052 a hostile network or a compromised administrator account can reach; Symantec says to audit the extcmd and temp\profile\extcmd paths of every PPB host against the product defaults (Symantec, 2026-11-18).
Detection
Process-creation lineage with ppbed.exe as the ancestor of cmd.exe or powershell.exe, every script staged under extcmd, whatever its name, certutil downloads and decodes, curl downloads and powershell -ep bypass loading .NET code in memory, inbound requests to TCP 3052 from addresses that do not administer the UPS, and on a domain controller ntdsutil, esentutl and new shadow copies; an unexpected DLL next to a trusted binary in a user-profile path marks the side-loaded implant (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

Triage: the activity looks like a power-management product launching cmd.exe, which defenders may dismiss as a routine power-related recovery process; scripts or event-to-command assignments that no administrator configured, children that are not shutdown or notification routines (which follows from the mechanism) and the absence of a preceding power event separate it from benign use (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

Defender takeaway
Treat PPB hosts as privileged execution surfaces: restrict TCP port 3052 to named administrator hosts, change the default administrator password and keep PPB patched, since CISA names 4.10.1 as the fixed build for its 2024 advisory (Symantec, 2026-11-18; CISA, 2024-05-02); where the techniques Symantec lists are found, assume Active Directory credentials are exposed and plan a krbtgt reset and wider credential rotation (Symantec, 2026-11-18).

entries.headline: Airlock Gateway: Smart Form Protection buffer overflow can crash or take over the gateway; update to 8.5.3 or 8.6.1
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-19707NATOA2

CVE-2026-19707, Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 and 8.6.0: attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response overflows a buffer in the Smart Form Protection feature and can cause denial of service or code execution on the gateway; fixed in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1, no exploitation reported (CVSS 4.0 9.5)

Airlock (Ergon) published CVE-2026-19707 on 2026-11-18 as the CNA. It says attacker-controlled HTML in a backend response can exploit the Smart Form Protection feature of Airlock Gateway 8.5.2 and earlier and 8.6.0, possibly leading to a denial of service or remote code execution against the gateway, and that the issue is fixed in 8.5.3 and 8.6.1 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18). The attack needs Smart Form Protection, or the corresponding expert settings, enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references, and the overflow happens while the gateway parses that response; the response can come from a malicious or compromised backend or from a trusted backend that returns attacker-supplied HTML, for example an application that stores and serves user-provided HTML files (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18). The record scores CVSS 4.0 9.5 with high attack complexity and says that compromising the gateway could also affect the availability and protection of other backends deployed behind it (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18). Airlock's release notes for 8.6.1 and 8.5.3 list a fix for a buffer overflow when decoding HTML entities in the same releases, without a CVE id (Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19; Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19). Airlock's support table shows 8.5 supported until 06/2027, 8.4 past its end of support in 08/2026 and 8.3 no longer supported (Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
Airlock Gateway 8.5.0 to 8.5.2 or 8.6.0 with Smart Form Protection enabled, which Airlock's documentation says requires URL encryption to be activated first, on a mapping whose backend can return attacker-supplied HTML (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18; Airlock documentation, 2026-11-19). Gateways on 8.4 and older are outside support and have no listed fix.
Detection
The record names no indicator; gateway process crashes or restarts and unexpected child processes on the gateway, and backend responses with unusual multi-byte HTML character references, follow from the mechanism (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18).
Defender takeaway
Update to 8.5.3 or 8.6.1, backends that serve user-supplied HTML behind a gateway with Smart Form Protection first; no source reports exploitation, so the order follows exposure rather than a known campaign (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-18).

entries.headline: Idunno.AntiCsrf (ASP.NET WebForms) unauthenticated deserialization RCE exploited, no patch: remove the module
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-131914exploitedNATOB2

CVE-2026-131914, Idunno.AntiCsrf 0.9.1 and earlier, a defunct anti-CSRF module for ASP.NET WebForms: one unauthenticated POST with a crafted CSRF form field is deserialized without validation and runs code in the IIS worker process; Mandiant observed exploitation in the wild and no patch exists, so the module has to be removed (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

Mandiant published advisory MNDT-2026-0048 and CVE-2026-131914 on 2026-11-18 for Idunno.AntiCsrf, a defunct open-source anti-CSRF HTTP module for ASP.NET WebForms, last released as 0.9.1 Beta in December 2008 on the since-retired CodePlex platform and with no active maintainer or official patch (Mandiant, 2026-11-18). In the module's PreRequestHandlerExecute step, once the CSRF cookie and the CSRF form field are both non-empty, it deserializes the form field with a parameterless ObjectStateFormatter, which performs no MAC, signature, encryption or machineKey validation and enforces no SerializationBinder restrictions, so a crafted serialized .NET object in that field runs code in the IIS worker process, w3wp.exe; one POST with no prior authentication or valid CSRF token suffices (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

The module runs before the page lifecycle, so any anonymously reachable .aspx page, or any page that relies on application-level session checks inside Page_Load, is reachable unless it opts out through ISuppressCsrfCheck or the SuppressCsrfCheck attribute; pipeline-level authentication rules run earlier and keep anonymous requests away from pages they protect (Mandiant, 2026-11-18). After the sink the module raises its own error, so the response is HTTP 302 when customErrors is active and HTTP 500 when its mode is Off, and recompiled or customised copies keep the sink under different file hashes (Mandiant, 2026-11-18). Mandiant states that active exploitation in the wild has been observed, names no actor, and says Google's FLARE team completed the root-cause analysis during an incident-response investigation on 2026-11-04 (Mandiant, 2026-11-18); the ENISA record scores the flaw CVSS 4.0 9.3 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-19).

Exposure
An ASP.NET WebForms application whose Web.config registers Idunno.AntiCsrf.AntiCsrfModule under httpModules or modules, or whose bin directory holds Idunno.AntiCsrf.dll; Mandiant says to search by name, not by hash (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).
Detection
IIS logs for anomalous POST requests to .aspx endpoints that return 302 or 500 with elevated request size (cs-bytes, where logged), carrying the module's default cookie __CSRFCOOKIE and form field __CSRFTOKEN, and process-creation telemetry for children of w3wp.exe, which follows from code execution in the worker; if the csrfSettings section is omitted from Web.config, a setter bug overwrites the fallback form field name with RaiseException, so the default field name is not a reliable hunting key on every deployment (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

Triage: the module's own tokens are a GUID cookie and a short serialized GUID in the form field, so a cookie that is not a GUID, or a large Base64 value in the CSRF form field, is not legitimate token traffic (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

Defender takeaway
Remove the module and its DLL and replace it with a supported anti-forgery mechanism, since no patch exists; on environments with evidence of exploitation, Mandiant says to rotate all secrets stored in Web.config and applicationHost.config, machineKey and encryption keys and database credentials included, and to inspect the web roots for unauthorized files (Mandiant, 2026-11-18).

HIGHCVE-2026-90817exploitedNATOB1

CVE-2026-90817, REDCap 13.3.0 up to 16.0.48 LTS, 17.3.9 LTS and 17.4.3 Standard: an unauthenticated chain from a public survey request through the Data Import controller to code execution on the server, exploited as of 2026-10-07 for cryptocurrency mining and listed by CISA; fixed in 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

Securifera, which found the flaw, describes a chain of five faults in REDCap, the research-data platform from Vanderbilt University. The public survey handler checks the passthrough value in two forms, so a double-encoded value reaches the root index.php dispatcher while the route restriction is skipped; the project user-rights object is built before the respondent identity exists, so the public context receives the Data Import privilege and the POST CSRF check is skipped because NOAUTH is defined; the Data Import commit path trusts the posted file name as a local path or PHP stream; the byte-order-mark cleanup writes changed bytes back to the same stream, which turns a CSV cleanup into an arbitrary overwrite; and a compiled-template cache file is then rendered as PHP through a route that works without a login (Securifera, 2026-09-27). An attacker needs only a valid survey hash, with no account, project membership, session cookie, role or CSRF token (Securifera, 2026-09-27); Securifera's repository publishes a proof of concept (Securifera repository, 2026-10-01).

Unit 42's note of 2026-10-07 reports active exploitation: an unauthenticated POST to a public survey URL stages a transient Blade-template web shell under the temp cache, run by php-fpm with the web server's permissions, which executes a Base64 bash cradle entirely in memory and pipes a payload disguised as a JPEG into bash (Unit 42, 2026-10-07). The chain deploys Monero miners, run with randomized syslog-themed process names, with at least four live workers; persistence is a modified crontab, an RSA public key appended to the authorized_keys of every accessible profile and an edited ~/.profile, and the attackers unset HISTFILE and purge the bash history (Unit 42, 2026-10-07). CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe (CISA, 2026-11-18).

Google's GTIG reported in June 2026 that the PRC-nexus cluster UNC6508 had exploited internet-facing REDCap servers of North American academic and medical organisations (Google GTIG, 2026-06-15). REDCap 13.3.0 through 16.0.48 LTS, 17.3.9 LTS and 17.4.3 Standard are vulnerable (Pentest-Tools, 2026-10-23); the CVE record names 16.0.49 LTS, 17.3.10 LTS and 17.4.4 Standard as the upgrade targets (OpenCVE, 2026-09-20).

Exposure
Any REDCap server from 13.3.0 to the builds above that serves a public survey; the attack needs a valid survey hash (Securifera, 2026-09-27).
Detection
Web access logs for POSTs to public survey URLs with a double percent-encoded passthrough and a Data Import route (Unit 42, 2026-10-07) and, where a WAF or proxy logs request bodies, a php:// stream in the file-name field (Securifera, 2026-09-27); transient Blade-template files under the web temp cache, a web-server worker or php-fpm spawning bash, and miner processes started under syslog-style names (Unit 42, 2026-10-07). Securifera's proof of concept deletes its injected cache so that REDCap regenerates a clean copy, so a clean cache does not prove the server was not hit (Securifera, 2026-09-27).

Triage: the survey flow is supposed to allow only the PDF route (PdfController:index), so a public survey request that reaches the Data Import controller or carries a stream wrapper in the file-name field is not benign (Securifera, 2026-09-27).

Defender takeaway
Upgrade now and check crontabs, authorized_keys, ~/.profile and processes on any server that was reachable on an older build, because an upgrade removes none of the persistence Unit 42 lists (Unit 42, 2026-10-07).
