entries.headline: HPE's Aruba wireless bulletin fixes 19 unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0+; HPE knows of no public exploit code
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-79844 +18updatedNATOA2

HPESBNW05162, HPE Networking (Aruba) AOS-8 and AOS-10 wireless: 76 CVEs fixed in one bulletin, 19 of them unauthenticated and network-reachable at CVSS 9.0 or above, across controllers, gateways and access points

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05162 (initial release 2026-10-22) fixes 76 CVEs in the wireless operating systems AOS-8 and AOS-10 for Mobility Conductors, Controllers, Gateways managed by HPE Networking Central, AOS-10 access points (AOS-AP) and AOS-8 Instant access points (AOS-IAP) (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). By the CSAF's CVSS 3.1 scores, 33 of the 76 rate 9.0 or higher (eight at 10.0, ten at 9.8, ten at 9.6, one at 9.4 and four at 9.3); the 19 rated 10.0, 9.8 or 9.4 need network access and no privileges, and the other 14 are reachable from the adjacent network (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). The named mechanisms include authentication bypasses and command injection in the AOS-10 interface and in the PAPI protocol, a buffer overflow and a command injection in the AOS-8 PAPI protocol that arrive as crafted packets on its UDP port, an authentication bypass in the AOS-8 SSH daemon, and SQL injection in the web-based management interface (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). HPE says the flaws were generally found by its internal security research, that it is not aware of public discussion or exploit code as of the release, and that customers are strongly urged to patch; for some of the critical rows exploitation also needs preconditions outside the attacker's control, which the bulletin does not itemise (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).

The bulletin and its CSAF name AOS-10 10.8.x up to 10.8.1.1, 10.7.x up to 10.7.2.6 and 10.4.x up to 10.4.1.13, and AOS-8 8.13.x up to 8.13.3.0 and 8.10.x up to 8.10.0.23; fixed builds are AOS-10.8.1.2, 10.7.2.7 and 10.4.1.14 and AOS-8.13.3.1 and 8.10.0.24 (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). Customers with AP-5xx access points in a FIPS-compliant environment must use the AOS-8.13.3.2-FIPS build or later (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-11-17). Since revision 2 of 2026-11-17 the AOS-10 PAPI authentication bypass carries CVE-2026-95787, which replaced CVE-2026-79845, and CVE-2026-95788 to CVE-2026-95791 were added, all below CVSS 3.1 9.0 (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
Any HPE Networking mobility conductor, controller, gateway, access point or virtual machine that runs a listed version; HPE's CSAF scopes the flaws by software version, so the check is the running version, not the hardware model (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). HPE presumes versions past end of maintenance affected and says installations past end of support should be considered potentially impacted (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). The named surfaces are the CLI and web management interfaces and the PAPI access-point management protocol on UDP port 8211 (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22)(HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Management-plane access and accounting logs for logins and sessions from outside the management segment, and network flow data for PAPI traffic on UDP 8211 or controller management ports from segments that carry users or guests. HPE publishes no detection guidance, so no post-compromise check is defined (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade controllers, gateways and access points to the fixed build of their train, management and PAPI-exposed units first, and apply HPE's management-segment restriction (a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN behind firewall policy) at once where the upgrade has to wait; HPE says it is not aware of public discussion or exploit code, so the order follows exposure of the management and access-point protocol paths rather than a known campaign (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22).
Correction25 Oct 2026 14:04 UTCrun 2026-10-25T1308Z-auditsummarycvessourcesbody

HPE's CSAF does not list wider affected ranges than the bulletin text: both name AOS-10 10.8, 10.7 and 10.4 and AOS-8 8.13 and 8.10 up to the stated builds, and neither carries a 10.6, 10.3 or 8.12 range (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22). What HPE adds instead is that versions past end of maintenance are presumed affected and installations past end of support should be considered potentially impacted (HPE Networking, 2026-10-22). The CSAF scores 33 of the 76 flaws at CVSS 9.0 or higher, ten of them at 9.6, and 14 of the 33 are reachable from the adjacent network, not 34, eleven and 15 (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-10-22).

Update19 Nov 2026 05:08 UTCrun 2026-11-19T0355Z-intelactionsbodycvessourcessummarytitle

HPE revised the bulletin on 2026-11-17 (revision 2). It replaced CVE-2026-79845 with CVE-2026-95787, the AOS-10 PAPI authentication bypass (CVSS 3.1 10.0, unauthenticated, network), with the same affected and fixed builds, and added CVE-2026-95788, CVE-2026-95789, CVE-2026-95790 and CVE-2026-95791, which revision 1 omitted by an editorial error; the four rate between 4.9 and 7.2, so the counts at CVSS 9.0 or higher are unchanged and the bulletin now covers 76 CVEs (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-11-17). It also added a note that customers operating AP-5xx access points in a FIPS-compliant environment must upgrade to AOS-8.13.3.2-FIPS or later (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-11-17). HPE's text still says it is not aware of public discussion or exploit code as of the release date (HPE Networking CSAF, 2026-11-17).

entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP2Shell in management servers and storage: Trend Micro released critical patches for Apex Central and Apex One server on 2026-11-11, Mobile Security for Enterprise on 2026-11-17 and Deep Discovery Analyzer by 2026-11-18, Quest KACE SMA and SDA have fixes and should block ports 80, 443 and 52230 until patched, and NetApp ONTAP 9 is affected by CVE-2026-109618 only, inside the PHP jail

Trend Micro's Download Center dates Critical Patch build 7351 for Apex Central and Critical Patch build 20113 for Apex One Service Pack 1 to 2026-11-11 (Trend Micro Download Center, 2026-11-11; Trend Micro Download Center, 2026-11-11). Both patches upgrade the bundled PHP module to 8.2.35, and only the Apex Central readme names PHP2Shell (Trend Micro, 2026-11-05; Trend Micro, 2026-11-09). The customer advisory KA-0024802, updated 2026-11-18, lists the Apex Central patch as CP B7351 and the Apex One server patch as CP B20113, critical patches 1020 for the Deep Discovery Analyzer 7.7 OS image and 1082 for 7.6 with none planned for 7.5 (upgrade to 7.6), and critical patches for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector (Trend Micro, 2026-11-18). Its Mobile Security for Enterprise row still reads impacted with a critical patch ETA of 17 November, while the Download Center lists Mobile Security for Enterprise 9.8 SP5 Critical Patch 10 dated 2026-11-17 (Trend Micro Download Center, 2026-11-17), whose readme says it includes the official fixes for both flaws (Trend Micro, 2026-11-17). Trend Micro says it has not seen successful exploitation in its products or services (Trend Micro, 2026-11-18).

Quest's knowledge-base article says all versions of the KACE Systems Management Appliance (SMA) and Systems Deployment Appliance (SDA) are affected and that CVE-2026-115560 does not affect them; KACE SMA 15.0 CU5 (15.0.378) and 15.1 CU2 (15.1.177) with PHP 8.4.27 were published on 2026-10-23, the cumulative updates 15.0 Patch 4 and 15.1 Patch 1 do not contain the fix, and the SDA 9.3 hotfix 9.3.312 with PHP 8.3.36 followed (Quest Software, 2026-10-29). Until an appliance is updated Quest says to block all public internet access and, because a potentially exploitable communication path remains after the agent tunnel on port 52230 is established, to block inbound web traffic including ports 80, 443 and 52230 (Quest Software, 2026-10-29).

NetApp's advisory lists ONTAP 9 as affected only by CVE-2026-109618, scored CVSS 4.0 9.2, where an unauthenticated attacker could potentially gain access as the www user but would be restricted to the PHP jail, and lists hotfix builds from 9.12.1P20HF1 to 9.19.1P4, 9.17.1P12, 9.15.1P21 and 9.18.1P9 among them (NetApp, 2026-11-18). CISA lists both PHP flaws as exploited since 2026-10-26, although none of the three vendors reports an exploited case (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A Trend Micro Apex Central, Apex One, Mobile Security for Enterprise or Deep Discovery Analyzer server whose console or web endpoints a hostile network can reach; any KACE SMA or SDA, whose web ports and agent port 52230 are named; any ONTAP 9 cluster whose web services are reachable and that runs a release other than the fixed builds (Trend Micro, 2026-11-02; Quest Software, 2026-10-29; NetApp Knowledge Base, 2026-10-26).
Detection
None of the three vendors publishes an indicator. For a management server or appliance that was reachable before its fix, the telemetry to review is shells and downloads started by its web service and outbound connections the server initiates; this is an inference, since the pages do not describe the attack.
Defender takeaway
Install the Trend Micro patches now (Apex Central, Apex One, Mobile Security for Enterprise, Deep Discovery Analyzer) and keep the Trend Micro, KACE and ONTAP management interfaces off untrusted networks until each is fixed; Trend Micro asks customers to restrict the impacted consoles to trusted addresses (Trend Micro, 2026-11-12).

Apex Central and the Apex One on-premises server stay due on 2026-11-11, Deep Discovery Analyzer on 2026-11-12 and the Trend Micro Web Security cloud service on 2026-11-06, and Trend Micro still says it has seen no exploitation in its products (Trend Micro, 2026-10-30). entries.headline: Confluence Data Center: Axis RCE (Remote API on) now exploited in N-able N-central; update to 9.2.28 or disable it
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-90436exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-90436, Atlassian Confluence Data Center 1.x to 9.x: remote code execution through the bundled Apache Axis behind the Remote API (XML-RPC and SOAP) when that API is enabled; fixed in 9.2.28, Confluence 10 not affected (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

Atlassian's advisory of 2026-11-09 says Confluence uses the third-party library Apache Axis in its XML-RPC and SOAP APIs and that Apache Axis has published a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-90436, that allows remote code execution (Atlassian, 2026-11-09). A Confluence Data Center instance is vulnerable only if the "Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP)" setting is enabled; the setting has been off by default for new installations since Confluence 3.0 and the feature was removed in Confluence 10.0, so 10.x is not affected, nor is Confluence Cloud (Atlassian, 2026-11-09). Atlassian scores the flaw 9.3 (CVSS 4.0, network vector, no privileges, no user interaction), lists Confluence Data Center 1.x to 9.x as affected and 9.2.28 as the fixed version (Atlassian, 2026-11-09). If patching must wait, clearing the Remote API checkbox needs no restart, and a request to the soap-axis1 confluenceservice-v2 servlet path should then answer HTTP 403. Atlassian says it "cannot confirm if your instances have been affected" and asks teams to check affected instances for compromise (Atlassian, 2026-11-09); no source reports exploitation of Confluence, and BSI CERT-Bund's bulletin rates the issue critical and its second revision notes that an exploit was added (translated from German) (BSI CERT-Bund, 2026-11-10). The Apache Axis project says the flaw allows unauthenticated remote class instantiation through a SOAP fault and that it does not expect to release an Axis 1.x fix (Apache Axis project, 2026-11-06), and the same flaw is exploited against on-premises N-able N-central servers (Huntback, 2026-11-12; Previdian, 2026-11-12; BleepingComputer, 2026-11-12).

Exposure
A Data Center instance on any 9.x or earlier release, with 9.2.28 the only fixed version listed, whose Remote API (XML-RPC & SOAP) setting is ticked; the setting sits under General Configuration, Further Configuration.
Detection
Web access logs for requests to the soap-axis1 servlet path and the XML-RPC endpoint from unexpected sources, and child processes of the Confluence JVM that the application does not normally start; this is an inference from the attack mechanics, not a source statement.
Defender takeaway
Switch the Remote API off today and upgrade to 9.2.28, because the flaw is already exploited against another product's embedded Axis; because Atlassian asks for a compromise check, review the access logs of any instance that had the API enabled and was reachable from untrusted networks.
Update13 Nov 2026 03:55 UTCrun 2026-11-13T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarysourcing_notesourcesbody

The same flaw, CVE-2026-90436, is now exploited against another product: it is the first stage of the 4EverAble2Shell chain on N-able N-central servers, followed by a separate root escalation (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-12). Huntback counts at least 21 production N-central servers running a cryptominer after a crafted SOAP fault sent to the Apache Axis endpoint (Huntback, 2026-11-12), and Previdian's honeypot recorded attempts at the chain (Previdian, 2026-11-12). No source reports exploitation of Confluence. The Apache Axis project says it does not expect to release an Axis 1.x fix (Apache Axis project, 2026-11-06), so a Confluence instance with the Remote API ticked relies on Atlassian's 9.2.28 or on switching the setting off.

Update19 Nov 2026 05:05 UTCrun 2026-11-19T0355Z-intelbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notetags

CISA added CVE-2026-90436 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18 on evidence of active exploitation, naming neither Confluence nor N-able N-central and no actor; the exploitation reported so far is against N-able N-central, not Confluence (CISA, 2026-11-18). Apache's announcement adds that the fault is parsed while the engine resolves the target service, before any per-service handler chain runs, so authentication handlers configured on a service do not protect against it, and recommends migrating from the end-of-life Axis 1 to a different SOAP engine such as Apache Axis 2/Java (Apache Axis project, 2026-11-06). Atlassian's advisory is unchanged and still says it cannot confirm whether instances were affected (Atlassian, 2026-11-09).

The fix is 9.2.28; the workaround is to clear the Remote API checkbox without a restart; Atlassian cannot confirm whether instances were affected and asks teams to check them; no source reports exploitation of Confluence, but the same flaw is exploited against N-able N-central servers that embed Axis.

entries.headline: LiteLLM: CISA lists the guardrail sandbox escape CVE-2026-40217 as exploited; the chain gives root on the AI gateway
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-47101 +2exploitedupdatedNATOB2

Obsidian Security: a three-CVE chain turns any LiteLLM user into root on the AI gateway; CISA lists the guardrail sandbox escape CVE-2026-40217 as exploited

Obsidian Security published a privilege-escalation-to-RCE chain in LiteLLM (BerriAI), the widely self-hosted AI gateway that proxies 100+ LLM providers behind one OpenAI-compatible API (Obsidian Security, 2026-06-11; The Hacker News, 2026-06-15). The chain starts with CVE-2026-47101 (authorization bypass): the key-generation endpoint accepts a caller-supplied allowed_routes without checking the caller's role, so an internal_user can mint a key reaching admin routes. CVE-2026-47102 (privilege escalation) follows: /user/update lacks field-level authorization, letting any authenticated user set their own user_role to proxy_admin. CVE-2026-40217 (RCE) ends it: LiteLLM's advisory says the sandbox around custom-code guardrails can be escaped using bytecode-level techniques, giving arbitrary code execution in the proxy process, which runs as root in the default Docker image, and that POST /guardrails/test_custom_code needs a proxy-admin credential in default configurations (LiteLLM advisory, 2026-05-07); Obsidian also ties CVE-2026-40217 to the production routes POST /guardrails and PUT /guardrails/{id}, which run user code with exec(), while the vendor's workaround names only the test endpoint (Obsidian Security, 2026-06-11). VulnCheck scores CVE-2026-47102 at CVSS 8.8 (3.1) (The Hacker News, 2026-06-15), and Obsidian rates the chained impact CVSS 9.9; chained, a default low-privilege account reaches the master key, the salt key decrypting stored secrets, the database URL and every configured provider API key, and can rewrite responses delivered to downstream AI agents ("man-in-the-gateway") (Obsidian Security, 2026-06-11). The chain is fixed in v1.83.14-stable, the first release that Obsidian says contains the complete fix set.

CISA added CVE-2026-40217 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18 on evidence of active exploitation; the alert names no actor or victim and does not say whether attackers held an administrator credential or used the other two flaws (CISA, 2026-11-18).

Exposure
Any LiteLLM proxy before v1.83.14-stable that untrusted or low-privilege users can reach: the guardrail endpoint needs a proxy-admin credential by default, and the chain's privilege escalation gives any authenticated user that role (LiteLLM advisory, 2026-05-07; Obsidian Security, 2026-06-11).
Detection
Proxy access logs for POST requests to /guardrails/test_custom_code, POST /guardrails and PUT /guardrails/{id}, for /key/generate calls that carry allowed_routes, and for /user/update and /user/bulk_update calls that set user_role to proxy_admin (Obsidian Security, 2026-06-11); process lineage for unexpected children of the proxy process follows from the code execution.
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to v1.83.14-stable or later, the first release with the complete fix set (Obsidian Security, 2026-06-11), and block the guardrail endpoint at the reverse proxy until then, as LiteLLM's advisory says (LiteLLM advisory, 2026-05-07); where exposure is suspected, rotate every provider API key, the database credentials and any MCP tokens stored in the proxy and audit every Custom Code Guardrail, the callbacks loaded under litellm_settings.callbacks and the holders of proxy_admin, as Obsidian advises (Obsidian Security, 2026-06-11); an instance that an untrusted user could reach on an older build counts as suspected, and the master key and the salt key that the chain reaches belong on the same rotation, with admin endpoints kept off the internet.
Update19 Nov 2026 05:04 UTCrun 2026-11-19T0355Z-intelactionsbodyclassificationcvesentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquesaffected_productstitleverificationconfidenceevent_date

CISA added CVE-2026-40217 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-18 on evidence of active exploitation it does not describe (CISA, 2026-11-18). LiteLLM's own advisory describes the flaw as a sandbox escape using bytecode-level techniques at POST /guardrails/test_custom_code that gives code execution in the proxy process, root in the default Docker image, requires a proxy-admin credential in default configurations, rates it Moderate at CVSS 4.0 5.9 and offers blocking the endpoint at the reverse proxy as the workaround; it names 1.83.11 as the fix in its text and 1.83.10 in its patched-versions field (LiteLLM advisory, 2026-05-07). v1.83.14-stable remains the fix for the whole chain.

Improvement22 Nov 2026 14:59 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditcvessourcessourcing_notesummary

Contradiction on the exploited mechanism: Google Threat Intelligence Group reports that an actor exploited "a user ID rebind vulnerability in the /key/regenerate endpoint (CVE-2026-40217) to elevate standard Virtual Keys into full PROXY\_ADMIN master administrative credentials" against a victim's LiteLLM gateway (GTIG, 2026-11-02), while LiteLLM's advisory describes CVE-2026-40217 as the guardrail sandbox escape. VulnCheck's advisory scores CVE-2026-47101 at CVSS 4.0 8.7 (VulnCheck, 2026-05-21).

entries.headline: C3RB3R hits Synology NAS; CISA lists CVE-2024-10441 as exploited, 360 names the September pair; update DSM
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-13684 +4exploitedupdatedNATOA3

CVE-2026-13684 / CVE-2026-13639, Synology DSM: two unauthenticated CVSS 9.8 flaws (SCGI output-encoding bug, login-logic entropy weakness) allow remote arbitrary file read/write and denial-of-service with no credentials; C3RB3R ransomware is encrypting NAS on outdated DSM and CISA lists the 2024 flaw CVE-2024-10441 as exploited

Synology disclosed eight CVEs in DiskStation Manager (DSM) on 2026-09-18 (Synology-SA-26:13). Two are unauthenticated and rated CVSS 9.8, CVE-2026-13684 (improper output encoding in the SCGI component) and CVE-2026-13639 (insufficient entropy in the login logic), and each lets a remote attacker with no credentials read or write arbitrary files and cause denial-of-service. Two more need only a low-privileged session: CVE-2026-13673 (8.8, LDAP API) and CVE-2026-6205 (8.1, Upload API). All four are fixed in DSM 7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9 and 7.2.1-69057-12, and Synology lists no mitigation for the unauthenticated pair (Synology PSIRT, 2026-09-18).

NCSC Switzerland recorded exploitation status as unknown on 2026-09-21 (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-09-21), and CERT-FR relayed the advisory the same day without commenting on exploitation (CERT-FR, 2026-09-21). heise online expected the terse advisory to draw ransomware authors and other criminals quickly, since Synology describes exploitation as very easy (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-09-18).

Synology said on 2026-10-29 that threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 against outdated DSM to encrypt data and extort ransom, naming no CVE and pointing to Synology-SA-24:20 (Synology, 2026-10-29), whose lead flaw, CVE-2024-10441, allows remote code execution without credentials (CVSS 9.8) (Synology PSIRT, 2024-11-05). The same day 360 identified the ransomware as C3RB3R, a Cerber variant, and named CVE-2026-13639 and CVE-2026-13684 as its entry point (translated from Chinese) (360, 2026-10-29). The accounts conflict: CISA's listing of CVE-2024-10441 on 2026-11-18 supports Synology's pointer to SA-24:20 (CISA, 2026-11-18), and no source corroborates 360's naming of the two September flaws. BleepingComputer says the name is borrowed from the 2016 Cerber ransomware-as-a-service operation and reports Shadowserver tracking over 380,000 internet-exposed Synology NAS (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-02).

Exposure
Any DSM below the fixed build of its branch in Synology-SA-26:13 (7.4-90075, 7.3.2-86009-4, 7.2.2-72806-9, 7.2.1-69057-12) (Synology PSIRT, 2026-09-18) or Synology-SA-24:20 (7.2.2-72806-1, 7.2.1-69057-6, 7.2-64570-4, 7.1.1-42962-7, 6.2.4-25556-8), the only fixes the two advisories name for DSM 7.1, 7.2 and 6.2 (Synology PSIRT, 2024-11-05), with the DSM management interface reachable over the network (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-09-21).
Detection
Encrypted shares show as a burst of renames to the .L0CK3D extension with a read-me3.txt note created in every encrypted directory; 360 says the ransomware skips 27 system directories and encrypts each file with its own ChaCha8 key kept under RSA-2048 (360, 2026-10-29). For the September flaws, which need network access to the DSM management interface (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-09-21), file reads or writes outside a session's own storage scope, or unauthenticated requests to the SCGI and login endpoints from outside the administrative source range, are the sharpest signal (an inference from the flaw classes).
Defender takeaway
Update every DSM to the build of its branch now and take internet-facing management interfaces offline first (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-02), since Synology confirms ransomware exploitation of outdated DSM, CISA lists CVE-2024-10441 as exploited (CISA, 2026-11-18) and Synology lists no mitigation for the September flaws; treat a NAS that was reachable on an older build as possibly encrypted or compromised and check its shares for the .L0CK3D extension and read-me3.txt notes before relying on it.

entries.headline: Apache httpd mod_http2 RCE: update to 2.4.71 or drop h2/h2c; Axis OS affected, no fix; Debian, Ubuntu, Red Hat fixed
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-119618updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-119618, Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 to 2.4.70: a race in mod_http2 assign_headers() corrupts heap memory and leads to remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled; fixed in 2.4.71, Red Hat calls it unauthenticated and claims public exploit research, Axis OS version 6.50.5.10 and higher is affected with no fixed release yet, no exploitation reported

Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71, released on 2026-11-11, fixes CVE-2026-119618, a race in mod_http2's assign_headers() that the project rates critical and says can lead to remote code execution, in versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11). The project publishes no CVSS score; Red Hat scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8 and says it allows unauthenticated remote code execution, with a worker thread writing into memory owned by the connection thread through a shared lock-free allocator (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11). Red Hat states that only servers with HTTP/2 (h2 or h2c) enabled through the Protocols directive are affected and that HTTP/1.1-only servers are not (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11); the project's own page is silent on that prerequisite (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11).

On exploitation the sources differ. Wiz wrote at its publication that no exploit was available and no exploitation in the wild was reported (Wiz, 2026-11-11), while Red Hat says public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit against a default-configured server with mod_http2 enabled, without linking it (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11). A researcher has since posted a test setup that reports memory corruption and Apache child-process crashes on 2.4.70, and Wordfence says it does not demonstrate remote command execution (Wordfence, 2026-11-12). No source reports attacks, and the project's advisory carries no exploitation or workaround statement (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11).

The upstream fix is 2.4.71. The project lists standalone mod_h2 releases from GitHub, 2.0.8 through 2.0.42, as affected and names no fixed standalone release (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11). Red Hat shipped mod_http2 errata for RHEL 9 (mod_http2-2.0.26-7.el9_9.1) and RHEL 10 (mod_http2-2.0.29-5.el10_3.1) on 2026-11-11, rates them Important (Red Hat, 2026-11-11; Red Hat, 2026-11-11), says the packages allocate each HTTP/2 stream from a separate allocator, which makes exploitation substantially more complex, and lists RHEL 8 and earlier as not affected (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11); Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine and SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 ship fixed packages (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-11-15; Ubuntu, 2026-11-12; Alpine Linux, 2026-11-13; SUSE, 2026-11-13). Axis says AXIS OS version 6.50.5.10 or higher is affected and has no fixed release yet, a service release for all affected tracks being planned within the next couple of weeks, and gives a workaround that sets System.HTTP2.AllowH2 and System.HTTP2.AllowH2c to no (Axis, 2026-11-16).

Exposure
An Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 to 2.4.70, or a distribution mod_http2 build without the vendor's fix, that has the mod_http2 module loaded and h2 or h2c in a Protocols directive for the server or a virtual host; the loaded modules and the Protocols directives of the configuration show it, and the distribution advisory, not the upstream version string, shows whether a backported fix is installed; AXIS OS version 6.50.5.10 and higher is affected (Axis, 2026-11-16).
Detection
Neither the project nor Red Hat publishes indicators of compromise; the researcher's test shows the corruption as httpd child-process crashes inside the allocator and HTTP/2 stream code (researcher repository, 2026-11-12), so watch for child crashes in the error log.
Defender takeaway
Update internet-facing servers that serve HTTP/2 to 2.4.71 or the distribution's fixed package and restart, and where no fix is available yet remove h2 and h2c from Protocols until it is (Wiz advises disabling HTTP/2 temporarily, Wiz, 2026-11-11), because Red Hat describes an unauthenticated path and a public exploit while the project describes neither.
Update13 Nov 2026 03:49 UTCrun 2026-11-13T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Debian's tracker now lists apache2 2.4.71-1~deb12u1 for bookworm (DLA-4902-1) and 2.4.71-1~deb13u1 for trixie (DSA-6620-1) as fixed, with forky still vulnerable (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-11-13); Ubuntu's USN-9090-1 fixes 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, 26.04 LTS and 26.10, and 20.04 LTS through ESM (Ubuntu, 2026-11-12) and Alpine 3.21 to 3.24 ship 2.4.71-r0 (Alpine Linux, 2026-11-13), while SUSE lists the issue as pending (SUSE, 2026-11-13). A researcher's public test setup reports memory corruption and Apache child-process crashes on 2.4.70 and a clean run on 2.4.71 (researcher repository, 2026-11-12), and Wordfence says it does not demonstrate remote command execution (Wordfence, 2026-11-12); the researcher's results table records crashes inside the allocator and the HTTP/2 stream code in an instrumented build (researcher repository, 2026-11-12), and the same repository lists mod_h2 2.0.43 as the fixed standalone release.

Update15 Nov 2026 14:51 UTCrun 2026-11-15T1407Z-auditheadlinesummarycvessourcesactionsbody

SUSE released apache2 2.4.71 for SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP7 (package 2.4.71-150700.4.30.1) under SUSE-SU-2026:5231-1, rated critical (SUSE, 2026-11-13), and SUSE's CVE page now lists fixed apache2 packages for the SUSE Linux Enterprise 15 SP4 to SP6 and 12 SP5 LTSS lines and openSUSE Tumbleweed while other SUSE products are still in progress (SUSE, 2026-11-13). The scores differ by assessor: Red Hat and SUSE give CVSS 3.1 9.8 with low attack complexity, while CISA ADP gives 8.1 with high attack complexity (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11; SUSE, 2026-11-13). Debian's tracker now lists forky and sid as fixed in apache2 2.4.71-1 (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-11-15).

Update18 Nov 2026 05:13 UTCrun 2026-11-18T0356Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytitle

Axis published a security advisory on 2026-11-16 saying AXIS OS version 6.50.5.10 or higher is affected by CVE-2026-119618, which it describes as a CVSS 9.8 remote code execution flaw that would let an unauthenticated attacker gain administrator access to the device, and which it traces to the Apache HTTP Server release 2.4.71 that fixes it (Axis, 2026-11-16). Axis names no tracks and no fixed version: it is working on a service release for all affected AXIS OS tracks within the next couple of weeks, with more accurate timelines to follow, and devices outside those tracks that are still supported will be patched according to their maintenance schedule (Axis, 2026-11-16). To Axis' knowledge no exploit is public and it is not aware of exploitation in its network products (Axis, 2026-11-16).

As an immediate workaround Axis sets the device parameters System.HTTP2.AllowH2 and System.HTTP2.AllowH2c to no through param.cgi, to be reverted once an update is installed, and suggests Axis Device Manager or another configuration tool for mass deployment (Axis, 2026-11-16).

entries.headline: Oracle CSPU: 56 unauthenticated rows at CVSS 9.0+, six at 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic, BI; Brotli rows on KEV
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-114835 +17updatedNATOA2

Oracle's November 2026 Critical Security Patch Update: 56 of its 62 rows at CVSS 9.0 or above are reachable over the network without authentication, six of them at CVSS 10.0 in Access Manager, WebLogic Server, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition; Oracle flags no row as exploited, but CISA lists the Brotli flaw behind three of them

Oracle's Critical Security Patch Update of 2026-11-17 carries 655 new patches (Oracle, 2026-11-17). Its risk matrices score 62 rows at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or above, 56 of them marked remotely exploitable without authentication and without privileges (Oracle, 2026-11-17); Tenable counts 62 critical patches across 57 CVEs (Tenable, 2026-11-17). Six of them score 10.0 with changed scope: Oracle Access Manager 12.2.1.4.0 and 14.1.2.1.0 in the Admin Console (CVE-2026-114835) and twice in the Authentication Engine (CVE-2026-91500, CVE-2026-91510), WebLogic Server TopLink Integration (CVE-2026-91569), Platform Security for Java (CVE-2026-114824) and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition Platform Security (CVE-2026-114784), all over HTTP (Oracle, 2026-11-17).

WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4.0 to 15.1.1.0.0 carries further unauthenticated rows at 9.8: Core over T3 and IIOP (CVE-2026-91470) and over SOAP (CVE-2026-91456), and TopLink Integration over HTTP (CVE-2026-91570, CVE-2026-91583) and TCP (CVE-2026-91585); Oracle words the T3 and IIOP row as an easily exploitable flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker with network access compromise WebLogic Server (Oracle, 2026-11-17). E-Business Suite 12.2.3 to 12.2.15 has four unauthenticated HTTP rows at 9.8 in Attachments (CVE-2026-114880), Application Object Library (CVE-2026-114924), Applications Framework REST Services (CVE-2026-114925) and Universal Work Queue (CVE-2026-114863), and APEX and REST Data Services have two at 9.8 over HTTPS (CVE-2026-114849, CVE-2026-114850) (Oracle, 2026-11-17). Oracle's footnote says the patch for the E-Business Suite row CVE-2026-114918 also addresses CVE-2025-61882 (Oracle, 2026-11-17), which CISA lists as exploited with known ransomware use (CISA, 2026-11-17). The release also carries three unauthenticated 9.8 rows for the Brotli flaw CVE-2026-111497 in Communications Diameter Signaling Router, Communications Unified Assurance and PeopleSoft PeopleTools (Oracle, 2026-11-17), a flaw CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-27 (CISA, 2026-11-17).

Oracle's matrices carry no exploitation flag of their own, and its interim relief is blocking the network protocols an attack requires or, for attacks that need certain privileges or package access, removing those; patches exist only for versions under Premier or Extended Support, and Oracle says earlier versions are likely affected too (Oracle, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
Communications Diameter Signaling Router, Communications Unified Assurance and PeopleSoft PeopleTools instances reachable over HTTP, whose Brotli rows are the KEV-listed CVE-2026-111497 (Oracle, 2026-11-17), and Access Manager, WebLogic Server, E-Business Suite, APEX or REST Data Services, Platform Security for Java and Business Intelligence Enterprise Edition instances on the listed versions that untrusted networks can reach over HTTP, HTTPS, SOAP, TCP, T3 or IIOP (Oracle, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Patch Communications Diameter Signaling Router, Communications Unified Assurance and PeopleSoft PeopleTools first, since their Brotli rows are the KEV-listed CVE-2026-111497, then internet-reachable identity, middleware, ERP and APEX instances, and until then block the protocols a row needs, T3 and IIOP for the WebLogic Core row (Oracle, 2026-11-17). Oracle names no per-flaw workaround, so unsupported versions have no vendor fix.
Correction22 Nov 2026 14:49 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditbodyheadlinesourcing_notesummarytitleactionsaffected_products

The headline and summary said none of the unauthenticated critical rows was exploited. Three of them, in Communications Diameter Signaling Router, Communications Unified Assurance and PeopleSoft PeopleTools, are the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 at 9.8 (Oracle, 2026-11-17), which CISA has listed as exploited since 2026-10-27 (CISA, 2026-11-17). Oracle's matrices still mark no row as exploited, and no exploitation of the other rows is reported.

entries.headline: TYPO3: backend user to installer to admin and RCE (SA-027 Critical); Form Framework flaw SA-029 exploited; update now
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-119623 +9exploitedNATOA2

TYPO3 core security releases of 2026-11-17 (ten advisories): a low-privileged backend user can write a file into the web root and re-enable the unauthenticated installer, which creates an administrator and leads to code execution (SA-026, SA-027 Critical), and TYPO3 states that a Form Framework flaw (SA-029) is actively exploited; fixed in 14.3.12, 13.4.40, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS

TYPO3 released ten core advisories on 2026-11-17, fixed in 14.3.12 LTS, 13.4.40 LTS, 12.4.52 ELTS, 11.5.57 ELTS and 10.4.63 ELTS (TYPO3, 2026-11-17); versions 10.0.0 to 10.4.62, 11.0.0 to 11.5.56, 12.0.0 to 12.4.51, 13.0.0 to 13.4.39 and 14.0.0 to 14.3.11 are affected (TYPO3 SA-027, 2026-11-17). SA-027 is rated Critical: placing a file whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the public web root or the project root re-enables the installer on a configured instance without authentication, which allows changing the database connection and creating a new administrator and system maintainer account, and that leads to remote code execution; leftover or restored marker files also work (TYPO3 SA-027, 2026-11-17). SA-026, rated High, supplies the file: the backend endpoint for adding online media accepts a target folder in the fallback storage, which points to the public web root, so any authenticated low-privileged backend user can create media files with a partially controllable name there (TYPO3 SA-026, 2026-11-17).

TYPO3 states that SA-029, a Medium information disclosure in the Form Framework, is known to be actively exploited, and names no actor, victim or behaviour (TYPO3 SA-029, 2026-11-17). A failed upload shows the raw storage error with the upload sub-folder, so an attacker can derive the public URL of an uploaded file, and where the form accepts HTML this becomes cross-site scripting unless the web server applies TYPO3's recommended Content-Security-Policy to the upload folder (TYPO3 SA-029, 2026-11-17). SA-032 closes the matching gap, an empty allowedMimeTypes list that was treated as no restriction and let unauthenticated visitors upload HTML or SVG to a public folder (TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17). SA-028 lets ImageMagick's MVG coder disclose any web-server-readable file through a processed image; it needs ImageMagick with its default configuration allowing the MVG coder, and unauthenticated visitors reach it where such an upload form exists (TYPO3 SA-028, 2026-11-17). SA-025 is an Import/Export path traversal that writes arbitrary files and needs an administrator or a user enabled for import (TYPO3 SA-025, 2026-11-17). Four lesser flaws are an incomplete open-redirect fix (SA-030), page-cache flooding where cHash validation is not enforced (SA-031), file-dump token reuse (SA-033) and an SSRF in the 14.x Dashboard RSS widget (SA-034) (TYPO3 SA-030, 2026-11-17; SA-031; SA-033; SA-034).

Exposure
Any TYPO3 instance on an affected version; the installer chain needs only a low-privileged backend account, and the Form Framework flaws need a public form with an upload element (TYPO3 SA-026, 2026-11-17; TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17).
Detection
Files whose name starts with FIRST_INSTALL in the web root or project root, and administrator or system maintainer accounts nobody created (TYPO3 SA-027, 2026-11-17); HTML or SVG files in the form upload folder and web-server logs for direct requests to them (TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17).
Defender takeaway
Update to the fixed release of each branch now. After updating, configure at least one allowed MIME type for every upload element, because an empty list now refuses uploads (TYPO3 SA-032, 2026-11-17); on 14.x configure the dashboard_rss allowed hosts, because the update alone does not mitigate SA-034 (TYPO3 SA-034, 2026-11-17); and deliver the form upload folder with a restrictive Content-Security-Policy, which nginx needs configured by hand (TYPO3 SA-029, 2026-11-17); and, after updating, configure image formats outside the default raster set, such as psd or ppm, explicitly in fileExtensionToMimeType so ImageMagick still processes them (TYPO3 SA-028, 2026-11-17).

NOTABLENATOA2

Barracuda's own account of a 44-hour intrusion into its cloud: a key given to an AI vendor and never retired, found in that vendor's compromised development environment, led an intruder across about ten cloud accounts to Kubernetes; notified Managed XDR customers must recreate their integration credentials

Barracuda says the attacker did not break in but used a valid cloud access key that Barracuda had issued to a third-party vendor, a company working in AI, for an earlier project and had not retired when the work ended (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). The key had been stored in a configuration file in the vendor's GitHub repository, which was exposed when the vendor's development environment was compromised (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). The first call with the key came on 2026-11-01 at 04:33 UTC; within minutes the attacker was mapping what the key reached and reading stored secrets such as AWS access keys and Azure service principal secrets, and each secret opened the next system, from cloud accounts to a data analytics system, to a source-code access token and on to Kubernetes clusters (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). In just under four hours on 2026-11-02 it pushed short-lived branches to a handful of repositories to trigger a build workflow written to print the build system's secrets into the job log, encoded so that log masking would not hide them, and its last recorded activity was at 23:31 UTC, about 10 cloud accounts and 44 hours after the start (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11).

In a Kubernetes cluster the attacker deployed a container that mounted the underlying server's file system read-only, enough to harvest that server's credentials, and tried to create a new administrative cloud identity, which was blocked (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). On servers where it had a shell, its commands searched for environment variables named WALLET, MNEMONIC, SEED and PRIV, Ethereum keystore files, extended private keys, seed phrase files and Kubernetes secrets with wallet-related names, and Barracuda calls the activity consistent with a financially motivated actor seeking cryptocurrency and reusable credentials (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). Barracuda says the resource names, the sequence of activity and the credential and wallet hunting routines match ARTEX, which many groups use, so the match shows how the attacker operated, not who it was (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11).

Exposure
A system the attacker reached stores the credentials Barracuda Managed XDR uses to collect data from customers' connected systems such as Microsoft 365, Google Workspace and endpoint security platforms; only organisations using the API integration for Managed XDR Cloud or Monitored Endpoint are affected, and Barracuda notified those with potentially affected credentials (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). Logging in that environment was not detailed enough to rule out access to the credentials (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11). Relevant as a supplier incident for any organisation whose monitoring runs on Managed XDR, and as a worked example of ARTEX-style cloud tradecraft.
Detection
In cloud control-plane audit logs, a long-lived key used by a non-vendor address, secret-store reads followed by use of those secrets in other accounts, resources named with the letter i followed by digits and no hyphen, short-lived branches in a handful of repositories that trigger a workflow, and container deployments that mount the node's file system (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13; Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11).
Defender takeaway
A notified customer revokes and recreates its integration credentials and reviews connected-system activity since 2026-11-01 (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13). Barracuda's own lesson is to remove standing credentials, especially long-lived keys held by third parties (Barracuda Blog, 2026-11-11), and to expire vendor credentials when an engagement ends (Barracuda Trust Center, 2026-11-13).

Builds on: FBI: various actors run ARTEX against many sectors, government included; Microsoft now names… · Entra app-credential abuse: agents hunt GitHub for secrets, an operator reaches MSP clients… · WorkOS breach agent was a researcher's ARTEX test that escaped its sandbox; legacy API, dev… · ARTEX in AWS: CloudWatch log searches for secrets, Cognito self-sign-up for credentials; hunt…

entries.headline: Mandiant: COLD RELIC turns one cloud compromise into the pretext for the next; enrolled passkeys outlive password resets
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

COLD RELIC: Mandiant shows the FSB-linked group reusing data stolen from one US organisation as the impersonation pretext for the next, then holding cloud tenants through MFA push fatigue and enrolled passkeys, backup codes and MFA devices that survive password and session resets

Mandiant reports a series of linked intrusions in which COLD RELIC, the name Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) now uses for the group formerly tracked as COLDRIVER and UNC4057 (also Star Blizzard, Callisto and Gossamer Bear), turned data stolen in one US organisation into the pretext for the next (GTIG, 2026-11-17). GTIG cites a US Department of Justice assessment that the group operates within Russia's FSB and names government officials, defense contractors and NGOs in Europe and North America among its targets (GTIG, 2026-11-17). In 2026 the operators approached a second US organisation over an encrypted messaging app while impersonating an employee of the first, shared phishing links that stole Entra ID credentials and tokens and sent the victim on to document lures matching the conversation, and registered a new MFA device on the account (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

In the late-2025 case the operators used the stolen credentials of a Super Admin account from a US residential proxy network close to the victim, pressed the user with MFA push notifications until one was accepted, registered a device model new to the tenant and kept access with passkeys, MFA backup codes and rogue MFA devices (GTIG, 2026-11-17). They took the whole cloud drive by mass sharing to an operator-run mailbox and by direct download, queried the admin investigation and email audit logs to check defensive visibility, viewed, modified and deleted Alert Center notifications, exported the employee list and ran a tenant-wide Customer Takeout export (GTIG, 2026-11-17). Access lasted several months through OAuth mail sync to an external client and re-authentication with enrolled passkeys that survived password and session resets, and in one case a password reset without revoking sessions did not evict the operators (GTIG, 2026-11-17). They searched for credentials, personnel data and .pst archives (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

Exposure
Google Workspace tenants, and Entra ID tenants that federate sign-in to Workspace as in the second case, whose privileged or staff accounts accept push, SMS or voice MFA or let users enrol passkeys, backup codes and devices without a second approval (GTIG, 2026-11-17).
Detection
In authentication logs, repeated failed logins or MFA challenges followed by a success from the same address, privileged sign-ins from residential-proxy networks that geolocate near the user, logins with a backup code, and new passkey or device registrations. In administrator audit logs, Customer Takeout creation, user-list downloads, audit-log investigation queries and Alert Center batch deletions. In Drive and OAuth logs, download spikes, external sharing to free mail providers, and authorisations of broad mail scopes to unapproved clients such as Thunderbird or Proton (GTIG, 2026-11-17). After a compromise, password changes alone are insufficient: revoke all sessions, refresh tokens and third-party OAuth permissions and remove unauthorised passkeys, backup codes and MFA devices (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

Triage: a directory export, a Customer Takeout or a passkey or device enrolment by an administrator can be routine; the cues in GTIG's account are an unfamiliar device, a non-corporate or residential-proxy network, or an enrolment right after an MFA-fatigue pattern (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

Defender takeaway
Move administrators and exposed staff to FIDO2 or WebAuthn hardware keys, which GTIG says cannot be approved through fatigue or intercepted by reverse proxies, require existing-administrator or out-of-band approval for new MFA devices and passkeys, and write session and OAuth revocation into compromise playbooks (GTIG, 2026-11-17).

entries.headline: Craft CMS unauthenticated SQL injection gives admin takeover; CCCS reports exploitation; update to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-123488exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-123488, Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1: an unauthenticated SQL injection in front-end search lets a visitor become an administrator on MySQL and MariaDB; the Canadian Cyber Centre reports exploitation in the wild and 4.18.9 and 5.11.2 fix it (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

Craft CMS 4.0.0 before 4.18.9 and 5.0.0 before 5.11.2 contain an unauthenticated SQL injection in front-end search: the attribute parameter is concatenated into the query unsanitized and emulated PDO prepares allow stacked statements, so a remote attacker can read and write the database, setting the admin flag or overwriting password hashes in the users table to gain administrator access (CVSS 4.0 9.3) (VulnCheck, 2026-11-06). Craft's own advisory, published on 2026-10-22 as critical, places the flaw on the front end of any site that uses craft.search, says it affects only MySQL and MariaDB, and says the write primitive was used to set the admin flag on user ID 1 (Craft CMS, 2026-10-22). The fixed releases are 4.18.9 and 5.11.2, and Craft's temporary workaround is to block front-end requests that carry the bracketed attribute token, plain or encoded, in the query string (Craft CMS, 2026-10-22). ENISA's record for CVE-2026-123488 lists Craft's advisory among its references (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-06).

On exploitation, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security's update of 2026-11-12 says open source reporting indicates the flaw is exploited in the wild (CCCS, 2026-11-12), and VulnCheck's advisory page states that it is in the VulnCheck KEV database (VulnCheck, 2026-11-06). No first-hand telemetry, victim statement or CISA listing was found.

Exposure
Craft CMS 4.0.0 to 4.18.8 and 5.0.0 to 5.11.1 on MySQL or MariaDB whose public pages use craft.search.
Detection
Web access logs for front-end search requests whose query string carries the bracketed attribute token that Craft's workaround blocks; database audit for changes to the admin column or password hashes in the users table, and new administrator accounts or sessions afterwards. Updating closes the injection but not an administrator flag or hash that was already written.
Defender takeaway
Update every Craft CMS site to the fixed release now, since the attack needs no account and ends in administrator access, and check the users table on any internet-facing site that ran an older build.

entries.action_label: BundID: mass automated logins lock citizen…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: BundID: mass automated logins lock citizen accounts; BSI confirms; password sign-in now needs an e-mail code
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOB2

BundID: automated mass login attempts against Germany's federal citizen accounts lock accounts; the BSI confirms the attack, password sign-in was switched off on 16 November and returned that afternoon behind an e-mail security code, and no compromise is evidenced

Germany's BSI confirmed to heise security and Handelsblatt on 2026-11-16 an IT security incident involving BundID accounts: automated, mass login attempts whose failures locked accounts, triggered automated mails and prompted account holders to reset their passwords (heise, 2026-11-16). The federal government switched off username-and-password sign-in on Monday morning for security reasons (Handelsblatt, 2026-11-16), while sign-in with the online ID card (eID) and the Elster certificate stayed possible (WEB.DE, 2026-11-16). The BSI says countermeasures it does not name repelled the attack and that it has no indication of a compromise of any account, and heise reports that locked accounts are apparently not being unlocked in bulk, so account holders must pass the password-reset flow or use another sign-in method (heise, 2026-11-16). Handelsblatt, citing government circles, describes the attack as credential stuffing, the automated replay of credentials from earlier leaks at other services (Handelsblatt, 2026-11-16). That afternoon the BundID site notice said two-factor authentication had been switched on for all accounts, with a security code by e-mail at every sign-in by username and password (Spiegel, 2026-11-16). An aggregator attributes the credential-stuffing label to the BSI, which neither heise nor Handelsblatt does (ad-hoc-news.de, 2026-11-16).

Exposure
Citizen-facing or employee-facing login portals that accept a password and lock an account after repeated failures.
Detection
Authentication logs showing a surge of failed password sign-ins spread over many usernames and sources, followed by lockout notices, password-reset mail volume and helpdesk contacts; a lockout storm is itself the alert.
Defender takeaway
The operator's containment was to switch off the password-only path while eID and other sign-in means stayed open, as heise and Handelsblatt report it, and to bring it back the same day only with an e-mail security code (Spiegel, 2026-11-16); a lockout-after-failures control turns credential stuffing into mass lockouts and reset mail even when no account is taken over, so settle that containment lever for your own portals before a run starts.
Improvement22 Nov 2026 14:53 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditbodyheadlinesourcessummarytitlesourcing_note

The same-day return of password sign-in now rests on the operator's own notice: on the afternoon of 2026-11-16 the BundID site said two-factor authentication had been switched on for all accounts, so every sign-in with username and password now needs a security code sent by e-mail, while sign-in with the online ID card and the Elster certificate stayed available (Spiegel, 2026-11-16).

entries.headline: GTIG quarterly: exploit_agent automates n-day exploitation, suspected DPRK cluster abuses .claude/settings.json
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

GTIG AI Threat Tracker, November 2026: an exposed exploit_agent framework automates patch diffing, exploit drafting and execution without a human, a suspected North Korean cluster plants a Claude Code startup download in internal repositories, and PRC-nexus actors stage and exfiltrate through an LLM platform's file hosting

Three findings from GTIG's quarterly update on adversary use of AI, published 2026-11-16, change what defenders can look for (GTIG, 2026-11-16). First, GTIG identified an exposed staging server hosting a multi-agent vulnerability research and weaponization framework, dubbed exploit_agent, that integrates frontier and local LLMs and runs continuous differential analysis of popular web application software: it compares code before and after patch announcements, analyzes the findings, drafts exploits and executes them automatically, which GTIG says is the first time it has seen LLM frameworks fully automate discovery and exploitation without a human in the loop (GTIG, 2026-11-16). The server also held scripts for internal reconnaissance, brute-forcing, installing web shells and removing other attackers' web shells, and its victim telemetry suggested interest in French media, entertainment and education websites (GTIG, 2026-11-16).

Second, in intrusions against cryptocurrency organizations in North America and Europe, a suspected MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE cluster used fraudulent recruiter profiles, sent targets to fake meeting platforms with ClickFix lures that ran likely LLM-authored staging scripts, and then pivoted into internal code repositories and modified .claude/settings.json so that Claude Code startup triggered the download of the SOMBERMEME backdoor; it masked lateral movement with GitHub personal access tokens named after Microsoft Copilot (GTIG, 2026-11-16). Third, in what GTIG calls a new trend, PRC-nexus actors abused LLM platforms and file-hosting backends for staging, dead-drop command channels and exfiltration, in one case staging lure archives and exfiltrating stolen data through a frontier model's file-hosting infrastructure (GTIG, 2026-11-16). GTIG separately assesses that the open-source agentic pentest frameworks it tracks, among them ARTEX, CAIRN, CyberStrikeAI and PentAGI, currently trade stealth for velocity: they generate forensic traffic, rely on recognizable identifiers and leave distinct code-level traces (GTIG, 2026-11-16).

Exposure
Organizations whose developers run Claude Code against shared repositories, where a committed project settings file executes at startup, and internet-facing web applications and plugins whose patches are public, since exploit_agent works from patch diffs.
Detection
Repository change monitoring for edits to .claude/settings.json and its hook or startup commands, and GitHub audit events that create personal access tokens named after a vendor assistant; for agentic scanning, the forensic traffic, recognizable identifiers and code-level traces that GTIG says pentest frameworks leave behind (GTIG, 2026-11-16).
Defender takeaway
Review a change to a project-level Claude Code settings file like a code-execution change, and move internet-facing web components to the fastest patch lane, because GTIG describes patch diffs being turned into executed exploits without a human.

It also reports a suspected MIDNIGHT NEPTUNE (North Korea) cluster that modified .claude/settings.json in victims' internal repositories so that Claude Code downloads the SOMBERMEME backdoor at startup, and PRC-nexus actors using an LLM platform's file-hosting backend for staging and exfiltration.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Unit 42: TGR-STA-0049 uses QUIC C2, logon-script spread and Exchange FullAccess loops against governments
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

TGR-STA-0049: Unit 42 describes the PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT implants, which use HTTP/3 over QUIC for command and control against government networks entered through unpatched Exchange servers, then spread through domain logon scripts and grant FullAccess on every mailbox

Unit 42 describes a campaign by TGR-STA-0049, also tracked as REF7707, Earth Alux and Ink Dragon, against Southeast Asian government entities since at least July 2025, and says the group's targeting also includes government organizations in South America and Europe (Unit 42, 2026-11-16). Server exploitation is the primary entry: unpatched Microsoft Exchange and web servers receive web shells, among them variants of ASPXSpy, Godzilla, Bysunue.aspx and Suo5, while phishing with decoy PDFs from lookalike government domains is secondary (Unit 42, 2026-11-16). The implants are two previously undocumented families: the Go-based PerfectPioneer RAT, active since July 2025 and run through DLL side-loading of a modified legitimate executable, decoy installers or phishing, and its modular C++ successor KUKURAT, deployed since March 2026, which loads at least 12 DLL modules from the command server into memory (Unit 42, 2026-11-16). Unit 42 says both families use HTTP/3 over QUIC as the primary command channel, with an automatic HTTP/2 fallback in the PerfectPioneer variant it analyzes, separate HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 builds of KUKURAT, and two PerfectPioneer variants, RatAAkk-tt and PerfectRat, that rely on HTTP/2 alone, and that some firewalls and inspection engines handle QUIC less well than TCP traffic (Unit 42, 2026-11-16). Two of the six PerfectPioneer variants, Pioneer and rat_http3_cc, carry a built-in blocklist that stops operators running noisy or destructive commands, and KUKURAT generates synthetic network, registry and file activity as camouflage (Unit 42, 2026-11-16).

After taking a domain controller, the operators installed malicious domain logon scripts, so each user's logon pulled KUKURAT; they also used PsExec, WMI and WinRM (Unit 42, 2026-11-16). Credentials came from LSASS dumps taken with rundll32 calling comsvcs.dll by ordinal rather than by the MiniDump name, from DCSync, and from Mimikatz, ProcDump, SharpDPAPI and SAM and SYSTEM hive dumps (Unit 42, 2026-11-16). On Exchange, the operators first listed accounts holding the ApplicationImpersonation role and, when none was found, ran a hidden PowerShell loop that granted a compromised account FullAccess on every mailbox (Unit 42, 2026-11-16). The exfiltration targeted pdf, docx, xlsx and png files whose names suggest international relations and internal political affairs (Unit 42, 2026-11-16).

Exposure
On-premises Exchange and other web servers that are unpatched and internet-facing, and Active Directory domains in which an attacker with domain controller access can edit logon scripts in SYSVOL or Group Policy.
Detection
Egress telemetry for outbound UDP 443 (QUIC) from servers that do not browse, since Unit 42 advises logging or blocking it so traffic falls back to TCP, paired with proxy and TLS egress telemetry because the HTTP/2-only variants and the KUKURAT HTTP/2 build never use UDP 443; SYSVOL and Group Policy change audit plus endpoint alerts on an uncommon startup process running under a domain user SID at logon, which raised an alert in Unit 42's telemetry; process events for rundll32 loading comsvcs.dll with an ordinal argument; and Exchange audit of ApplicationImpersonation role holders and of Add-MailboxPermission loops that grant FullAccess across all mailboxes (Unit 42, 2026-11-16).
Defender takeaway
Patch or isolate internet-facing Exchange and web servers first, then check domain logon scripts, ApplicationImpersonation holders and mailbox permissions, and decide whether servers need outbound UDP 443 at all.

Its new PerfectPioneer and KUKURAT implants use HTTP/3 over QUIC as the main command channel in most variants, the operators spread KUKURAT through domain logon scripts after taking a domain controller, and on Exchange they grant a compromised account FullAccess on every mailbox.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Symantec: AI-assisted retailer intrusion pivots through SolarWinds Orion's bundled RabbitMQ Erlang cookie
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Symantec: a September 2026 intrusion at a US retailer shows attackers switching to AI-generated PowerShell and, about ten minutes after first querying SolarWinds Orion, using the RabbitMQ Erlang cookie bundled with it to run a command on a second server

Symantec's Threat Hunter Team describes a September 2026 intrusion at a US retail organization in which the attackers first worked by hand on a compromised web server, with typing errors and every staged payload terminated by security software, and then, the next day, submitted about 50 long, error-free PowerShell scripts over roughly two hours, with labelled output sections and comments that read as a model's reasoning (Symantec, 2026-11-12). Symantec assesses AI assistance with high confidence and an operator relaying output to an AI tool, not an autonomous agent, with moderate confidence; it could not identify the model (Symantec, 2026-11-12). The initial infection vector is unknown (Symantec, 2026-11-12).

The earliest activity, on 2026-09-18, ran cmd.exe directly under sqlservr.exe on three SQL Servers, which Symantec reads as commands issued through the database service, most likely xp_cmdshell; on one host the attackers compiled the public EfsPotato exploit with csc.exe from base64 text decoded by certutil and saved the SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY hives (Symantec, 2026-11-12). On a web server compromised through w3wp.exe they side-loaded malicious DLLs with a legitimate Bitdefender executable and a G DATA executable placed in ProgramData, used a utility called BreakChain to relaunch them so they no longer appeared as children of w3wp.exe, copied one to a file named w3wp.exe, and planted ASP web shells in the application's images folder (Symantec, 2026-11-12). The AI-style scripts then harvested credentials from connection strings, FileZilla, WinSCP and PuTTY settings, saved RDP files and IIS configuration, read the Erlang cookie file of the RabbitMQ broker that ships with Orion; running Orion's bundled erl.exe with that cookie, they called the broker on a second web server to run an encoded operating system command (Symantec, 2026-11-12). Later activity searched a probable domain controller for NTDS.dit, SYSVOL cpassword values and LAPS passwords and ran a Chisel tunnelling tool and a password sprayer (Symantec, 2026-11-12).

Symantec says no second-phase technique was new and suggests a possible link, through a shared address and the retail focus, to the operation Gambit Security described on 2026-09-22 (Symantec, 2026-11-12). No Swiss or public-sector victim is named; the case matters for the transferable chain and its AI-assisted tempo.

Exposure
Windows estates running SolarWinds Orion with its bundled RabbitMQ broker alongside SQL Server hosts and IIS web applications; the Erlang cookie file on the Orion host is the pivot.
Detection
Process-creation telemetry with parent lineage for cmd.exe or PowerShell started under sqlservr.exe or w3wp.exe, csc.exe started by PowerShell on a server, certutil decoding a text file in ProgramData, a vendor-signed security executable running from ProgramData and loading a DLL beside it, an executable named w3wp.exe outside the IIS directory, and erl.exe started from the Orion directory with a cookie argument and a remote broker call; registry hive save events for SAM, SYSTEM and SECURITY.

Triage: long, labelled PowerShell is not the signal on its own, because administrators write such scripts too; a parent of sqlservr.exe or w3wp.exe rather than an administrator session, credential-store targets and a blocked loader returning rebuilt are.

Defender takeaway
Hunt SQL Server and IIS hosts for this lineage, treat an Orion server as a lateral-movement bridge to every host that runs its RabbitMQ node, and alert on behavior rather than file names, since the tools were renamed and rebuilt after each block.

entries.headline: ScreenConnect clients before 26.6.5 run guest-pushed files unprompted; Huntress confirms exploitation against MSPs
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-84869exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-84869, ConnectWise ScreenConnect: a missing file-transfer authorization check lets an active remote session push and auto-run files on the Host (CVSS 9.9); Huntress confirms exploitation against MSP technicians since October 2026

ConnectWise's own disclosure describes a client-side condition in ScreenConnect Support and Access sessions where file-transfer actions could be processed through an active remote session "without proper authorization or Host confirmation," letting files be transferred to and executed on the Host system, including through elevated execution paths (ConnectWise, 2026-09-08). ScreenConnect servers are not affected, only client versions before 26.6.5, the release that fixes CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9).

Starting 20 August 2026, before ConnectWise's disclosure, Huntress's SOC found rogue ScreenConnect clients deployed via social engineering (a fake tech-support Quick Assist session in one case, a phishing-driven MSI in another) that immediately spawned four chained VBScript stagers via wscript.exe. The stagers profile the host (existing ScreenConnect install, installed security-product names, available RAM to rule out a sandbox), then pull an AES-encrypted payload bundle keyed to that profile from Dropbox. Depending on the profile, the final PowerShell stage installs a ScreenConnect backdoor client concealed as a hidden Windows service (its registry Uninstall entry removed and a restrictive service security descriptor applied), builds a UAC-bypass helper via a hijacked ms-settings: protocol handler routed through ComputerDefaults.exe, sets AmsiUtils.amsiInitFailed = true to blind AMSI, adds all of C:\Users as a Defender exclusion, and disables Defender reporting, notifications and Hypervisor-Protected Code Integrity; the package also drops a vulnerable WinRing0 kernel driver alongside the payload (Huntress, 2026-09-03).

The installed backdoor client gives the infection a worm-like spread: it continuously inspects ScreenConnect's own connection-status collection for newly established Host sessions and, on each new connection, packages the same four VBScript stagers into a ScreenConnect file-transfer message flagged to auto-run, so connecting to an infected client can make the server-side Host system receive and run the same chain, independent of the original social-engineering vector (Huntress, 2026-09-03). That matches the unauthorized file transfer ConnectWise later patched, but Huntress's post notes the patch without tying the August incidents to CVE-2026-84869 (Huntress, 2026-09-03). No named threat-actor cluster is attributed by any source; CISA added the CVE to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-09-11 (CISA KEV, catalogue version 2026.09.11).

Exposure
Every ScreenConnect host client and Access agent before 26.6.5, whatever the server version, because the vulnerable code runs on the technician's machine; the server's connection history records which client version each technician used (Huntress, 2026-11-16).
Detection
On the server, guest-originated file-run events (RanFiles, SentFiles) in App_Data\Session.db that overlap an open host connection; on technician workstations, the ScreenConnect client starting cmd, PowerShell or script hosts from its Temp folder, msiexec unpacking an MSI into a user-profile folder, and outbound relay connections to domains you do not own, often on port 8041 (Huntress, 2026-11-16). A client that ran such a file needs a compromise check, because patching does not remove a rogue client that is already installed.
Defender takeaway
Any MSP-managed or self-hosted ScreenConnect deployment, including the IT-service-provider chain that reaches public-sector customers, should patch to 26.6.5 immediately and treat every pre-patch client as a potential re-infection vector, not just the host that was originally targeted. Triage: a benign ScreenConnect file-transfer message is initiated by a human technician against a session they are actively working; the worm's signature is a file-transfer action auto-queued the moment a new Host connection appears, with no corresponding operator action, immediately followed by wscript.exe spawning multiple child .vbs processes.
Update17 Nov 2026 04:35 UTCrun 2026-11-17T0355Z-intelentitiessourcesevidenceactionsbodytitletechniques

Huntress confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians in a campaign it separates from the crypto-exchange-named decoy sessions it reported on 2026-11-13, and it describes the SCKit malware as appearing to leverage a vulnerable server-side extension, not to exploit this flaw directly (Huntress, 2026-11-16). On 2026-11-12 a technician at one MSP joined a blank-named Access session on the MSP's server and the host client ran a batch file the guest had pushed, with no prompt; within about nine seconds a hidden PowerShell relaunch, a curl download and an administrative-image unpack of an MSI ended with a rebranded ScreenConnect client connected to an attacker relay on port 8041 (Huntress, 2026-11-16). Huntress read the delivery side from server databases: between 2026-10-20 and 2026-11-16 attacker guests made 688,000 run-file requests for update.bat-style files from 29 source addresses on 42 MSP servers, repeating them in case a technician joined, and Huntress assesses with high confidence that the spray operator and the relay operator are the same (Huntress, 2026-11-16). In October an attacker also joined three real customer support sessions as an extra guest and asked the technician's client to run a path-traversal file into the Startup folder; two of the three technicians were on vulnerable Windows clients and the Mac client failed (Huntress, 2026-11-16).

The vulnerable code runs on the technician's machine, so updating the server alone does not close it, and Huntress saw many technicians on 22.x, 24.2 and 25.8 clients weeks after 26.6.5 shipped (Huntress, 2026-11-16). Server-side, Huntress points to guest-originated file-run events (RanFiles, EventType 85, or SentFiles, 86) in App_Data\Session.db, read from a copy, that overlap an open host connection; on workstations it points to the ScreenConnect client running batch or script files from its Temp folder, and to any client whose command line names a relay the organisation does not own (Huntress, 2026-11-16).

Correction22 Nov 2026 14:50 UTCrun 2026-11-22T1407Z-auditactionsbodyheadlinesummarytitle

The entry said Huntress traced exploitation of CVE-2026-84869 back to 20 August. Huntress's post on the August incidents describes rogue ScreenConnect clients that push their infection chain to every Host that connects to them, and its 8 September update notes ConnectWise's patch without tying those incidents to the CVE (Huntress, 2026-09-03); the exploitation Huntress confirms runs from October (Huntress, 2026-11-16). The entry also had the spread running from an infected client to the hosts it connects to; Huntress describes the Host side of a session with an infected client receiving and running the chain.

entries.summary: CVE-2026-84869 (CVSS 9.9) lets file-transfer actions inside an already-active ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote session run without the authorization or Host-confirmation step the product is meant to require; ConnectWise fixed it in 26.6.5 on 8 September. Huntress has confirmed exploitation against MSP technicians since October 2026, with attacker guests spraying run-file requests across 42 MSP servers. Earlier, from 20 August, Huntress saw rogue ScreenConnect clients that push their infection chain as an auto-run file transfer on every new connection, behaviour that matches the flaw, though Huntress does not tie those incidents to the CVE.
entries.title: CVE-2026-84869, ConnectWise ScreenConnect: a missing file-transfer authorization check lets an active remote session push and auto-run files on the Host (CVSS 9.9); Huntress confirms exploitation against MSP technicians since October 2026

updates.summary: Huntress confirmed exploitation of CVE-2026-84869 against MSP technicians: on 2026-11-12 a guest-pushed batch file ran on a technician's client with no prompt and installed a rogue ScreenConnect client within about nine seconds, while attacker guests were making 688,000 run-file requests on 42 MSP servers between 2026-10-20 and 2026-11-16. Updating the server does not fix it; every technician host client must be on 26.6.5 or later.

Huntress does not tie its 20 August rogue-client incidents to CVE-2026-84869; the exploitation of the flaw it confirms runs from October 2026. The worm-like spread runs from an infected client to every Host that joins a session with it, not the other way round.
