entries.headline: Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-111497exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

Node.js shipped security releases on 2026-10-21 for CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder it bundles: an invalid block switch was reported as a need for more input instead of a format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input to an eight-byte internal buffer (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory or remote code execution (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). Imperva ran code carried in Brotli data against the official 24.22.0 image in its laboratory (Imperva, 2026-10-22).

CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 "based on evidence of active exploitation" (CISA, 2026-10-27). ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, although the chain got no shell against ELLIO's own copy (ELLIO, 2026-10-26). Cisco and Palo Alto say they know of no malicious use against their own products (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28).

Fixes are in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1; end-of-life lines stay affected (Node.js project, 2026-10-21; ELLIO, 2026-10-26). The decoder is Google's, so Bun (fixed in 1.4.4), Istio, the PyPI packages Brotli (fixed in 1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy and Microsoft .NET carry the flaw too (ELLIO, 2026-10-26; Tenable, 2026-10-26; OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-23; Envoy, 2026-10-23; .NET Blog, 2026-10-25).

Exposure
A service on Node.js 22.x, 24.x or 26.x below the fixed releases that decodes Brotli from an untrusted party, either request bodies inflated by Express 5 or body-parser 2 or compressed responses that fetch() consumes from a server an attacker influences (Imperva, 2026-10-22); Python code that decompresses untrusted data with the PyPI packages (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-23); Envoy with the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23); .NET applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager, critical on 9.1.1 with no patch yet (Broadcom, 2026-10-28); PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls that inspect Brotli traffic with TLS decryption enabled (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29); Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and the Visual Exporter app in every Splunk Enterprise version, and Citrix Unicon eLux Scout (Splunk, 2026-10-28; Citrix, 2026-10-30); and WordPress hosts through the xmlrpc.php pingback and the operating system's libbrotli, where Patchstack shows a worker crash only (Patchstack, 2026-10-30). Read the Node.js release number, not process.versions.brotli, which says 1.2.0 on patched and vulnerable builds alike (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).
Detection
In web server, proxy and WAF logs, requests that carry a Brotli content encoding to endpoints that parse bodies, followed by worker crashes or restarts. A shell or new outbound connection from that workload is the strongest signal, and payload signatures, WAF content matching and body-size limits do not catch it (Datadog, 2026-10-29). Where systemd-coredump is enabled, forced crashes write core files that can hold other visitors' session cookies and key material, so restrict who can read them (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).
Defender takeaway
Replace the runtime, the two Python packages and any Envoy with the decompressor configured now, as CISA lists the flaw as exploited, and move Splunk Enterprise 10.0 to 10.2 or higher and disable its Visual Exporter app (Splunk, 2026-10-28); where an update has to wait, reject Content-Encoding: br as NCSC Switzerland advises (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26) and, if the application accepts no compressed request bodies, set the body-parser inflate option to false (Akamai, 2026-10-26).
Update26 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-26T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidencesourcessummary

Two more vendors have shipped fixes for the same decoder flaw. Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 says a buffer overflow in its Brotli decompressor allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code with a crafted Brotli-compressed stream; it names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable, v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 as fixed, and limits the impact to deployments that have the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23). Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3) fixes the same CVE, and an application is exposed only when it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data through ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic decompression or the Brotli APIs (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); .NET Blog, 2026-10-25 lists the fixed releases. As of 2026-10-26 no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration against Node.js.

Update27 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessummarytags

NCSC Switzerland (BACS) published advisory 13105 on 2026-10-26 on the Brotli decoder flaw: it names Node.js, Microsoft .NET, Visual Studio, PowerShell, the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages and Bun among the affected dependents, rated the exploitation status unknown with a proof of concept available in its text of that day, and gives as the temporary measure disabling Brotli decoding of untrusted data and rejecting Content-Encoding: br until patched, with services restarted and containers rebuilt after updating (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26).

Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS 12.2 before 12.2.4-h1, 12.1 before 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.7-h11 and 12.1.10-h3, and 11.2 before 11.2.4-h23, 11.2.7-h23, 11.2.10-h17, 11.2.13-h4 and 11.2.16-h1 as affected, but only on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls that have inspection of Brotli-compressed traffic and TLS decryption enabled on the dataplane; PAN-OS 11.1 and 10.2 and the management interface are not affected, and the hotfixes carry estimated dates from 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26). Brotli encoding is disabled by default in PAN-OS 11.2.4 and later, the command show system setting brotli shows whether a firewall is exposed (Enabled: yes), and set system setting brotli-encoding disable is the vendor's interim mitigation; Palo Alto rates the urgency moderate and is not aware of malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26).

PHP rebuilt its Windows packages as 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 on 2026-10-26 with Brotli 1.2.1; the vulnerable decoder is reachable there through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled, which cURL leaves off by default (PHP, 2026-10-26). Ubuntu lists brotli fixes for 26.10 (1.2.0-4ubuntu0.1), 26.04 LTS (1.2.0-3ubuntu0.1), 24.04 LTS (1.1.0-2ubuntu0.1) and 22.04 LTS (1.0.9-2ubuntu0.1), marks 20.04 LTS as needing evaluation and its nodejs package on 20.04, which vendors Brotli, as vulnerable (Ubuntu, 2026-10-26).

Update28 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryprioritytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyaffected_productsentities

CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 "based on evidence of active exploitation", naming no actor or victim (CISA, 2026-10-27). ELLIO's sensors recorded a public checker that maps hosts decompressing Brotli and then, on 2026-10-26, one Brotli-coded request body of about 23 MB built against Node.js 24.22.0 on x86-64, which ELLIO reads as adoption by an operator focused on mass exploitation; its own test of the attacker's chain against that build got no shell in 50 attempts, so a failed attempt shows as a worker crash (ELLIO, 2026-10-26). Tenable relays the report and has not confirmed it (Tenable, 2026-10-26); Cisco and Palo Alto report no malicious use against their own products (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28). Palo Alto's advisory, as read on 2026-10-28, shows six of the nine PAN-OS hotfixes released and the other three, 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.10-h3 and 11.2.4-h23, due on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

JFrog reproduced a remote crash of a ClickHouse server with one request carrying a crafted 23 MB body, with the fix merged but not released when it wrote (JFrog, 2026-10-25). Akamai gives a lever for Express 5 and body-parser 2 services that accept no compressed request bodies: set the inflate option to false (Akamai, 2026-10-26). A Node.js build is judged by its release version, because the bundled version string reads 1.2.0 on patched builds as well (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).

Update29 Oct 2026 07:03 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-intelsummaryupdated_atentitiesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceactionsbody

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0008, issued on 2026-10-27 and revised as 0008.1 on 2026-10-28 to clarify the impacted products, lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager as affected because it uses Node.js: a malicious actor with network access to SDDC Manager may exploit the flaw to execute arbitrary code (Broadcom, 2026-10-28). Broadcom rates it critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8, on SDDC Manager 9.1.1 only and important, 7.5, on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, none has a patch yet, and workarounds are in KB460732 for 9.1.1 and KB460734 for the others (Broadcom, 2026-10-28).

Palo Alto Networks' timeline of 2026-10-29 removes the estimated dates of 11.2.4-h23, 12.1.4-h13 and 12.1.10-h3 because those builds are released, so every PAN-OS hotfix listed for this flaw is now available (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

Correction01 Nov 2026 13:56 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditaffected_productsbodycvessources

The 2026-10-26 section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory held only for that day: CISA listed the flaw as exploited on 2026-10-27, and NCSC Switzerland's advisory, updated on 2026-10-29, now gives the status as actively exploited with a proof of concept available (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26). ELLIO's capture is not the only attack telemetry: Zscaler's decoys recorded 402 events from 20 source addresses against 12 customers within a day of disclosure, 60% of them exploitation attempts and the rest reconnaissance (Zscaler ThreatLabz, 2026-10-28).

Datadog, which reproduced the bug, finds no conventional indicators because no attacker infrastructure is involved and lays out three layers to correlate (Datadog, 2026-10-29): decoder errors, where a vulnerable Node.js build returns Z_BUF_ERROR "unexpected end of file" (which benign truncated input also produces) and a patched one ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH; process signals, a worker exiting with signal 139 right after a Brotli transfer or pinned at full CPU inside a decompression call; and decompressed output carrying bytes the client never sent, the memory-disclosure path, so endpoints that echo or reflect decompressed content are the ones to check first. Payload byte signatures, WAF content matching and body-size limits do not catch it, because the WAF forwards compressed bytes and the middleware counts decompressed size (Datadog, 2026-10-29). Palo Alto's advisory also lists Prisma Cloud Application Security Transporter Client before 0.2.9 as affected, fixed in 0.2.9 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

Update03 Nov 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-intelsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Patchstack reports that WordPress ships no Brotli of its own but links the operating system's libbrotli through libcurl, so one unauthenticated POST to xmlrpc.php can take down a PHP worker on a stock install: the pingback method makes WordPress fetch an attacker-named URL and decode the Brotli reply (Patchstack, 2026-10-30). A laboratory demonstration killed a worker or pinned it at full CPU, its author says no code execution is included, and Patchstack says no public chain aims at PHP; the fix is a patched libbrotli package, and the official wordpress:latest image still carried a vulnerable one when Patchstack wrote (Patchstack, 2026-10-30).

Update05 Nov 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-intelsummaryaffected_productsentitiescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Splunk's advisory SVD-2026-1015, published on 2026-10-28 and updated through 2026-11-06, lists Splunk Enterprise, the Splunk Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA, Attack Analyzer, Python for Scientific Computing, several AppDynamics components and Smartlook as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them; the page gives no CVSS score, no attacker position and no exploitation statement, and it covers the Brotli flaw and three DNS and TLS hostname-validation flaws together, so it does not show which of them reaches a given product (Splunk, 2026-10-28). Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable while 9.4 and 10.2 or later are not (as revised on 2026-11-06), Splunk recommends upgrading to 10.2 or higher for the bundled Node.js runtime and plans to upgrade the packages in a future 10.0 release, and the upgrade does not remediate the Visual Exporter app, which every Splunk Enterprise version includes and which Splunk says to disable or remove (Splunk, 2026-10-28). The page gives no fix for the other listed products.

Citrix bulletin CTX697300, published on 2026-10-30 and revised on 2026-11-03 with remediation for the LTSR and Cloud Gateway products, lists Unicon eLux Scout as affected by CVE-2026-111497 alone and names the fixes as hotfix 2609.1 for Scout On-Prem, 2508 CU2 LTSR for Scout On-Prem LTSR and 2605.1-3 for Scout Cloud Gateway On-Prem, without a vulnerable version range or an exploitation statement (Citrix, 2026-10-30). Neither Splunk nor Citrix says anything on malicious use against its products.

Correction08 Nov 2026 13:53 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditactionsbodycvesevidencesourcing_notesummaryaffected_productssources

Splunk revised advisory SVD-2026-1015 on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06: Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable, versions 9.4 and 10.2 and higher are not affected, and 10.2 or higher stays the upgrade target for 10.0 (Splunk, 2026-10-28). A 9.4 instance therefore needs no upgrade for the bundled Node.js runtime; the Visual Exporter app is still included in every Splunk Enterprise version and is still to be disabled or removed (Splunk, 2026-10-28). The revised list adds Splunk Observability Cloud and the Splunk Observability OpenTelemetry Collector as affected and names Splunk Synthetic Runner 1.71.0 or higher as its fix (Splunk, 2026-10-28). Keycloak 26.8.2, released on 2026-11-05, fixes the flaw in its bundled Brotli decoder (Keycloak, 2026-11-05). The 27 October update's statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory was already outdated when written: ELLIO had reported exploit traffic in the wild on 26 October (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).

entries.summary: CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available, and Splunk lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 (not 9.4, and not 10.2 or later) among the products that include affected Node.js packages, with 10.2 or later as the upgrade target and its Visual Exporter app, present in every version, to be disabled.
entries.title: CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

updates.summary: Envoy and Microsoft have shipped fixes for the same Brotli decoder flaw: Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 lists v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 for deployments with the Brotli decompressor configured, and Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14) covers applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

NCSC Switzerland rates exploitation of the Brotli flaw unknown with a proof of concept available and names rejecting Content-Encoding: br as the interim measure; Palo Alto lists PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls that inspect Brotli traffic with TLS decryption enabled (hotfixes due by 2026-10-30), and PHP for Windows and Ubuntu shipped fixes. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26; JFrog shows the decoder reachable beyond HTTP and Cisco and Palo Alto report no malicious use against their products. The entry's earlier statement that no source reports exploitation is replaced, the priority moves from notable to high. Palo Alto's advisory, as read on 2026-10-28, shows six of its nine PAN-OS hotfixes released and three due on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30.

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0008.1 lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager as affected, critical (CVSS 3.1 9.8) on 9.1.1 and important (7.5) on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, with the patch pending and workarounds only; the SDDC Manager workaround is added to the actions. Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 records the last three PAN-OS hotfixes (11.2.4-h23, 12.1.4-h13 and 12.1.10-h3) as released, so the PAN-OS action no longer says they are due. Removed from the main text: ELLIO's reading of the attacker as a mass-exploitation operator and its count of 50 attempts (the 2026-10-28 section still carries them). The Ubuntu 20.04 entry in the CVE record now shows the ESM fix.

An earlier section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside the laboratory is dated to the day it held; NCSC Switzerland now rates the flaw actively exploited, and Zscaler's first-day decoy telemetry joins ELLIO's. Datadog's detection layers (decoder errors, worker crashes, leaked decompressed output) and what does not catch the attack are added, as is Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud Transporter Client.

Patchstack reports that default WordPress installs reach the Brotli decoder without authentication through the xmlrpc.php pingback and the operating system's libbrotli, shown to crash a worker but not to execute code; WordPress hosts need a patched libbrotli package, which the official WordPress image did not yet carry.

Splunk's advisory lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and lower, its Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA and Attack Analyzer as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them, with Splunk Enterprise 10.2 or higher as the upgrade target and the Visual Exporter app to be disabled, and Citrix names Unicon eLux Scout with hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR and 2605.1-3 as the fixes.

Splunk narrowed advisory SVD-2026-1015 on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06: only Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable, 9.4 and 10.2 or later are not, so the upgrade applies to 10.0 instances alone while the Visual Exporter app is still to be disabled on every version. The revision adds Splunk Observability components and a Synthetic Runner fix, Keycloak 26.8.2 fixes the flaw in its bundled Brotli decoder, and the 27 October statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory was outdated, since ELLIO had reported exploit traffic on 26 October.

entries.action_label: Bitdefender: a 3AM affiliate joined a school…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Bitdefender: a 3AM affiliate joined a school estate's AD domains with new trusts after stealing Veeam credentials
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

3AM ransomware affiliate in a UK school estate: Bitdefender documents backup-credential theft, rogue domain admins and new two-way trusts between Active Directory domains, with a command-retry pattern it reads as a model-driven loop

Bitdefender MDR attributes the intrusion to a 3AM (ThreeAM) ransomware affiliate on the encryptor build and its command-line pattern; the target was a school estate in the UK whose domains began as separate Active Directory environments, and initial access is unknown (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). In September 2026 the attacker first took credentials from the backup software: a modified copy of a public script read the credentials stored in Veeam's databases on three backup servers and decrypted them with the Windows Data Protection API, and a browser credential database was copied from a terminal server (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). It then worked with built-in tools (PowerShell, WMI, reg, netsh, rundll32) and a few public ones (an Impacket-like remote-execution tool that returns output over administrative shares, Mimikatz renamed to look like a monitoring binary), enumerated domain trusts from a domain controller, searched SYSVOL logon scripts for the names and subnets of other schools, created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three separate domains with two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents, which anti-tampering controls blocked, deleted system-state backups and encrypted machines with a Rust-based encryptor (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Bitdefender's reading, which it calls interpretation and not a finding, is that a model drove part of the work: commands call the Veeam web interface on a port and with a login method that do not match the vendor documentation, output is self-labelled, scripts carry numbered revisions, and retries arrive 40 to 101 seconds apart whatever the size of the change, while a new task takes minutes. Every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host with no agent, so the automation itself was never seen, and Bitdefender says it could not document anything about a language model (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
A Windows estate that runs Veeam Backup & Replication and has several Active Directory domains or a flat network that an unmanaged internal host can reach; the unmanaged host is the gap, because it ran no agent and sat outside Bitdefender's visibility.
Detection
In directory-service change events, new trust relationships between domains, which Bitdefender calls a rare change that is cheap to alert on, and new domain-administrator group members; in backup-server logs, Veeam web-interface calls and credential-store reads from hosts that are not backup administrators'; in endpoint telemetry, saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM registry hives by any process that is not a known backup or administration job, LSASS access, a Windows Defender exclusion for the temporary directory, and the same command re-issued with small edits at a steady cadence; across hosts, file contents staged into registry values, which Bitdefender calls an unusual channel and a strong indicator to hunt for, and sent out by HTTP POST to an internal host, and probe or confirmation artifacts such as a scheduled task named for the probe left on production hosts; in authentication logs, unmanaged hosts authenticating to domain controllers (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).
Defender takeaway
Alert on any new domain trust and on additions to the domain-administrator groups, alert on credential-reading access to backup-software databases and on saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM hives outside known backup or administration jobs, put an endpoint agent on every machine because the staging host here was unmanaged, and limit remote execution and administrative shares to known management hosts (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Initial access is unknown, every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host, and Bitdefender reads the 40 to 101 second retry cadence as a model-driven loop, flagged as its own interpretation; it says a new trust between domains is a rare change that is cheap to alert on.

entries.action_label: Binance's report: fake recruiter, trojaned pyenv…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Binance's report: fake recruiter, trojaned pyenv, AI-tool pivot and a deployment token reached the signing service
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Binance's own report on the 2026-10-29 theft of about USD 6.34 billion: a fake recruiter's coding assignment compromised an engineer's laptop, an internal AI tool carried the attacker to two colleagues and a container-deployment token, and a deployed container reached the wallet signing service; the FBI attributes it to North Korea's TraderTraitor

Binance says the theft of about USD 6.34 billion in digital assets on 2026-10-29 was "a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign" and not a single breach or a simple phishing incident (Binance, 2026-11-03). In September 2026 a software engineer whose job-platform profile named Binance was approached by a person posing as a project director, interviewed by a purported HR representative on live video and then by a purported CEO in a chat application, and told to download an "assignment" repository onto his work computer; its setup code replaced the legitimate pyenv executable in the Homebrew installation with a malicious version, repointed the symlink and spawned a zsh shell, and the 0-day malware was not detected by endpoint protection (Binance, 2026-11-03). On 2026-10-20 the attacker used that computer and an internal AI tool to gain control over a wallet DevOps engineer and a second wallet software engineer, and found a container-deployment permission token on the first engineer's computer; on 2026-10-29 it logged onto the second engineer's computer with the stolen credentials, deployed a container and triggered a script that launched the attack on the wallet signing service (Binance, 2026-11-03). Binance reports an earlier supply-chain event in June 2026, when a wallet DevOps engineer installed a tampered Homebrew installation while searching for an AI coding tool, and says its security team blocked 57 suspected North Korea-linked cases in 2026 (Binance, 2026-11-03). The FBI says North Korea was responsible and calls the activity "TraderTraitor" (FBI, 2026-10-31). BleepingComputer notes that fake job interviews leading to malware installs are a common tactic of the North Korean campaigns known as Contagious Interview and Operation Dream Job, a comparison Binance does not make (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-03).

The transfer to other organisations is the access chain, not the loss: a developer endpoint reached through a recruiting lure, a trojaned version-manager binary that endpoint protection missed, an internal AI tool through which the attacker gained control over two colleagues, by a method Binance keeps confidential, and a deployment token that turned one workstation into code execution in a trusted pipeline.

Exposure
Any organisation whose developers, DevOps or administrators can be approached through job platforms and run third-party assignment code on managed laptops, and any internal AI assistant or agent reachable from a compromised employee endpoint.
Detection
In endpoint file-event telemetry, a version-manager or interpreter binary deleted, renamed and re-linked inside a package-manager directory followed by a shell spawned from it, which is the sequence Binance describes for pyenv in the Homebrew installation (Binance, 2026-11-03); in process lineage, shells started from a repository's setup scripts; in token-use logs, a container-deployment token used from a host that is not its owner's; in the access logs of internal AI tools, activity that touches other employees' accounts or endpoints from one user's session, a pattern the takeover of two colleagues through such a tool implies (an inference; Binance does not describe the mechanism).
Defender takeaway
Treat a recruiter's "assignment" repository as untrusted code and keep it off managed machines, restrict what an internal AI tool can reach with one user's session and what a stored deployment token can deploy, and alert on shells spawned from replaced developer-tool binaries; Binance's own stated fixes are tighter device controls, rebuilt systems and tools, rotated credentials and tokens, and AI-based behavioural anomaly detection (Binance, 2026-11-03).
Correction08 Nov 2026 14:05 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditbody

Binance's report says the attacker "used an internal AI tool to gain control over" two further engineers and that some technical details will remain confidential (Binance, 2026-11-03); it does not say how the tool was abused, so the earlier description of it letting one user act on colleagues' machines went beyond the source. The access-log pattern for internal AI tools is an inference from that takeover, not a mechanism Binance describes.

actions: On every Linux server that ran cPGuard on 2026-11-02, update to the latest version (the disclosure names 5.88.26 as the clean update), confirm that the hidden root shell and the scheduled task the fake update left are gone, then reset root and local passwords from a trusted environment and rotate the root SSH keys, the MySQL root password, any cloud storage keys and every secret in root's shell history; rebuild from a clean backup taken before 1 November any server the vendor tells you the attacker logged in to by hand.

entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: cPGuard update channel pushed a fake root update to about 2,950 servers on 2 Nov; update, then rotate root secrets
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

OPSSHIELD cPGuard: an attacker who registered as a customer reached the vendor's billing and licensing server and shipped a fake update on 2026-11-02 that ran as root on about 2,950 Linux servers, copying root secrets and leaving a root shell and a scheduled task

OPSSHIELD says the attacker registered a customer account under a false identity on the vendor's billing portal, studied how the cPGuard agent talks to the licensing system with a trial install, sent crafted requests to the portal's callback pages, gained the ability to run commands on the billing and licensing server, took the keys used to publish updates and shipped a fake update for about 70 minutes on 2026-11-02; the vendor's logs do not record the exact request that gave access (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). cPGuard agents installed the fake update between 02:08 and 03:20 UTC, and it ran as root (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The script copied the local password hashes, root's SSH private keys and authorization files, the MySQL root password and root's shell history back to the attacker, and root's cloud storage keys on a small number of servers; it also left a hidden root shell and a scheduled task (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The vendor puts the affected servers at about 2,950 and the exposed billing-portal accounts, with name, company, postal address, e-mail and hashed password, at about 7,900 (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). A clean update, 5.88.26, removes the hidden root shell and a follow-up update removes the scheduled task (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), but credentials copied before cleanup may still be usable (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The shared exposure is every operator of a cPGuard server: BleepingComputer says hosting firms and server administrators commonly run it alongside panels such as cPanel, DirectAdmin and Plesk (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
Any Linux server on which cPGuard was installed and online between 02:08 and 03:20 UTC on 2026-11-02; the vendor's earlier advisory framed the exposure as an install of versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 shown by "Successfully updated" entries in the product's install log, which proves installation and not that the script ran (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), and the later disclosure narrows the fake update to 02:08 to 03:20 UTC without repeating a version range or withdrawing that check (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). Holders of a billing-portal account are exposed separately.
Detection
In the install log, the affected version entries of 2026-11-02; on the host, the hidden root shell and the scheduled task the update left, which the vendor says to confirm are gone after updating; in authentication logs, root logins and use of the copied SSH keys from new sources after 2026-11-02, on this server and on every server that trusted its keys; in egress logs, the update script's collection and outbound copy of root's files.
Defender takeaway
Treat any server that ran the fake update as compromised for credential purposes even after the update: reset root and all local passwords, from a trusted environment as the earlier advisory says (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), create new root SSH keys and remove the old public keys from every server that trusted them, change the MySQL root password and any database passwords it holds, rotate every secret in root's shell history and any cloud storage keys, and treat servers reached with those keys as exposed; rebuild from a clean backup taken before 1 November any server the vendor says the attacker logged in to by hand, and reset the billing-portal password with two-factor login (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03).

entries.headline: Canton Vaud: school IT-support platform breached, data of about 3,500 teachers and 38,000 pupils copied; pupil arrested
entries.html:
ROUTINEupdatedNATOA2

Canton Vaud: unauthorised access to the IT-support platform of its Gymnases and professional schools copied the names, school e-mail addresses and support requests of about 3,500 teachers and 38,000 pupils; police arrested a 16-year-old pupil of the schools on 2026-10-31

The Swiss canton of Vaud says unauthorised access, detected on 2026-10-26, to the IT-support platform of its Gymnases and professional schools copied the names, school e-mail addresses and support requests of about 3,500 teachers and 38,000 pupils; passwords are not stored on the platform and no grades or pupil files are affected (Etat de Vaud, 2026-10-31). The canton names targeted fraudulent messages that pose as the school or IT support as the main risk (Etat de Vaud, 2026-10-31); it gives no access method, actor or platform product. Vaud police announced on 2026-11-03 the arrest, on 2026-10-31, of a 16-year-old pupil of the affected schools, suspected of the intrusion between 23 and 26 October; he was questioned and released, his equipment was seized, and the juvenile court's investigation aims to establish how the intrusion happened and whether data were downloaded or passed to third parties (Le Temps, 2026-11-03, translated from French; Inside IT, 2026-11-03).

Defender takeaway
The sources give no access method, so there is no patch or configuration change to prescribe; school and cantonal IT teams should brief users to expect impersonation of IT support and to report urgent or unusual messages, as the canton advises (Etat de Vaud, 2026-10-31).

Vaud's cantonal police announced on 2026-11-03 that a 16-year-old was arrested on Saturday 2026-10-31, suspected of intruding into the IT-support platform of the canton's post-compulsory schools and extracting data from it between 23 and 26 October 2026 (translated from French) (Le Temps, 2026-11-03). The education directorate says the suspect is one of its pupils and faces an administrative sanction, up to exclusion, that runs apart from the criminal case; he was questioned and released, his IT equipment was seized and is being analysed, and the investigation, led by the juvenile court, aims to establish the circumstances of the intrusion and whether data were downloaded or passed to third parties (Le Temps, 2026-11-03; Inside IT, 2026-11-03). The platform was disconnected from the internet on detection and then secured with the support of the canton's security operations centre, according to the police communiqué; the access method and the platform product are still not stated (Le Temps, 2026-11-03).

Improvement08 Nov 2026 14:09 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditsourcessourcing_note

The police communiqué, published on vd.ch, says the platform was disconnected from the internet as soon as the access was detected and then secured with the support of the canton of Vaud's operational security centre, that a criminal complaint was filed, and that the suspect was identified quickly and released after questioning; the cyber investigation division of the criminal police leads the inquiry under the juvenile court (translated from French) (Etat de Vaud, 2026-11-03). entries.action_label: Berlin confirms extortion after a phishing click…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Berlin confirms extortion after a phishing click reaches the shared state network; media reports name Rhysida
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Berlin's state government confirms an extortion attempt after a phishing click opens the shared Landesnetz; media reporting names Rhysida

Germany's Berlin state administration is the target of a live extortion attempt following a compromise of its Landesnetz, the shared network serving every Senate department and state agency; Der Tagesspiegel and rbb24 both independently date the two affected departments' disconnection from the network, as a containment measure, to 2026-08-14 (translated from German) (Der Tagesspiegel, 2026-08-28; rbb24, 2026-08-29); Berliner Zeitung independently dates the attack becoming publicly known to the same day, stating the departments were disconnected shortly after the incident became known without giving a separate explicit date for the disconnection itself (translated from German) (Berliner Zeitung, 2026-08-28). Contradiction: Security Affairs instead states "Berlin first disclosed the compromise on August 17, isolating" the same two departments, dating both the public disclosure and the network isolation itself three days later than the German-language reporting (Security Affairs, 2026-08-29). The 2026-08-14 date is the better-corroborated account, though the discrepancy is not resolved. Investigative reporting, not an official technical disclosure, is the first to name a mechanism: the attackers apparently gained access to the Landesnetz through an employee's click on a phishing email (translated from German) (Der Tagesspiegel, 2026-08-28). Forensic investigators found the actual data exfiltration ran between 2026-08-07 and 2026-08-12 (Security Affairs, 2026-08-29), several days before the two affected departments were disconnected.

Der Spiegel reported, citing security sources, that the ransomware group Rhysida is behind the attack (heise online, 2026-08-29), an attribution Berlin's Senate administration has declined to confirm, citing investigative-tactical reasons (heise online, 2026-08-29). Rhysida's own dark-web leak site independently posted an entry titled "Berlin, Germany" on 2026-08-28 claiming 5.79 terabytes of data across roughly 1.44 million files, including personal data on 12,076 individuals, more than 5,000 personnel files, plaintext credentials for internal systems, disciplinary and court records, Bundesrat committee protocols, and vulnerability analyses concerning Berlin's water supply (Security Affairs, 2026-08-29). Rhysida demanded 30 Bitcoin, about EUR 2 million (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-08-29), with a one-week ultimatum running from 2026-08-28 (translated from German) (Der Tagesspiegel, 2026-08-28); Berlin's Governing Mayor Kai Wegner and Interior Senator Iris Spranger jointly confirmed the extortion attempt and publicly refused to pay, stating the state of Berlin will not submit to extortion (Security Affairs, 2026-08-29). Whether the affected systems were also encrypted, not only exfiltrated, is disputed: one outlet attributes to unnamed "experts" the claim that the Rhysida ransomware was the tool used to both encrypt the systems and steal the data (translated from German) (BornCity, 2026-08-29), while every other cited source describes only data theft and extortion without confirming encryption, so encryption is not asserted.

CrowdStrike is conducting a forensic investigation across every Senate department and state agency network-wide, an effort Tagesspiegel's sources expect to take several more days (Der Tagesspiegel, 2026-08-28). The department networks disconnected on 2026-08-14 were reconnected on 2026-08-23, but staff report continuing operational degradation days later, with many now working over private internet connections because the corporate network remains impaired; the same reporting flags that workaround as a new, self-inflicted security exposure (Der Tagesspiegel, 2026-08-28). Per the joint CISA/FBI/Multi-State ISAC advisory on the group, current as of its 2025-04-30 update, its initial-access techniques include compromising internal VPN access points using valid credentials at organizations lacking multi-factor authentication, and separately deploying Gootloader malware (CISA, 2025-04-30).

Defender takeaway
The exposure pattern here, a single employee's phishing click reaching a shared administrative network broad enough to threaten a different department's critical-infrastructure and judiciary holdings, is directly transferable to any DACH shared-network government architecture, including Swiss cantonal and federal administrative networks: segment administrative domains so that one credential or endpoint compromise cannot reach unrelated departments' sensitive holdings, and verify that phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication and out-of-band verification cover every remote-access and VPN path that Rhysida's documented playbook targets.

Triage: the reported mechanism, a user's click on a phishing email followed by multi-day bulk data exfiltration, surfaces at the point of delivery in mail-flow logs and, in egress and data-loss-prevention telemetry, as a sustained high-volume outbound transfer from one department's network segment; BSI's advisory adds that, where applicable, TerminalFix operators may stage exfiltration into attacker-controlled cloud storage, for example Azure, with the provider's own transfer tool (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04), but BSI does not confirm to rbb24 that the Berlin attack followed that pattern (rbb24, 2026-10-21), so no process-level discriminator is offered here.

Update05 Sep 2026 04:50 UTCrun 2026-09-05T0409Z-intelupdated_atsourcesevidencebody

Rhysida's one-week ultimatum expired on 2026-09-04 at roughly 15:35 local time; the Berlin Senate had publicly committed not to pay, and about an hour after the deadline the group published the full stolen dataset on its darknet leak site, replacing the prior partial "auction" listing (heise online, 2026-09-04). Chaos Computer Club spokesperson Joachim Selzer confirmed the complete dataset (including personnel files and documents Selzer describes seeing directly, such as employment references) is now publicly accessible to anyone. Whether the dataset actually contains the drinking-water vulnerability analyses and administration credentials the group had earlier claimed remains unverified by any party this entry cites: Left-party parliamentary faction leader Tobias Schulze stated the Senate now has the opportunity to check whether the prior assumptions about the leaked data are accurate, and should notify affected individuals and organizations as quickly as possible once it does. No further technical root-cause detail beyond the phishing vector has been disclosed by the Senate.

Update06 Sep 2026 04:50 UTCrun 2026-09-06T0409Z-intelupdated_atsourcesevidencebody

A structural consequence of this incident has now surfaced at the federal level. Asked in a Bundestag inquiry whether, given ongoing severe attacks on states and municipalities, the government would bring forward a constitutional amendment planned earlier by the previous coalition to make the BSI a true central authority for cyber incidents, the Federal Interior Ministry pointed only to the existing constitutional framework (heise online, 2026-09-03). Under that framework, the BSI may assist a state in defending against a serious cyberattack only after that state explicitly requests administrative assistance, and durable bilateral cooperation agreements still gate faster support, which heise notes do not yet exist with all 16 federal states while the ministry points to the 14 that do; in practice the BSI has repeatedly had to help first and formalise the legal basis afterward (heise online, 2026-09-03). The ministry points instead to its 14 existing cooperation agreements, its NIS2-transposition-driven expansion of BSI's powers, and increased staffing and budget as sufficient. Green-faction deputy chair Konstantin von Notz, who filed the inquiry, called the reversal "devastating for Germany's IT security" (translated from German) given the still-unfolding fallout from this exact incident. The tension is directly transferable to any federated cyber-incident-response model, including Switzerland's own federal/cantonal/communal cooperation structure with BACS: a central technical authority's ability to help is gated by a request-and-agreement process rather than by its own capacity to act.

Separately, on the incident itself, the Chaos Computer Club's Joachim Selzer identified specific record types now visible in the fully-published leak beyond the personnel-and-employment-reference material already recorded here: an internal request form for a new mobile phone bearing the requesting employee's handwritten signature, which Selzer noted gives a criminal a usable signature sample (heise online, 2026-09-04).

Update07 Sep 2026 04:47 UTCrun 2026-09-07T0411Z-intelupdated_atsourcesevidencebody

Follow-up reporting establishes for the first time that the scope of the published leak extends well beyond the personal data first identified. Citing Der Tagesspiegel, heise reports the dataset also includes information on district-heating and power plants, fuel depots, backup-power installations, electrical substations, prisons, waterworks, and armaments companies and the Bundeswehr (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-09-06), a materially broader critical-infrastructure and defense-industrial exposure than the water-supply-vulnerability material Rhysida itself had claimed at disclosure.

Germany's BSI issued a public warning on 2026-09-05 of an elevated threat level stemming from the leak. The agency states data containing information on critical infrastructure, companies and organizations can, depending on its sensitivity, also increase the threat level (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-09-05), and separately warns of heightened targeted-phishing risk against anyone who had contact with affected individuals or institutions (heise online, 2026-09-05). BSI additionally flags a hack-and-leak risk specific to the political calendar: Berlin holds a state-parliament election on 20 September 2026, and stolen documents can be released or recontextualized at a moment favorable to an attacker (heise online, 2026-09-05). BSI assesses the underlying intrusion itself as financially rather than politically motivated (heise online, 2026-09-05), an assessment attributed to BSI, distinct from opposition politicians' own separately reported alarm about the incident's severity.

Berlin's government responded on 2026-09-06 by establishing a dedicated coordination unit ("Steuerungseinheit") in which BSI, the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) and the domestic intelligence service (BfV) jointly review and assess the leaked material, and by starting a risk-based notification process to contact affected citizens, employees and companies by letter or email (heise online, 2026-09-06). Independent IT-security expert Manuel Atug separately stated that the state of Berlin acted grossly negligently and deliberately failed to comply with classified-information protection requirements (translated from German), adding that he had already flagged the same security gaps to Berlin's parliamentary interior committee in 2023 and 2025 (heise online, 2026-09-06). Contradiction: the heise 2026-09-06 timeline separately dates full network reconnection to 2026-08-24, one day later than the 2026-08-23 date this entry's main analysis attributes to Der Tagesspiegel; both dates are carried without resolving the one-day gap.

The same 2026-09-06 report adds a fourth account of the date sequence: its own retrospective timeline states the two affected Senate departments were isolated from the Landesnetz on 2026-08-14 (matching Der Tagesspiegel and Berliner Zeitung's dating of the isolation, not Security Affairs' 2026-08-17) and separately states the Senate chancellery's public press statement disclosing the "ICT incident" followed on 2026-08-17 (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-09-06). This distinguishes network isolation (2026-08-14, now three independent accounts) from the Senate's own formal press disclosure (2026-08-17) as two separate events, but Security Affairs' claim that the isolation itself happened on 2026-08-17 remains an unresolved discrepancy with the German-language reporting, not one this update can settle.

Update08 Sep 2026 04:49 UTCrun 2026-09-08T0411Z-intelupdated_atentitiestechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_noteconfidenceclassificationbody

Germany's BSI published an advisory on 2026-09-04 describing the compromise of an anonymized "state institution" whose technique matches the multi-stage TerminalFix campaign Microsoft documented on 2026-08-28, the advisory itself never names Berlin (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04). The same day, BSI posted on its official Mastodon account that it was intensively involved in handling the Berlin incident and separately linked to its detailed TerminalFix security notice (BSI on Mastodon, 2026-09-04); heise reports that juxtaposition as confirmation that TerminalFix is specifically the attack vector the Rhysida operators used against Berlin's two affected Senate administrations (heise online, citing BSI, 2026-09-07), the first technical confirmation, reported by heise, of both the access vector and the attribution this entry had previously carried only from investigative journalism. BSI attributes the Rhysida ransomware and leak site to a financially motivated group it tracks as Vice Spider, cross-referenced against the aliases Vice Society, WhiteNefas, White Hekate, DEV-0832 and Vanilla Tempest, active since at least mid-2021 and using the Rhysida ransomware and leak site almost exclusively since June 2023 (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04). BSI's advisory adds a detail beyond what Microsoft's original write-up described: where applicable, TerminalFix operators stage exfiltration into attacker-controlled cloud storage, for example Azure, using the cloud provider's own transfer tooling such as azcopy (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04). BSI further states that incident reports place a malware family it names LoremIpsumLoader (also known as AxolotLoader) within the campaign, and attributes that loader to the same group responsible for Rhysida (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04). BSI assesses the campaign as opportunistic, purely financially motivated cybercrime with no established link to a state or politically motivated actor, and states Rhysida shows no particular regional focus on Germany, concentrating instead on education and healthcare, with public administration a more distant top-five target sector (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04).

Update10 Sep 2026 05:05 UTCrun 2026-09-10T0410Z-intelsourcesevidencebody

CDU defense-policy spokesperson Roderich Kiesewetter told Süddeutsche Zeitung "this data leak is of grave scope and endangers our national security" (translated from German) and that total-defense plans circulating on the darknet weigh very heavily, while heise reports that the published dataset includes civil-defense emergency and protection plans and barracks documents alongside the critical-infrastructure material already recorded here; Germany's Bundeswehr Operative Führungskommando and the Nationales Cyberabwehrzentrum have joined BSI in reviewing the security fallout (heise online, citing Süddeutsche Zeitung, 2026-09-07). Separately, the Berlin district of Lichtenberg has refused to deploy CrowdStrike's Falcon Agent on its own servers: "in an internal letter, he cites concerns, according to rbb, about near-unlimited data access, possible disruption to specialised administrative applications, and remaining monitoring risks for staff" (translated from German), while the district states it has found no evidence of intrusion on its own systems and is demanding the Senate assume full responsibility and cost for the response (heise online, citing rbb24, 2026-09-07). Berlin's data protection commissioner Meike Kamp has now issued concrete guidance for potentially affected individuals: "change passwords, closely monitor account activity, and increased scepticism toward phishing emails" (translated from German) (heise online, citing Meike Kamp, 2026-09-07).

Defender takeaway
The Lichtenberg dispute is a transferable governance lesson for any DACH federated administration, Swiss cantonal/communal architecture included; an incident-response tool that needs broad endpoint data access can itself become a point of inter-departmental conflict when trust in central IT governance is already damaged, so decide the incident-response tooling and data-access model before an incident forces the question under public pressure.
Update02 Nov 2026 03:47 UTCrun 2026-11-02T0256Z-intelsourcing_notesourcesevidencebodypriorityconfidenceclassification

rbb24 Recherche reported on 2026-10-21 that the attack-detection system introduced in 2026 had licences for only five percent of all devices, according to the Senate department for urban development, which also said that extending it to every device was not possible "for financial reasons"; rbb's research shows that neither the endpoint identified as the criminals' entry point nor the servers from which data later flowed were covered by it (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). Both departments also said that in 2024 the funds needed for IT security were available only in part to the extent required, although the state's information-security guideline has obliged agencies since 2017 to provide enough staff and money (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). The stolen data includes a copy of the transport senator's identity card and of her digital signature and, rbb's analysis shows, further identity-card copies and personal documents of employees; the mobility department confirmed to rbb that the data is mostly unstructured files from shared and personal directories (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21).

BSI told rbb that it had warned repeatedly since at least March 2025 of fake security prompts that make users run a malicious command themselves, publicly and in daily situation reports that also went to representatives of the federal states, and that it described the TerminalFix variant in September 2026; it does not confirm to rbb that the Berlin attack followed that pattern, saying only that it is in close contact with Berlin and supporting the response (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). BSI's advisory of 2026-09-04 does not name Berlin (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04), so the link between TerminalFix and this incident rests on BSI's Mastodon post, which heise reads as confirmation (heise online, 2026-09-07), and not on a BSI statement to rbb that the Berlin attack followed that pattern. rbb describes the chain for such warnings: the Berlin-CERT run by the IT service centre ITDZ passes relevant reports to each agency's information-security officers, and each agency is itself responsible for acting on them; the ITDZ and the Senate Chancellery did not say whether BSI's warnings reached the two departments or what followed (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21).

Defender takeaway
The transferable gap is licence coverage, not the absence of a tool. Compare the endpoints and servers that actually run the detection agent, file servers holding shared and personal directories first, with the estate, and settle who in a federated administration is accountable for acting on a national-CERT warning, because in Berlin's chain the ITDZ and the Senate Chancellery left open whether the warnings reached the two departments.
Correction08 Nov 2026 14:04 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditbody

Kiesewetter's quoted assessment to Süddeutsche Zeitung is that the leak is of grave scope, endangers national security and that total-defense plans circulating on the darknet weigh very heavily; the list of leaked material, civil-defense emergency and protection plans and barracks documents among it, is heise's own reporting (heise online, citing Süddeutsche Zeitung, 2026-09-07). It is heise that says bilateral BSI cooperation agreements do not yet exist with all 16 federal states; the Federal Interior Ministry points to the 14 agreements that already exist (heise online, 2026-09-03).

updates.summary: Rhysida's ultimatum lapsed on 2026-09-04 after Berlin's Senate refused to pay; the group then published the full stolen dataset on its darknet leak site, replacing its prior partial "auction" listing. Chaos Computer Club spokesperson Joachim Selzer confirmed the complete dataset is now publicly accessible to anyone, but whether it actually contains the drinking-water vulnerability analyses and administration credentials the group had earlier claimed remains what the Senate itself must still verify, per a state-parliament faction leader's own account.

Germany's federal government has quietly abandoned a plan set by the previous coalition to amend the Basic Law so the BSI could act as a true central authority for state- and municipal-level cyber incidents, per the Interior Ministry's own written Bundestag reply: a structural gap in federated cyber-incident response the fallout from this exact incident has now surfaced. Separately, the Chaos Computer Club identifies specific exposed record types (personnel matters, employment references, a handwritten signature on an internal device-request form) in the now fully-published leak.

Follow-up reporting establishes for the first time that the published leak extends well beyond personnel data: it includes records tied to district heating and power plants, fuel depots, backup-power installations, electrical substations, prisons and defense-industrial / Bundeswehr-related material. Germany's BSI issued a public warning of an elevated threat level from the leak (heightened targeted-phishing risk plus a hack-and-leak risk given Berlin's 20 September state election) while assessing the underlying intrusion itself as financially motivated. Berlin's government set up a dedicated coordination unit (BSI, BKA and the domestic intelligence service BfV jointly reviewing the material) and started a risk-based notification process for affected citizens, employees and companies.

Germany's BSI officially confirms, for the first time, both the intrusion technique and the actor attribution this entry had previously carried only from investigative journalism: the compromise matches BSI's own TerminalFix campaign advisory, and Rhysida is attributed to a group BSI tracks as Vice Spider (aka Vice Society, WhiteNefas, White Hekate, DEV-0832, Vanilla Tempest). BSI's advisory adds that operators staged exfiltration into attacker-controlled Azure cloud storage using the vendor's own azcopy tool and separately names the malware family LoremIpsumLoader (aka AxolotLoader) as attributed to the same group. Confidence moves from medium to high on the strength of this national-CERT technical confirmation.

The leak's national-security framing sharpens: a CDU defense-policy spokesperson states the published dataset includes civil-defense/total-defense emergency plans and barracks documents alongside the critical-infrastructure material already recorded, prompting the Bundeswehr's own operational command to join BSI's review. Separately, the Berlin district of Lichtenberg has refused to deploy CrowdStrike's Falcon Agent on its own servers over data-access and monitoring concerns, and Berlin's data protection commissioner has issued concrete victim guidance.

rbb24 Recherche reported on 2026-10-21 that the Senate department for urban development's attack-detection licences covered only five percent of devices and that neither the entry endpoint nor the servers the data left from were covered; BSI told rbb24 it does not confirm that the Berlin attack followed the TerminalFix pattern.

Attribution fixes in the September sections: heise, not Kiesewetter, lists the civil-defense plans and barracks documents in the leaked data, and heise, not the Interior Ministry, says cooperation agreements do not exist with all 16 states; the ministry points to 14 existing agreements.

entries.action_label: Talos: NIK C2 implant calls the OpenAI API from the…
entries.classification_html: NATOB2
entries.headline: Talos: NIK C2 implant calls the OpenAI API from the victim host and bills the victim's own key if none is given
entries.html:
ROUTINENATOB2

NIK C2: Talos documents a Go Windows implant that sends operator prompts to the OpenAI API from the infected host and falls back to the victim's own API key

Cisco Talos found a command-and-control framework it calls NIK C2, with a live server, whose 64-bit Go implant for Windows takes more than 52 commands: browser and Wi-Fi credential theft, keylogging, screen, camera, microphone and clipboard capture, hidden VNC, RDP session interaction, an embedded SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy with a reverse tunnel for lateral movement, AMSI patching, UAC bypass and process hollowing (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). It talks to its server over TLS WebSockets on port 443 with an HTTP polling fallback about every 250 milliseconds under AES-256-GCM, persists through registry Run keys and COM hijacking, masquerades under a system-process name such as svchost.exe and runs a watchdog process (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). The new part is the ai_generate command: the implant builds an OpenAI Chat Completions request from an operator prompt on the infected host, posts it to OpenAI from the victim's address and returns the answer to the panel; if the operator gives no key it reads the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable, so OpenAI charges the victim's payment method and its logs show the victim's key (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29; Infosecurity Magazine, 2026-10-29). A screen-locking ransomware module encrypts no files: PowerShell copies the boot sector to a temporary file, and a looping batch file reopens a lock page shown through mshta.exe (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Talos sees at least three implant versions and assesses with moderate confidence that the framework is functional; its post names no victims, sector or delivery method (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Windows hosts; the post gives no initial-access method, so exposure cannot be read from an estate's configuration. A host that holds an OPENAI_API_KEY in its environment lends that key to the operator.
Detection
In egress and proxy telemetry, requests to the OpenAI API from a process that is not a sanctioned AI client, in particular a process named like a system binary such as svchost.exe that runs from the user's Roaming Microsoft Network folder, the install location the post describes; in process and registry telemetry, the fodhelper.exe UAC-bypass pattern (a command written under the ms-settings shell key and removed within seconds), an AMSI patch in a PowerShell session and, from the lock-screen module, a Run key that launches a looping batch file (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29); on the OpenAI side, usage or billing under a key the owner did not use.
Defender takeaway
Add the OpenAI API (and other LLM endpoints) to the list of destinations that only sanctioned clients may reach, and rotate any OpenAI key found on a host where this framework ran, because the implant bills and logs it as the victim's own.

entries.headline: CERT-UA: Dahua cameras are taken over through the Easy4IP cloud even with no port exposed; turn P2P off
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2021-33044 +1exploitedNATOA2

Dahua cameras and recorders: CERT-UA warns that attackers take devices over through the Easy4IP cloud relay even when no port is exposed, then view video, change configuration and add accounts

CERT-UA's alert (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23; dated 2026-10-23 by Security Affairs, 2026-10-27) reports recorded compromises of Dahua IP cameras and DVRs in which attackers had the video stream, changed the device configuration and created accounts of their own (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27). The main vector is Easy4IP, Dahua's peer-to-peer remote-access feature: a device with it enabled opens an outbound connection to Dahua's cloud and registers by serial number, and access then runs through the cloud, bypassing NAT and firewall, with no published port and no public address (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23; Security Affairs, 2026-10-27). Serial numbers follow a predictable pattern, a 10-character model prefix and a five-character hexadecimal counter that rises almost sequentially, so attackers can guess them at scale and learn which devices are cloud-connected without hitting rate limits (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27). Authentication is then beaten with weak or known passwords or with the authentication-bypass flaws CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045 in outdated firmware, which CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2024-08-21, although their use in the October cases remains unconfirmed (eSecurity Planet, 2026-10-27). Dahua fixed both in 2021 with model-specific firmware builds and rates them CVSS 8.1 (Dahua, 2021-11-15). CERT-UA does not say who was targeted, how many devices are affected or who is behind the activity (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27).

The Hacker News says the activity shares similarities with Hunt.io's earlier Operation CameraSwarm, which reported more than 14,530 Dahua cameras compromised between 2026-06-17 and 2026-07-22 with brute-forced credentials and the same two-flaw chain, nearly 2,000 of them given a backdoor account that survives a password change and, on most firmware, a factory reset (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27); eSecurity Planet says no connection to the October incidents has been established (eSecurity Planet, 2026-10-27). Dutch intelligence services warned in July that Russian state actors compromise IP cameras to collect intelligence on military transports (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
Any Dahua IP camera, NVR or DVR with Easy4IP enabled, whether or not it has a public address; CERT-UA warns that such devices may be vulnerable even when they cannot be reached directly from the internet (Security Affairs, 2026-10-27).
Detection
In each device's audit log, DVRIP authentication events from the local address 127.0.0.1, which CERT-UA reads as a sign of access through the P2P cloud, plus accounts nobody created and unauthorized configuration changes; text overlaid on the video image is another sign, but its absence proves nothing (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27; Security Affairs, 2026-10-27).

Triage: a login from 127.0.0.1 shows only that the session arrived through the P2P relay, so where staff or an installer legitimately use Easy4IP it is normal; the account name, the time and the configuration change that follows separate the two.

Defender takeaway
Turn Easy4IP off wherever it is not needed, keep cameras off the internet and reach them through a VPN limited to authorized addresses, review the account list and the cloud accounts linked to each device, and update the firmware by hand, CERT-UA's four steps (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23; Security Affairs, 2026-10-27); check all Dahua devices on the network, forgotten ones included (Security Affairs, 2026-10-27), and do not count on a password on outdated firmware, since those flaws make knowing it unnecessary (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23).

Builds on: Dutch intelligence: Russia hijacked default-credential internet cameras along military-supply…

actions: Update the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, on every internet-facing server and container image to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or to your distribution's patched package, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and every long-running worker, rebuild images, and confirm the running version, because a distribution backport can keep the old version string; isolate any application that cannot be updated from public networks until it is.

After updating, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on every PHP host and keep it there until PHP's next regular bugfix release: CVE-2026-115560, which the October releases do not fix, needs session upload progress to be enabled.

List every appliance and management server whose web interface embeds PHP (firewalls, network access control and security consoles), take each interface off the internet and install its vendor's PHP2Shell fix, because Dream Research reports Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewalls rooted through an exposed management interface.
