entries.headline: PHP2Shell: CISA lists both flaws as exploited after honeypot code execution; update the runtime, not the CMS
entries.html:
CRITICALCVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

The PHP project released PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both CVSS 4.0 9.2, and urges all PHP users to update immediately (PHP, 2026-10-21; PHP, 2026-10-20). CVE-2026-109618 is memory corruption when PHP handles an out-of-memory error: it aborts the request with longjmp() while internal request data is only partly initialised, and request cleanup then treats the invalid data as valid (PHP, 2026-10-21). CVE-2026-109619 is stale global state: request-owned state survives a fatal error after its memory is freed, and a later request on the same worker uses it (PHP, 2026-10-21). Every PHP installation serving web requests is at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed; the project rates mod_php highest, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs (PHP, 2026-10-21). The confirmed impact is unauthenticated code execution as the web worker account, validated against mod_php with default settings, and for the second flaw against both mod_php and FPM through session upload progress, which is on by default and needs no session_start() call (PHP, 2026-10-21; PHP, 2026-10-21). The advisory for the second flaw also lists heap use-after-free and memory disclosure among the confirmed impacts (PHP, 2026-10-21), and Sansec says the leaked worker memory can hold passwords, session tokens, API keys and TLS private keys from other requests, and files the upload-progress memory disclosure under CVE-2026-109618 where the PHP advisories list it under CVE-2026-109619 (Sansec, 2026-10-21).

The fixed branches are 8.2 to 8.5; PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates, and the project published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for people who build from source, while distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance (PHP, 2026-10-21). Cloudflare says all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later are affected (Cloudflare, 2026-10-21). The fix is in the runtime, so updating WordPress, a plugin or a theme does not change exposure (Wordfence, 2026-10-20). Products that embed PHP are affected through it: Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 as affected, with all twenty hotfixes released, and notes that the issue applies to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-30), and ENISA, the Commission, CERT-EU, Europol EC3 and the CSIRTs network point to NCSC-NL's repository for software that bundles PHP (ENISA, 2026-10-21).

CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 and revised its alert the same day; the alert names no actor and does not say how CISA learned of the exploitation (CISA, 2026-10-26; CISA KEV, 2026-10-26). Code execution was documented in a honeypot report by Adel Karimi of Perplexity dated 2026-10-24: on three disposable targets running PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker Apache mod_php, 35 execution-stage requests were each followed by a shell started directly by an Apache worker, in a four-stage multipart chain (memory pressure, memory disclosure, more memory pressure, an execution request adjusted to the leaked layout); the chain is consistent with CVE-2026-109618, the records do not establish a CVE-2026-109619 path and no second-stage download was observed (Karimi, 2026-10-24; SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). Earlier reports describe scanning and attempts: Cloudflare saw attack traffic against its customers while the flaws were still leaked (Cloudflare, 2026-10-21), watchTowr's honeypots recorded exploitation on 2026-10-21 (watchTowr, 2026-10-21), and VulnCheck's canary hosts recorded scanning from 08:37 UTC that day (VulnCheck, 2026-10-21). VulnCheck says it holds a working exploit for CVE-2026-109618 that, as of 2026-10-26, supports mod_php on PHP 8.2.28 to 8.2.34, 8.3.22 to 8.3.35, 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 to 8.5.11 with default settings and display_errors off, and WordPress on default Docker installs (VulnCheck, 2026-10-26). Palo Alto Networks' advisory for both flaws now states that active exploitation has been observed targeting its management interface exposed to the internet, after a copy of 2026-10-27 said very limited exploitation, and names no victim or actor (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-27); Dream Research's recovered artifacts, described next, add a detailed account of a production compromise through these CVEs, while Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update of 2026-10-23 that had linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws and says it is unable to confirm that the initial access is associated with them (Unit 42, 2026-10-25), and CrowdStrike, Wordfence and Sophos reported no successful exploitation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23; Wordfence, 2026-10-22; Sophos, 2026-10-22). Dream Research describes the chain it recovered: a custom PHP2Shell build tailored to the management web server of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (PHP 8.0.30), combined with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300, gave unauthenticated root on 24 internet-facing firewalls and led, through the second of two firewalls of a US government-affiliated organization (the first crashed), to an outbound SSH tunnel, the rooting of the organization's firewall management server and a password-spraying attack on its Active Directory, and CISA's entry for the kernel flaw says the same chaining (Dream Research, 2026-10-29; CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). In Switzerland, SRF reported on 2026-10-26 that TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 customers in connection with the PHP flaw after a data theft at its booking-system supplier Camping.Care, and Blick, citing SRF, writes that the attackers used the two flaws; neither names a CVE (SRF, 2026-10-26; Blick, 2026-10-26).

PHP posted an informational advisory on 2026-10-23 for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix: it needs an application that sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize, switches it to php with ini_set() before session_start(), and leaves session upload progress enabled; PHP calls it an unlikely vector, issues no emergency release, suggests session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release and will publish the full advisory then (PHP, 2026-10-23). PHP has not stated affected versions or a severity score for CVE-2026-115560, and no exploitation is reported (The Hacker News, 2026-10-23).

Assessments of how easy exploitation is diverge. Sansec says an attack needs specific knowledge of the target server and specific conditions on it, that nobody has shown a single request that works against any vulnerable server, as there was for Log4Shell and Shellshock, that a researcher who tested the public proofs of concept found they do not work against a default PHP installation, and that mass exploitation is therefore less likely than it first expected, while it advises updating anyway (Sansec, 2026-10-21). CrowdStrike expects no single universal exploit but says a reliable one is feasible against a specific deployment profile, such as a fixed Docker image, because an attacker can calibrate offsets and heap grooming in advance (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23), and the SANS Internet Storm Center, reading the public proofs of concept, finds a universal, reliable one-click exploit quite difficult (SANS ISC, 2026-10-23). Red Hat rates CVE-2026-109618 Important (CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity, against 9.8 at NVD), says reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing, and says its standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM, whose workers exit on early initialization failures, so code execution is difficult in practice and typically needs non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution (Red Hat, 2026-10-21). That sits against VulnCheck's weaponized exploit above, and the advice of the PHP project, BACS, CERT-EU and ENISA to update is unchanged. Vendors of products that embed PHP report as follows: Citrix lists the NetScaler management GUI on every supported version (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22); Cisco lists Expressway, Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul, Duo Access Gateway and ISE Portal Builder, with fixes at 15.5.21, 26.2.1.9 (November 2026) and 3.2.0 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-30); Fortinet keeps only FortiDDoS, FortiSOAR and FortiSOAR PaaS under investigation (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-10-26); Splunk lists its products as unaffected or remedied (Splunk, 2026-10-26); Tenable's patch SC-202610.2 updates the bundled PHP in Security Center and Enclave Security to 8.2.35 (Tenable, 2026-10-23; Tenable, 2026-10-23); Siemens lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices running PAN-OS as affected (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-23); and WatchGuard says none of its products are affected (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Every internet-facing server or container image that runs PHP, and every product, appliance or administration interface that embeds it, internal ones included; BACS stresses that operators often do not know a product uses PHP, and that distribution packages can carry the fix under an unchanged version number, so the running version and the vendor's security information decide (BACS, 2026-10-21). On WordPress the running PHP version is shown under Tools > Site Health > Info > Server (Wordfence, 2026-10-20).
Detection
AWS, as relayed by Inside IT, advises an operator who cannot exclude a compromise to start the investigation at least from 2026-10-17, its earliest honeypot exploit attempt (Inside IT, 2026-10-22); the telemetry is, in web access logs, multipart POST requests to PHP endpoints from unfamiliar sources, including multipart requests that use the upload-progress code path, which VulnCheck's canaries saw scanners send (VulnCheck, 2026-10-21); in PHP error logs and process telemetry, worker crashes and fatal errors, and processes started by the web server or PHP worker account, since the code runs with the web worker's privileges (PHP, 2026-10-21), above all a shell started directly by an Apache worker, as in Karimi's honeypots and, since 2026-10-28, on GreyNoise's sensors, where it went on to open bash reverse shells over /dev/tcp, and create a .ssh directory under /var/www (Karimi, 2026-10-24; GreyNoise, 2026-11-01), which CISA also names as the behaviour to watch for (CISA, 2026-10-26); on Windows servers running IIS with PHP-CGI, Morphisec reports the web worker w3wp.exe starting php-cgi.exe, which started cmd.exe and a packed payload that tried to open a reverse shell (Morphisec, 2026-10-28); and in the web root, new or changed files. BACS asks operators to examine logs and systems for unusual requests, crashes, changed files and unexpected processes, and says an update does not remove a compromise that has already happened (BACS, 2026-10-21). ReliaQuest, which reproduced exploitation of CVE-2026-109618 in controlled labs, reports a sequence across the PHP error, Apache access, Apache error and system logs: a POST that returns HTTP 500, PHP memory exhaustion reported "in Unknown on line 0" where an ordinary memory error names the application file and line, heap corruption, and an abort of the Apache worker that handled the request within seconds; each event can be benign alone, the full sequence on the same process is the stronger indication, and linking request to crash needs the process ID in the Apache access log as well as the error log (ReliaQuest, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
Update the PHP runtime on every internet-facing host today and restart the workers, internet-facing systems first and then internal and embedded installations, and take the management interface of every appliance that embeds PHP off the internet; where an update must wait, CERT-EU advises isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until the fix is applied and verified (CERT-EU, 2026-10-21). The project's interim settings (disable session upload progress, enforce memory_limit=-1 administratively, a low post_max_size, block multipart requests at the proxy where uploads are not needed) reduce only some attack paths, and BACS says a web application firewall alone is not enough (BACS, 2026-10-21; PHP, 2026-10-21). PHP 8.1 and older need a vendor backport, the project's source backports or an upgrade, ASLR is not a safe reason to wait on x86-64 given VulnCheck's exploit, and an update does not remove an attacker who is already in. The October releases do not fix CVE-2026-115560, so keep session upload progress disabled on updated hosts until PHP's next regular release (PHP, 2026-10-23). Because the flaws can disclose worker memory, rotating session secrets, API keys and other credentials that the PHP workers handled is a reasonable step on hosts that were reachable while unpatched.
Update22 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-22T0256Z-intelactionsbodyclassificationconfidencecvesevidenceheadlineimmediate_actionpriorityregionssourcessourcing_notesummarytagstechniquestitle

The fixed releases shipped on 2026-10-21 between 13:30 and 14:00 UTC, depending on the source, together with the technical advisories, so the earlier statement that no fix existed no longer holds (CERT-EU, 2026-10-21; ENISA, 2026-10-21; Sansec, 2026-10-21). ENISA, the European Commission, CERT-EU, Europol EC3 and the CSIRTs network advise organisations to identify their PHP-based applications, coordinate with hosting and service providers, apply the update to internet-facing systems first, and isolate exposed applications from public networks where that is not possible (ENISA, 2026-10-21). BACS published its warning the same day, telling operators to check embedded and internal PHP installations as well as public sites, to restart long-running PHP processes and rebuild containers, to verify the running version, and, where an immediate update is impossible, to consider disconnecting critical applications from the internet (BACS, 2026-10-21). BACS told RTS it knows of no reliable, confirmed substitute for the updates and that the interim measures give no guaranteed full protection (RTS, 2026-10-21).

Attack traffic was reported on the day: Cloudflare saw it against its customers while the flaws were still leaked, watchTowr's honeypots recorded exploitation, and VulnCheck's canary hosts logged scanning from 08:37 UTC and at least one unsuccessful web-shell attempt through a session file, while VulnCheck says it holds a working exploit for CVE-2026-109618 that succeeds on x86-64 with ASLR enabled; no source reports a confirmed compromise (Cloudflare, 2026-10-21; watchTowr, 2026-10-21; VulnCheck, 2026-10-21). Palo Alto Networks confirmed that every PAN-OS and Panorama release is affected through the management web interface, with no fixed release yet (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-21).

Public-sector sites went offline as a precaution, mostly on the evening of 2026-10-21. The canton of Basel-Stadt activated its crisis staff and shut down every PHP-run cantonal website with no restoration time given, while stating that no security-relevant incident had been registered (Canton of Basel-Stadt, 2026-10-21). The Ticino cantonal administration temporarily disabled some online services, the website of the University of Geneva was unreachable, and the EPFL site displayed a notice that its pages were currently unreachable, although nau.ch says it still worked (nau.ch, 2026-10-21); RTS lists the EPFL and University of Geneva sites as temporarily suspended (RTS, 2026-10-21). Several Neuchâtel canton and city sites were unreachable without an official statement; Arcinfo presumes a link to the PHP flaw, which the state had not confirmed (RTS, 2026-10-21). Lodur, the platform many Swiss fire brigades use to manage their fire brigades and alarm groups, was out of service because its provider took its servers offline as a precaution: users could neither read stored data nor edit alarm groups, though the Valais cantonal fire office said this does not necessarily mean the alarm-triggering systems are down (nau.ch, 2026-10-21; RTS, 2026-10-21). Publica took its website offline on the afternoon of 2026-10-21 as a precaution, says it has closed the vulnerabilities with security updates and was back online that evening, and states the outage is unrelated to the cyberattack on its software supplier (Publica, 2026-10-21). Dutch authorities took DigiD, MijnOverheid, Overheid.nl, TweedeKamer.nl and the tax authority offline for a time, and most were back by that evening (Security.nl, 2026-10-21); RTS reports that the site of the Paris police prefecture was also suspended (RTS, 2026-10-21). Basel-Stadt said it would report on progress on the morning of 2026-10-22, and no restoration status had been published as of the early morning of 2026-10-22 UTC.

Update23 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-23T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

BACS told Keystone-SDA and SRF on 2026-10-22 that no attack in Switzerland attributable to the two flaws is known to it, while stressing that unrecognised or unreported incidents cannot be excluded and that it has no reliable figures on affected websites, shops and internal applications (SRF, 2026-10-22; watson.ch, 2026-10-22). It also said that PHP-based applications of the federal administration were affected, that the responsible bodies were told to update, and that it has no complete overview of the update status (watson.ch, 2026-10-22; Inside IT, 2026-10-22).

The shutdowns were large and mostly short. The Basel host Cyon took all of its more than 100,000 customer websites offline for some hours and says everything has run again since the morning of 2026-10-22; the University of Geneva's site was still unreachable that afternoon, and Basel-Stadt still had pages offline at midday and says it found no data outflow (SRF, 2026-10-22). Neuchâtel disabled all PHP-based sites, ne.ch and many commune pages among them, its IT department installed the fix, and the EPFL gave its members access to its services by VPN while its site stayed down (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). Risikomonitor's live view counts 576,549 checked Swiss web servers, 540,169 already patched and 20,231 (3.5 %) still affected, with the PHP version hidden on the other 16,149 (Inside IT, 2026-10-22).

In the United Kingdom, a minister told the House of Lords on 2026-10-22 that 32 government services were unavailable and four partly unavailable, largely from precautionary measures while updates and mitigations were applied, and that the government knows of no confirmed compromise of central government systems, an assessment she extended to the wider public sector (UKAuthority, 2026-10-22; The Register, 2026-10-22). The Register adds that government sites in Germany, France, Belgium, Finland and the Netherlands were also taken offline as a precaution and that the NCSC sent 50,000 warnings (The Register, 2026-10-22).

Attack activity began before the release. Inside IT, citing a post by Cloudflare's chief executive, reports millions of attack attempts, the first at 07:43 UTC on 2026-10-21, more than six hours before the release, and relays that AWS threat intelligence recorded an exploit attempt against a honeypot on 2026-10-17 from a commercial anonymisation network, proofs of concept and attempts by several actors from 2026-10-21, and advises an operator who cannot exclude a compromise to start the investigation at least from 2026-10-17; whether the attempts would have succeeded on real systems is open (Inside IT, 2026-10-22). The Register likewise reports that AWS says attackers were exploiting the flaws four days before disclosure (The Register, 2026-10-22).

Update24 Oct 2026 03:36 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 added to its brief on 2026-10-23 a report that linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws and retracted that update on 2026-10-25; the update of 2026-10-26 below carries the retraction (Unit 42, 2026-10-25).

Other vendors report no successful exploitation. CrowdStrike has not observed any in the wild or in its honeypots and expects a reliable exploit only against a specific deployment profile, such as a fixed Docker image (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23); Wordfence knows of no compromise among the more than 74,000 attempts its firewall intercepted (Wordfence, 2026-10-22); and Sophos corrected on 2026-10-22 its earlier report of successful exploitation to scanning and a small number of failed attempts, one of them a blocked attempt to deliver a likely Mirai-derived botnet variant (Sophos, 2026-10-22). VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 on AMD64 and ARM64 with default settings and display_errors off under mod_php, and WordPress on default Docker installs, as of 5:30 PM ET on 2026-10-23 (VulnCheck, 2026-10-21). Neither flaw is in CISA's KEV catalog as of version 2026.10.23 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-23).

PHP posted an informational advisory on 2026-10-23 for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix: it needs an application that sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize, switches it to php with ini_set() before session_start(), and leaves session upload progress enabled (PHP, 2026-10-23). PHP calls it an unlikely vector, issues no emergency release, suggests session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, says a host that applied that setting from the 2026-10-21 advisory should keep it, and will publish the full advisory with the next release (PHP, 2026-10-23). PHP has not stated affected versions or a severity score, and no exploitation is reported (The Hacker News, 2026-10-23).

Vendor statuses moved. Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-23, now describes a workaround for Expressway in its bug record, keeps the fixed release 15.5.21 undated, lists Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul with a fix in 27.1.1 (February 2027), exploitable there only by an authenticated administrator and with a workaround described, and lists Duo Access Gateway with fixed release 3.2.0 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-23). Splunk now lists only Smartlook as under investigation (Splunk, 2026-10-23). Palo Alto Networks' advisory now lists WF-500 and WF-500-B as unaffected, a correction its timeline dates 2026-10-23, its table no longer distinguishes Panorama, and a note says the issue applies to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the PAN-OS hotfix dates of 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30 are unchanged (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-24).

Update25 Oct 2026 03:38 UTCrun 2026-10-25T0256Z-intelaffected_productsentitiessourcesevidencebody

Tenable's Security Center (versions 6.6.0, 6.7.2, 6.8.0 and 6.9.1) and Enclave Security (1.7.0, 1.8.0 and 1.9.1) bundle PHP, and patch SC-202610.2 updates the bundled PHP to 8.2.35 (Tenable, 2026-10-23; Tenable, 2026-10-23). Siemens lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 application-hosting devices running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS 10.2, 11.1, 11.2, 12.1 and 12.2 as affected by the two flaws and in its revision of 2026-10-28 tells operators to upgrade to the corresponding available PAN-OS version, with further patch information from customer support (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-28).

ReliaQuest says it independently reproduced exploitation of CVE-2026-109618 in controlled labs, with code execution only where the exploit's prerequisites were already present, and that it has not observed successful exploitation in customer environments (ReliaQuest, 2026-10-22). The sequence it saw in its logs is a POST that returns HTTP 500, PHP memory exhaustion reported "in Unknown on line 0", heap corruption and an abort of the Apache worker that handled the request within seconds, which it reads as a stronger indication when the events involve the same process (ReliaQuest, 2026-10-22).

Update26 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-26T0256Z-intelbodyevidenceimmediate_actionsourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 the update of 2026-10-23 in which it had reported post-exploitation by agentic attack platforms at a European government entity. Its brief now says that what its researchers saw was an attack against a European government agency executed in the context of a vulnerable PHP application, that this led them to believe it was exploitation of these flaws, and that it is unable to confirm that the initial access is associated with the specific PHP2Shell CVEs (Unit 42, 2026-10-25). The observations of the retracted update, including the command-batch markers and the Active Directory activity, are no longer part of the brief. The brief still recommends assessing exposure and patching immediately (Unit 42, 2026-10-25).

What remains documented is scanning and attack attempts, reported by Cloudflare, watchTowr, VulnCheck and others, and VulnCheck's working exploit for specific PHP builds; CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation, and no source tied a named CVE to a production compromise. The Hacker News article of 2026-10-25 relays the retracted account and has since added a note at its top recording Unit 42's retraction (The Hacker News, 2026-10-25).

Update27 Oct 2026 03:48 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelbodycvesevidenceheadlineimmediate_actionsourcessourcing_notesummarytags

CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 and updated its alert the same day, which still tells operators to patch internet-facing systems first, to take PHP-based systems offline where they cannot be patched or run PHP 8.1 or earlier, and to monitor for PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools (CISA, 2026-10-26; CISA KEV, 2026-10-26). The listing follows a honeypot report by Adel Karimi of Perplexity dated 2026-10-24, relayed by SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer on 2026-10-26, that documents successful code execution: 35 execution-stage requests against three honeypots running PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker mod_php, each followed by a shell started directly by an Apache worker, consistent with CVE-2026-109618 and not establishing a separate CVE-2026-109619 path (Karimi, 2026-10-24; SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). It is honeypot evidence: no second-stage download was observed, Karimi says it does not measure exploit reliability on other worker counts, PHP builds or applications, and, as of 2026-10-27, no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise; Unit 42's retraction of 2026-10-25 stands. Expel's Marcus Hutchins calls it by far the highest-quality confirmation of in-the-wild exploitation he has seen (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26).

VulnCheck's page, updated as of 2026-10-26, extends its working exploit to mod_php on PHP 8.2.28 to 8.2.34 and 8.3.22 to 8.3.35 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 to 8.5.11 (VulnCheck, 2026-10-26). In Switzerland, SRF reports on 2026-10-26 that TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 customers because data was stolen at its booking-system supplier Camping.Care in connection with the PHP flaw: names, telephone numbers and reservation numbers were used in fraudulent WhatsApp messages, and TCS says account and IBAN data were not affected; neither SRF nor TCS names a CVE or the entry point (SRF, 2026-10-26).

Update28 Oct 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelsummaryimmediate_actionevidencesourcing_notebodysources

Palo Alto Networks' advisory for both flaws now states that active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet, and its severity is Critical with urgency Highest (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28). A copy of the page taken on 2026-10-27 at 17:10 UTC said instead that very limited exploitation had been observed (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-27). The advisory names no victim, actor or post-exploitation behaviour and does not say which flaw was used. It is a vendor statement about its own product, Unit 42's retraction of 2026-10-25 stands (Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, 2026-10-25), and Palo Alto's remaining PAN-OS hotfixes are due by 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28).

Update29 Oct 2026 07:03 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-intelsummaryupdated_attechniquesentitiessourcesevidencesourcing_notereferencesactionsbody

CISA's catalog entry of 2026-10-28 for the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 says it can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Dream Research reports a chain that takes these flaws to root on appliances: a custom, non-public PHP2Shell build for the management web server of one large vendor's firewall software, which runs PHP 8.0.30 with a high memory limit, gave code execution as the nobody user, and the kernel flaw lifted it to root in one HTTP request in under 15 minutes (Dream Research, 2026-10-27). Dream found the build tuned to eleven firmware versions, nine exploitable, with offsets from the vendor's own PHP library, the deployment-specific calibration CrowdStrike expects a reliable exploit to need (an inference) (Dream Research, 2026-10-27; CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23). From about 19,000 internet-facing firewalls of that vendor it narrowed to 240, rooted 24 and left a PHP webshell on each, and from the second of two firewalls of a US government-affiliated organization (the first crashed) built a persistent outbound SSH tunnel, rooted the organization's firewall management server through it and began an attack on its Active Directory; Dream could not tell whether that attack succeeded, does not name the vendor, calls the campaign apparently Chinese and AI-assisted and does not attribute it to a named actor (Dream Research, 2026-10-27). The targets were firewalls whose management interfaces were reachable from the internet (Dream Research, 2026-10-27).

Palo Alto Networks' advisory as read on 2026-10-29 lists all PAN-OS hotfixes as released except 11.1.7-h12, due on 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

Update01 Nov 2026 04:10 UTCrun 2026-11-01T0256Z-intelsummaryactionssourcing_notesourcesevidencetechniquesentitiesbody

GreyNoise's live tracker, last updated 2026-11-01 03:48 UTC, records successful exploitation on its deliberately vulnerable sensors from 2026-10-28, the first when an Apache worker spawned a shell that ran curl, and counts 1,177 confirmed exploitations from five attacker addresses, defined as sessions in which the web server ran operating-system commands (GreyNoise, 2026-11-01). The count is of shell events on sensors, not of compromised servers. The commands recorded on 2026-10-29 include bash reverse shells over /dev/tcp, creation of /var/www/.ssh, queries to the cloud metadata address and downloads of the linPEAS and gitleaks enumeration and secret-scanning tools; secret-scanning runs over /var/www/html and system directories appear in the sessions of 2026-10-31 (GreyNoise, 2026-11-01).

Hunt.io, reading open-directory captures, says shells have been confirmed only on honeypots and sensors, which it names as watchTowr, 0x4D31 and GreyNoise, and that its shared exploit kit has not been seen landing on a live victim, while relaying Dream Research's and Unit 42's account of PAN-OS firewalls rooted in production as the first confirmed production compromises; in one capture an operator who ran the chain against a national government got only a crash, because session files lay outside the webroot, and then broke in with a different bug (Hunt.io, 2026-10-28).

Dream Research updated its report on 2026-10-29 to say that the affected devices run Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and that the operation rooted 25 PAN-OS firewall and management servers, and Unit 42 says it independently verified the attacker's tooling and confirmed the reported results (Dream Research, 2026-10-29; Unit 42, 2026-10-29). The earlier description of "one unnamed vendor" above is superseded.

Update01 Nov 2026 14:01 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbodyevidencesources

Morphisec reports blocking post-exploitation on a customer's Windows server running IIS with PHP-CGI, where the IIS worker process w3wp.exe started the PHP-CGI handler php-cgi.exe, which ran a command shell that launched a packed payload; the payload used shellcode to load networking libraries and tried to open a reverse shell to an external server (Morphisec, 2026-10-28). Morphisec ties the chain to the PHP flaws but says its agent did not detect the PHP exploitation itself, and it describes one customer; it says every earlier confirmed exploitation report described a Linux environment (Morphisec, 2026-10-28). On Windows, the process signal is therefore php-cgi.exe under w3wp.exe starting cmd.exe or other executables.

Siemens' advisory for RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices, at version 1.1 of 2026-10-28, now tells operators to upgrade to the corresponding available PAN-OS version and to contact customer support for further patch information (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-28). The Hacker News has added a note to its 2026-10-25 article recording Unit 42's retraction (The Hacker News, 2026-10-25). Hunt.io puts watchTowr's report of exploitation of both flaws on its honeypots on 2026-10-21 earliest, ahead of Karimi's honeypot report (Hunt.io, 2026-10-28).

immediate_action.action: Two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP itself are on CISA's exploited list since 2026-10-26, honeypots recorded working code execution and Palo Alto reports attacks on internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, fixed builds (8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35) have been out since 2026-10-21, and public proofs of concept circulate. Update PHP, not the CMS, on every internet-facing server and container image, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and all long-running workers, and confirm the running version, because distribution packages can keep the old version string. Isolate anything that cannot be updated from public networks, and check web roots, logs, crashes and unexpected processes, since an update does not remove an attacker who is already in.

entries.summary: The PHP project released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2), two flaws in the runtime that allow unauthenticated remote code execution as the web worker account, most directly on Apache mod_php, with no upstream release for PHP 8.1 and older and a third path, CVE-2026-115560, left unfixed (keep session.upload_progress.enabled=0). CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, after a honeypot operator documented 35 successful code executions on PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker mod_php and VulnCheck extended its working exploit across builds of PHP 8.2 to 8.5; GreyNoise's sensors have recorded shell sessions since 2026-10-28, Palo Alto Networks' advisory now reports active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces, Dream Research recovered a custom build chained with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that rooted 25 Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewall and management servers and attacked a US government-affiliated network, SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the flaws without naming a CVE, and Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to them. As of 2026-10-22 BACS knew of no attack in Switzerland but said federal PHP applications were affected and that it had no complete overview of the update status, and Swiss cantons, universities, Cyon, the Lodur platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution.
entries.title: CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

updates.summary: The fixed releases (PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35) shipped on 2026-10-21, so the earlier no-fix status ends; Cloudflare, watchTowr and VulnCheck report attack traffic and at least one unsuccessful web-shell attempt, proofs of concept are circulating, VulnCheck holds an exploit that succeeds with ASLR enabled and no source reports a confirmed compromise, so priority moves to critical. Swiss cantons, universities, the Lodur fire-brigade platform and Publica took sites offline as a precaution, and BACS, CERT-EU and ENISA tell operators to update the runtime, check embedded installations and look for compromise.

BACS says it knows of no attack in Switzerland but that PHP applications of the federal administration were affected and that it has no complete overview of the update status; the host Cyon took more than 100,000 sites offline for hours, a UK minister reports 32 government services unavailable with no confirmed compromise, and AWS reports a first exploit attempt on 2026-10-17. Sansec and Red Hat judge exploitation harder than VulnCheck's exploit suggests, and Palo Alto now schedules PAN-OS hotfixes for 2026-10-26 to 2026-10-30.

Unit 42 reports a confirmed intrusion of a European government entity with agentic post-exploitation, from its own telemetry and without naming the victim or the flaw that gave the foothold, while CrowdStrike, Sophos and Wordfence report no successful exploitation; PHP adds an informational advisory for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix, and advises session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until its next regular release. VulnCheck's exploit now covers PHP 8.5.10 and 8.5.11 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26, and Cisco, Splunk and Palo Alto Networks revised their product statuses.

Tenable's patch SC-202610.2 updates the PHP bundled in Security Center and Enclave Security to 8.2.35, and Siemens lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices running PAN-OS as affected with patch information only through customer support. ReliaQuest's lab reproduction gives a log sequence for detection (a POST returning HTTP 500, PHP memory exhaustion in Unknown on line 0, heap corruption, an Apache worker abort within seconds) and it has not seen successful exploitation in customer environments.

Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update that linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws and says it cannot confirm that the initial access is associated with them; the summary, the detection guidance and the 2026-10-24 section no longer carry that account. Priority stays critical: the scanning, attack attempts, public proofs of concept and VulnCheck's working exploit do not rest on the retracted report, and no source ties a confirmed compromise to these flaws.

CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 after a honeypot operator documented the first successful code execution (35 shells on three PHP 8.4.26 mod_php targets); no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise. VulnCheck's exploit now also covers PHP 8.2 and 8.3 builds on mod_php, and SRF links a data theft at TCS Camping's booking-system supplier to the PHP flaw; the entry's earlier statements that neither flaw was listed and that no source reported successful exploitation are replaced.

Palo Alto Networks' advisory for both flaws now says that active exploitation has been observed against its PAN-OS management interface exposed to the internet, after a copy of 2026-10-27 said very limited exploitation; it names no victim or actor, and Unit 42's retraction of 2026-10-25 stands. Priority stays critical.

Dream Research reports a production chain of a custom PHP2Shell build with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that gave unauthenticated root on 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and led to an attack on the Active Directory of a US government-affiliated organization; CISA's catalog entry for the kernel flaw of 2026-10-28 says the same chaining. The earlier statement that no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise is replaced, an action for appliances that embed PHP is added, the URWB fix date in the vendor list is corrected from March 2027 to November 2026 (advisory version 1.9), and the PAN-OS hotfix status is updated to nineteen of twenty released (advisory of 2026-10-29). Removed from the text: the sentence on the release time, Karimi's two-source-address-clusters and PHPSESSID remarks in the main text (the 2026-10-27 section keeps his reliability caveat), VulnCheck's failed web-shell attempt in the main text (the Detection line keeps it), the lab log-path remark and most of Sansec's note on its CVE attribution (kept as a short clause); the 'no source ties a named CVE' statement of 2026-10-27 is dated, and the evidence record for Karimi's clusters remark is dropped.

GreyNoise's live tracker records successful exploitation on its deliberately vulnerable sensors from 2026-10-28, with reverse shells, a .ssh directory under /var/www, cloud-metadata queries and secret-scanning tools in the sessions of 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-31; Hunt.io reports that an operator's attempt against a national government failed because session files lay outside the webroot, and relays that PAN-OS firewalls were rooted in production. Dream Research's updated report names Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS as the product behind the chain first described with an unnamed vendor, which Unit 42 says it verified.

Morphisec reports PHP2Shell post-exploitation on a Windows server running IIS with PHP-CGI (the IIS worker starting php-cgi.exe, a command shell and a packed reverse-shell payload), the first such account it knows of; Siemens now points APE1808 operators to the available PAN-OS versions, and The Hacker News carries Unit 42's retraction.

entries.headline: Microsoft patches an exploited Windows Shell zero-day that evades Mark of the Web protections on files and links
entries.html:
HIGHCVE-2026-96951exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-96951, Windows Shell: a Mark of the Web bypass exploited as a zero-day, fixed in the 2026-10-13 cumulative updates and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 8.8)

Microsoft's 2026-10-13 release fixes CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell security feature bypass that Microsoft marks as exploited and not publicly disclosed (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13); CISA added it to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog the same day, citing evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-10-13). Microsoft says an attacker who exploits it could evade Mark of the Web defenses, by sending a crafted file by email or instant message or enticing the user to click a link or open an attachment (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Microsoft's record gives the root cause as improper neutralization of special elements in a command (command injection, CWE-77) (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13). Rapid7 describes the effect as Windows not showing the dialog that says it protected the PC, because the tag that triggers it is bypassed, calls this the second exploited Windows Shell zero-day this year, and says the flaw also affected Outlook.com, patched in a build several weeks ago (Rapid7, 2026-10-13). Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 receives no patch while Server 2012 R2 does (Rapid7, 2026-10-13), and Microsoft's record lists no Windows Server 2012 product for this flaw (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-13).

Exposure
Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2012 R2 through 2025 where users open files or links from mail, chat or the web, and Microsoft Edge below 154.0.4258.62 (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-26); the fixed build per release is in the CVE record, and Rapid7 reports no patch for Windows Server 2012.
Detection
Microsoft, CISA and Rapid7 name no actor, payload or victims and no source describes the exploit's behavior, so this is a hunt hypothesis that follows from the mechanism: the failed control is the Mark of the Web tag, so there is no warning dialog for a user to report. Look at mail gateway, chat and endpoint file-origin telemetry for internet-origin files, archives and shortcuts that execute without the usual download warning, and at process lineage from explorer.exe into scripting interpreters and living-off-the-land binaries shortly after a mail or browser download.

Triage: a file a user created or received from a trusted local source also carries no tag; the discriminator is an internet origin (mail, chat or web download) together with the absence of the tag on the opened item.

Defender takeaway
Install the October cumulative update now, ahead of the monthly cycle, and confirm Edge is at 154.0.4258.62 or later, on endpoints that open mail and web downloads first; because the tag is the control that failed, attachment blocking and mail-gateway detonation remain the compensating layer until the update is deployed, and Rapid7 reports no patch for Windows Server 2012.
Update01 Nov 2026 14:00 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditactionsaffected_productsbodycvessources

Microsoft revised the CVE record on 2026-10-26 to add Microsoft Edge (Chromium-based) to its security updates table, with 154.0.4258.62 as the fixed build, and encourages customers running a supported Edge version to update to it (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-10-26). That Edge stable build was released on 2026-10-05 (Microsoft Learn, 2026-10-05), so an Edge that updates automatically already carries it; an estate that pins or defers Edge versions should confirm it. Microsoft does not say how Edge is involved in the bypass.

entries.headline: Bern's cantonal cybersecurity law is in force: 24h/72h incident reporting and a named accountable officer per agency
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOA2

Canton of Bern confirms 1 November 2026 entry-into-force for its new cybersecurity law (ICSG): 24h/72h mandatory incident reporting and named security accountability for every cantonal administrative unit

Canton Bern's government council (Regierungsrat) confirmed on 2026-09-10 that the cantonal Gesetz über Informations- und Cybersicherheit (ICSG), passed by the Grand Council on 12 June 2025 (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-09-09), and its implementing Verordnung über die Informations- und Datensicherheit (IDSV) enter into force on 1 November 2026 (headtopics.com / Kanton Bern Regierungsrat, 2026-09-10), a date also carried on KAIO's own page. From that date, every cantonal administrative unit must report cyberattacks and security incidents within 24 hours; where personal data is affected, a 72-hour deadline applies instead (headtopics.com / Kanton Bern Regierungsrat, 2026-09-10). The law introduces a graduated procedure for ICT assets: depending on protection need, either uniform baseline minimum measures apply or a detailed security-and-data-protection concept is required, and the canton classifies information as "intern", "vertraulich" or "geheim" only where unauthorised disclosure would harm its interests (headtopics.com / Kanton Bern Regierungsrat, 2026-09-10). New obligations include rules on personal security screening (Personensicherheitsprüfung) and, from 1 November 2026, explicit accountability assigned to each agency's or directorate's own top leadership as the designated security officer, supported by security officers and a new central advisory unit inside KAIO that also runs the cantonal information-security management system (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-09-09). The ICSG/IDSV explicitly satisfies the security requirements for cooperation with the federal government under the national Informationssicherheitsgesetz (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-09-09).

Municipal bodies and other public-task carriers in the canton are bound by the ICSG/IDSV only to the extent they process cantonal or federal information, use cantonal or federal ICT resources, or process personal data; the cantonal rules otherwise apply to them only as a recommendation (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-09-09). The canton is also standing up a dedicated platform for reporting security incidents, vulnerabilities and data-security breaches, for which KAIO's page, as changed on 2026-10-30, still gives no details (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-10-30). Transition periods of two to three years apply for administrative units to fully implement the new requirements (headtopics.com / Kanton Bern Regierungsrat, 2026-09-10), and this complements rather than duplicates the revised cantonal data-protection law, already in force since 1 September 2026 (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-09-09).

Defender takeaway
The obligations apply from 1 November 2026: cantonal Bern administrative units and any body handling cantonal or federal Bern information or ICT resources need a named SIVE (Sicherheitsverantwortliche/r) and a working 24-hour/72-hour incident-reporting path now, ICT-asset classification scheduled within the transition window, and, for suppliers, the AGB ISDS BE terms in contracts that cover processing information or personal data.
Update01 Nov 2026 13:59 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbodyevidenceheadlinesourcessummary

The ICSG and its ordinance IDSV are in force from 1 November 2026, and the former directorate ordinance on information security and data protection (ISDS DV) lapses the same day (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-10-30). KAIO's page, as changed on 2026-10-30, says the baseline directive Grundschutz BE, which defines the protection requirements for cantonal authorities, is expected to enter into force in the first quarter of 2027, and that the existing directive ICSGW stays valid until then. Annex 4 of Grundschutz BE holds the canton's general terms on information security and data protection (AGB ISDS BE, version of 27 October 2026), which the cantonal administration must agree as part of contracts whose subject is the processing of information or personal data, so suppliers of the canton should expect them in new contracts. The incident-reporting platform is still announced without details. Communes and other public-task carriers are bound to the extent that they process cantonal or federal information, use cantonal or federal ICT resources or process personal data (Kanton Bern KAIO, 2026-10-30).

entries.headline: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets is not enough
entries.html:
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB1

GhostAction returns: stolen maintainer credentials push a fake security-audit workflow into the victims' own GitHub repositories, which now harvests credentials from the entire git history

StepSecurity reports that on 2026-10-08 the GhostAction GitHub Actions credential-theft campaign used the accounts of two open-source maintainers to push a workflow disguised as a security improvement to 345 repositories, among them an Uber-owned repository that one maintainer could still write to (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09). The operator holds a maintainer's GitHub credential, which StepSecurity assesses as most plausibly a personal access token leaked through infostealer logs or credential dumps, then commits a workflow titled to look like a security audit straight to the default branch under the victim's own identity, unsigned and without a pull request; that push runs it, and nothing in an audit log looks anomalous unless the content is read (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09). GitGuardian says the technique remains at the core of the Mini Shai-Hulud malware family (GitGuardian, 2026-10-07).

The newer payload sends the named Actions secrets and every cloud, AI-provider and SaaS credential pattern found in the working tree and the entire git history to a hardcoded address over plain HTTP, so no DNS lookup occurs (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09). The wave was far larger than those first counts: GitGuardian counts more than 30,000 repositories between 8 and 12 October (GitGuardian, 2026-10-07) and, as lower bounds, a further 72,026 commits to 22,964 repositories from 1,792 accounts between 13 and 21 October, 1,382 of which had already pushed the 8 October payload, so the stolen tokens still work (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
Any GitHub account whose token or session credential has leaked, every repository it can write to, and since 14 October any developer machine that opened such a repository in VS Code with the workspace trusted (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27); StepSecurity says a workflow posing as a security audit or an Actions security workflow that appeared in a repository you maintain since 2026-08-31 means treat it as a confirmed breach (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09).
Detection
Source-control audit logs: workflow files added straight to default branches without a pull request by a maintainer identity, unsigned commits landing in many repositories within minutes; an organisation-scoped code search with StepSecurity's published content-marker queries for security-themed workflow files; runner egress logs: an HTTP POST to a bare IP address with no preceding DNS lookup (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09). Removing the workflow does not undo the theft: StepSecurity says any secret ever committed to a repository must be treated as compromised, so treat each run as an exfiltration, scan the full history and rotate every credential found (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09); GitGuardian adds that the GitHub credential that allowed the injection must be revoked too (GitGuardian, 2026-10-07), and that on developer machines and self-hosted runners a crontab entry fetching and running a script from the operator's server every five minutes survives cleaning the repository (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27).

Triage: the audit-log pattern separates this from a team adding a scanning workflow: no pull request, unsigned commits across many repositories, and a manual dispatch right after creation (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09).

Defender takeaway
Search the GitHub organisations your teams and suppliers administer for security-themed workflow files and for hidden editor tasks that run on folder open; on a hit revoke the committing credential, rotate everything in the repository's full history and check the crontab of every machine that opened or ran it. StepSecurity saw requiring approval for workflow runs stop the exfiltration and names branch protection on .github/workflows so workflow changes need pull-request review (StepSecurity, 2026-10-09).
Update20 Oct 2026 08:42 UTCrun 2026-10-20T0835Z-auditbodyevidencesourcing_notesummary

GitGuardian updated its analysis on 2026-10-13 from its own dataset: between 8 and 12 October the campaign targeted more than 30,000 repositories across 3,000 users and organisations by compromising the GitHub accounts of about 1,900 users, and tried to extract 3,174 secrets from public repositories' CI, with the largest spike on 8 and 9 October (GitGuardian, 2026-10-07). Socket's update of 9 October, with more than 500 accounts and tens of thousands of repositories since 7 October, is of the same order (Socket, 2026-10-09). GitGuardian says GitHub started preventing the malicious workflow from running on 9 October, so the further waves it saw on 10 and 12 October, with the same payload, could not extract any secrets (GitGuardian, 2026-10-07); a workflow from those later waves still means the account that committed it is compromised. Part of the October victims had already been hit in the September 2025 and August 2026 waves, and GitGuardian assesses that the operator likely relies in part on secrets left unrotated since earlier campaigns (GitGuardian, 2026-10-07).

Update01 Nov 2026 13:58 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditactionsbodysourcessummarytechniquesevidence

GitGuardian's analysis of 2026-10-27 counts, as lower bounds from its own feed, 72,026 commits from the operator to 22,964 public repositories between 13 and 21 October, 7,989 of them new victims, pushed by 1,792 accounts of which 1,382 had already pushed the 8 October payload: the tokens stolen earlier were never revoked (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). The campaign now ships five payload families and reaches beyond GitHub-hosted runners. One family is a Node.js stealer disguised as a font file and launched by a hidden VS Code task that runs when a developer opens the folder and trusts the workspace; it reads cloud, package-registry, Git, Kubernetes and AI-tool credential files, SSH keys and token-bearing environment variables, and since no workflow is involved, GitHub's workflow hold does not stop it. Self-hosted-runner workflows query the cloud instance metadata service for role credentials, and the revived 2025 workflow requests a GitHub OIDC token and tries to assume every AWS IAM role found in the environment (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). Three families install a cron job that fetches and runs a script from the operator's server every five minutes, so a developer laptop or runner that ran one stays under control after the repository is cleaned. GitGuardian found no successful run of the workflow payloads, which GitHub's hold caught (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). Between 22 and 26 October, loaders of a separate campaign, PolinRider, were added to GhostAction commits and force-pushed; GitGuardian sees no clear link between the two operators (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). It warns against reverting the attacker's "Update" commits, which restores the previous malicious version, and has seen re-infection where tokens were kept after a clean-up (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27).

entries.headline: PHP2Shell hits NetModule routers (fix: NRSW 5.0.0.105), macmon, Schneider, B&R, HMS, Wibu and Oracle products
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP2Shell in industrial, building and network-access products: Belden NetModule NRSW is fixed in 5.0.0.105 and macmon 6.x must move to 7.x, with notices from Schneider Electric, B&R, HMS Networks, Wibu-Systems, Johnson Controls and Oracle

Industrial, building and network-access vendors have published their own notices for the PHP runtime flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which CISA lists as exploited since 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-26). Belden says all versions of NetModule NRSW, including the latest mainline release 5.0.0.104, are affected and recommends upgrading to 5.0.0.105; where the upgrade is not possible it advises disabling the web interface after confirming SSH access, with the CLI settings http.status=0 and https.status=0 (Belden, 2026-10-22). NetModule AG is headquartered in Bern, Switzerland (Belden, 2022-03-14). Belden's macmon 6.x and 7.x use PHP in the web interface: a patch for 7.x is in the service portal, 6.x must move to 7.x, and the HTTPS web interface and guest portal must not be reachable from the internet unprotected (Belden, 2026-10-22).

Schneider Electric lists EcoStruxure Security Expert (fixed in 1.48.4.0), ProLeiT LINEoptimize (remediation through ProLeiT support) and EcoStruxure Control Engineering, where its revision of 2026-10-26 gives an automatic update if the hosting virtual machine can reach the debian.org and sury.org repositories and a Schneider patch otherwise (Schneider Electric, 2026-10-26; SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26). Its revision of 2026-10-28 adds EcoStruxure Foxboro DCS H90 Server, on HPE ProLiant DL380 Gen9 with Windows Server 2016, with only a mitigation: block TCP ports 2301 and 2381, used by the HPE System Management Homepage (Schneider Electric, 2026-10-30). B&R says APROL up to R 4.4-65 is affected, with patches planned for 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-29 (B&R, 2026-10-23). HMS Networks says Netbiter firmware up to 3.00.10 can be exploited from the LAN or the USB port and that 3.00.11 fixes it (HMS Networks, 2026-10-23). Wibu-Systems lists the web interface of CodeMeter License Central and its extensions; 5.2.3 is the update for 5.2.x, a manual php.ini hardening is strongly recommended on 5.2.2, and a new patch installer covers 5.1.2 and 5.0.x (Wibu-Systems, 2026-10-29). Johnson Controls has released patches for several Illustra product lines and fixed Visonic PowerManage in 5.0.45 (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26). Oracle's Security Alert, revised on 2026-10-26, patches Oracle Secure Backup 19.1.0.0.0 to 19.1.0.1.0, Oracle Solaris 11 and eight Oracle Communications products for CVE-2026-109618 (CVSS 3.1 9.8) and says it will extend the alert as more patches become available (Oracle, 2026-10-26).

Exposure
A NetModule router running NRSW, a macmon server, or any other listed product whose web interface answers from a network that is not a trusted administrative one; the vendors name the web interface as the affected component (Belden, 2026-10-22; HMS Networks, 2026-10-23).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade every NetModule NRSW router to 5.0.0.105, disabling the web interface where that is not yet possible, block TCP 2301 and 2381 to Foxboro DCS H90 servers, and keep the web interfaces of the other listed products off untrusted networks until their patches are installed; install the vendor fix wherever one is listed, such as the macmon 7.x patch (Belden, 2026-10-22), Security Expert version 1.48.4.0 (Schneider Electric, 2026-10-26), Netbiter 3.00.11 (HMS Networks, 2026-10-23) and CodeMeter License Central 5.2.3 (Wibu-Systems, 2026-10-29).
Update01 Nov 2026 13:52 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessummarytagstitle

Belden's advisory PSIRT-10, now at version 1.1, recommends upgrading NetModule NRSW to 5.0.0.105; disabling the web interface is the mitigation only where the upgrade is not possible, so the earlier statement that no patched NRSW release exists no longer holds (Belden, 2026-10-22). Schneider Electric's bulletin, at version 3.2.0 of 2026-10-30, added EcoStruxure Foxboro DCS H90 Server on 2026-10-28 with a mitigation only: check that firewalls block TCP ports 2301 and 2381, used by the HPE System Management Homepage (Schneider Electric, 2026-10-30). Wibu-Systems released CodeMeter License Central 5.2.3, which applies its post-update configuration recommendations automatically, and a new patch installer for 5.1.x and 5.0.x (Wibu-Systems, 2026-10-29).

entries.headline: Adobe Campaign Classic build 9402 is now affected: APSB26-162 adds a pre-auth CVSS 9.8 SQL injection; update to 9403
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-82004 +20updatedNATOA2

Adobe Campaign Classic: eight unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in APSB26-142 and three more in APSB26-134, with build 9403 as the fix after APSB26-162

Adobe's Priority 1 bulletin APSB26-142 covers Adobe Campaign Classic v7 7.4.4 build 9401 and earlier on Windows and Linux and names build 9402 as the fix; it was published on 2026-09-08 with one CVE and revised on 2026-09-22 to add seventeen more, for eighteen, all rated Critical (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-09-22). Ten of the eighteen need no privileges: eight are CVSS 10.0 with the vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H (CVE-2026-82004, an OS command injection; six code-injection flaws, CVE-2026-73369, -84412, -89275, -75699, -75703 and -75721; and CVE-2026-75723, an incorrect-authorization flaw), plus CVE-2026-83660 (SSRF, 9.9) and CVE-2026-75728 (incorrect authorization, 9.1) (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-09-22). The remaining eight require low or high privileges. The earlier bulletin APSB26-134 (Priority 1, 2026-08-25) fixed three more unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in build 9401, CVE-2026-76197 and CVE-2026-76195 (OS command injection) and CVE-2026-76193 (SSRF) (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-08-25).

Adobe states it is not aware of exploitation of any issue in APSB26-142, and none of these CVEs is in CISA's KEV catalog as of the 2026-10-01 version (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-09-22; CISA KEV, 2026-10-01). The bulletin applies to fully on-premise deployments and the on-premise components of hybrid deployments; Adobe-hosted instances are already remediated, and because the hosted fixes did not increment the customer-visible build number, some hosted instances still report build 9401 (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-09-22). Adobe's table names build 9402 for all eighteen; estates that stopped at build 9401 or earlier carry the ten unauthenticated flaws, and build 9402 itself is affected by APSB26-162, fixed in build 9403 (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
On-premise Campaign Classic v7 servers, and the on-premise tier of hybrid deployments, running build 9402 or earlier; the flaw classes (OS command injection, code injection, incorrect authorization, SQL injection and SSRF) are network-reachable, so reachability of the Campaign endpoints from outside decides how urgent the update is.
Detection
Adobe publishes no detection guidance or compromise check for these flaws; the flaw classes point to web access logs for requests to Campaign endpoints from unexpected sources, process-creation events in which the Campaign server or its web-server parent starts a shell or interpreter, and outbound requests from the Campaign host to internal services.
Defender takeaway
Update the on-premise tier to build 9403 and check the build on the server itself, since a hosted instance's displayed build is not a reliable signal; an internet-reachable on-premise instance that sat on build 9401 or earlier carried ten unauthenticated paths and warrants a compromise assessment, because Adobe provides none.
Update01 Nov 2026 13:51 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditactionsbodycvesheadlinesourcessummarytitle

Adobe's Priority 2 bulletin APSB26-162 of 2026-10-27 covers Campaign Classic v7 7.4.4 build 9402 and earlier on Windows and Linux and names build 9403 as the fix, so build 9402, the earlier fix, is affected (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-10-27). Its eight flaws are all rated Critical. One needs neither privileges nor user interaction: CVE-2026-105781, a SQL injection at CVSS 3.1 9.8. Four need low privileges at 9.9 (code injection CVE-2026-104351, OS command injection CVE-2026-104353, incorrect authorization CVE-2026-105780 and SQL injection CVE-2026-105489), CVE-2026-104350 is a reflected cross-site scripting flaw at 9.3 that needs user interaction, and CVE-2026-104354 and CVE-2026-105779 are SQL injections at 9.1 (Adobe PSIRT, 2026-10-27). entries.headline: WS_FTP Server: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 admin-credential leak, five more critical flaws; fix 2025.0.4, 2024.0.7
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-84295 +6updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-84295, Progress WS_FTP Server: an unauthenticated remote authentication flaw can expose administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0), with two more unauthenticated flaws, fixed in 2025.0.4 and 2024.0.7; no exploitation found

Progress, as CNA, published CVE-2026-84295 on 2026-10-29: improper authentication in WS_FTP Server on Windows that "could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to access sensitive information, including administrative credentials"; its CVSS 3.1 vector is network, low complexity, no privileges and no user interaction, scored 10.0, and the record names no component or endpoint (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29). Two further flaws carry an unauthenticated vector with high attack complexity: CVE-2026-90865, an OS command injection that could allow command execution with elevated privileges under certain configurations (9.0) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), and CVE-2026-90867, improper access control in the Web Admin console that could expose administrative functionality to remote authentication attempts (8.1) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29). CSIRT Italia counts 6 critical and 3 high flaws in the release, of types including authentication bypass, remote code execution and arbitrary file read and write (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30).

The record for CVE-2026-84295 names versions before 2024.0.6 and 2025.0.3 as affected (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), and the records for the other two name versions before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), so 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4 is the build to reach. CSIRT Italia lists 2025.0.3 (10.0.3) and 2024.0.6 (9.0.6) and earlier as affected and says that for unsupported versions the vendor will not release a workaround or patch (translated from Italian) (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30). No source reports exploitation: CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, although CVE-2023-40044 in the same product has been listed since 2023-10-05 with known ransomware use (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-10-30).

Progress's bulletin, as listed by heise, carries fifteen CVEs, six of them critical (heise online, 2026-11-02). Besides the three above: CVE-2026-90868, an OS command injection that could allow arbitrary command execution under certain configurations (9.9) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); CVE-2026-90866, a path traversal by a delegated Host Administrator, potentially enabling remote code execution (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); CVE-2026-90864, a path traversal that lets a delegated Host Administrator reach data beyond their permitted scope (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); and CVE-2026-90863, missing authorization in the administrative interface (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29). NCSC Switzerland describes the exposed administrator credentials as the start of a chain: command injection under certain configurations (CVE-2026-90868, CVE-2026-90865) or a scope escape (CVE-2026-90863, CVE-2026-90866) leads to a complete compromise of the server, and it lists exploitation as unknown (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-02). Builds 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 have been available since 2026-10-01 (heise online, 2026-11-02).

Exposure
Any WS_FTP Server on Windows below 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4; CSIRT Italia describes it as a secure file-transfer server used within organisations and with external partners, so instances reachable from partner or public networks come first (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30). The records name no component for the authentication flaw, so no configuration is known to make an instance safe.
Detection
No source publishes an indicator. For an instance that was reachable before the fix, the records to review are the web-server logs of the Web Admin console and the file-transfer server's own logons for administrator access from unfamiliar addresses, and process creation by the service or its web worker, since CVE-2026-90865 is command execution (an inference from the described flaw).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4, partner-facing instances first, and rotate the administrator credentials afterwards, because the upgrade does not change credentials an attacker already read; take an instance on an unsupported branch off the network or migrate it.
Improvement03 Nov 2026 03:32 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarycvestechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Six of the bulletin's fifteen flaws are critical: besides CVE-2026-84295 and CVE-2026-90865, CVE-2026-90868 (9.9), CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 (9.1 each), and NCSC Switzerland ties the credential exposure in CVE-2026-84295 to command injection and scope-escape flaws that lead to a complete compromise of the server (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-02; heise online, 2026-11-02). All four added flaws need privileges: CVE-2026-90866 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29), CVE-2026-90864 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29) and CVE-2026-90863 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29) need a delegated Host Administrator, and CVE-2026-90868 (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29) is scored for an attacker with low privileges.

entries.headline: Microsoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick Assist ended in AD CS certificates for privileged accounts and a DC
entries.html:
NOTABLENATOB2

Teams help-desk impersonation to domain-controller identity: Microsoft traces two intrusions from a Quick Assist session to AD CS ESC1 certificates with DCSync, and to PetitPotam relayed to ESC8 Web Enrollment

Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any threat actor, that began with an external Teams contact (across the broader activity Microsoft saw organisation-themed tenant names and support-style display names) who persuaded a user to open Quick Assist and read out the connection code; the activity did not exploit a Teams vulnerability. In the session the operator placed an archive in Downloads, extracted it into a newly created KB-prefixed folder under the user profile and started the payload with a portable Python, JavaScript or Java runtime, which ran host and network discovery and assessed AD CS (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

In the first case a certificate template open to ESC1, where the requester supplies the identity, produced certificates for three privileged accounts, and about 90 minutes later for eight more after a second wave against 16 users; DCSync began within seconds of obtaining one privileged certificate. Defender's automated disruption blocked more than 1,000 SMB attempts, but a privileged account excluded from automated response stayed usable, reached a file server and ran a renamed Rclone that copied a share to an external SFTP destination (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). In the second case the operator used PetitPotam to make a domain controller authenticate to the attacker's host, relayed that NTLM authentication to an AD CS Web Enrollment endpoint, obtained a certificate from the Domain Controller template and used it for PKINIT to get a ticket-granting ticket for the controller's account; Defender raised ESC8 alerts and the customer isolated the workstation (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

Exposure
A forest with an enterprise CA whose authentication-capable templates accept requester-supplied identity with broad enrollment rights (ESC1), or whose Web Enrollment or Certificate Enrollment Web Service endpoints lack HTTPS and Extended Protection (ESC8), where Teams accepts external chats and calls and users can start Quick Assist; Defender for Identity's AD CS posture assessments, or an inventory of /certsrv endpoints and template permissions, shows the first two (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).
Detection
New external Teams contacts from help-desk-themed tenants; in process telemetry, a portable runtime started from a freshly created KB-prefixed folder under the user profile after a remote-support session; in CA records, certificate requests and issuances correlated by requester, subject alternative name and template with the first authentication using the certificate; and a domain controller account authenticating to Web Enrollment from a device that is not that controller, which Microsoft calls a strong pivot (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). After containment, revoke the unauthorized certificates and assess issued Kerberos tickets separately; a password reset and a reimage of the first workstation leave both in place.

Triage: a help-desk Quick Assist session is routine; what separates this one is an external-tenant initiator with no matching ticket and an interpreter runtime launched from a newly created user-writable folder rather than a managed install path.

Defender takeaway
Require HTTPS and Extended Protection on every enrollment web endpoint, drop the ones nobody needs, review authentication-capable templates and require approval where enrollment is broad, and enable the Certification Services audit subcategory and CA audit filter; limit Teams external access and restrict remote-support tools to approved ones. Treat a containment exclusion as an incident decision with a manual compensating step, because in the first case the one excluded privileged account was the route to the file server (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

entries.headline: PHP2Shell hits Broadcom endpoint-security servers: App Control 8.12.2 or 8.13.2; SEPM fix builds unconfirmed
entries.html:
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Broadcom Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager, Carbon Black App Control Server, CloudSOC SpanVA and Content Analysis and Malware Analysis: PHP2Shell reaches the endpoint-security management servers; App Control Server 8.12.2 and 8.13.2 are the fixes Broadcom names

Broadcom's Enterprise Security Group advisory 39404, published on 2026-10-21 and last revised on 2026-10-30, lists four products as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619: Carbon Black App Control Server (moved to affected on 2026-10-22), Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager (SEPM, 2026-10-22), the CloudSOC SpanVA Appliance (2026-10-23) and Content Analysis and Malware Analysis (CASMA), which moved from under investigation to affected on 2026-10-30; the page states no versions, fixes or workarounds, and lists Content Analysis (CAS), the Symantec Endpoint Protection agent, Symantec Endpoint Security, Data Loss Prevention, Cloud Secure Web Gateway and Zero Trust Network Access among the products that are not vulnerable (Broadcom, 2026-10-30). CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-10-26); Broadcom's advisory says nothing about attacks on these products.

Broadcom's article 459982 says the App Control Server is affected in all supported versions and that builds 8.12.2 and 8.13.2 are available and contain only PHP-related changes: an installation on 8.12 or earlier may take either, one already on 8.13 must take 8.13.2 (Broadcom, 2026-10-22). For SEPM, NCSC-NL's tracker lists builds 14.3.27716.10000 and 14.4.494.0000 as the fixes, on the strength of a community report that cites Broadcom's SEPM advisory, which needs a login and which the maintainer did not verify (NCSC-NL, 2026-10-30). No fix is stated for the CloudSOC SpanVA Appliance or CASMA.

Exposure
A Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager, Carbon Black App Control Server, CloudSOC SpanVA appliance or CASMA whose management console or web service a hostile network can reach; Broadcom gives no version ranges, so every instance not on a fixed build counts. The flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, are in the PHP runtime.
Detection
Broadcom publishes no indicator. For a server that was reachable before its fix, review shells and downloads started by the console's web service and outbound connections the server initiates; this is an inference, since the pages do not describe how these products run PHP.
Defender takeaway
Put these consoles on administrator networks now and on fixed builds as soon as they exist: App Control Server has its fix, SEPM's rests on an unverified reading, and Broadcom's advisory 39404 listed no fix for CloudSOC SpanVA or CASMA as of 2026-10-30. Re-read Broadcom's advisory 39404 before relying on a status, because CASMA changed on 2026-10-30.
Correction01 Nov 2026 14:05 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbodysourcing_note

The takeaway said CloudSOC SpanVA and CASMA have no fix. Broadcom's umbrella advisory 39404, last revised on 2026-10-30, lists both as affected and states no fix or workaround, while their own product advisories, 39429 and 39475, need a Broadcom login, so the absence of a fix is what the umbrella page shows, not a confirmed state (Broadcom, 2026-10-30).
